In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

We have previously spoken at length about the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'a) at the beginnings of the surahs of the Qur'an. Whenever this phenomenon recurs, we speak about the realms of minds in understanding it. Since the Real (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, repeats it, we too must repeat our discussion of it. Why does Allah scatter this phenomenon throughout the surahs of the Qur'an? So that it remains always in mind.

We have said: the noble Qur'an is built in all its verses and surahs on continuity (al-wasl), not on pausing (al-waqf). Read: ﴿Dark green.(64) So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?(65) In them are two gushing springs.(66) So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?(67)﴾ [Ar-Rahman]

He did not say ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?(67)﴾ [Ar-Rahman] and stop; rather he joined it: ﴿In them are two gushing springs(66)﴾ [Ar-Rahman], because the Qur'an is continuous, with no separation whatsoever between its verses. Therefore there is no obligatory pause (waqf wajib) in the Qur'an; rather you may pause for shortness of breath, but when you repeat, you repeat with continuity.

Likewise the Qur'an is built on continuity between the surahs. When a surah ends, it does not end on a sukun. He, glory be to Him and exalted, did not say ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾ with a sukun on the nun, but (tur'ajun bismillahi al-rahmani al-rahim), so that another surah begins connected.

This, then, is a general characteristic of the verses and surahs of the Qur'an, except for the disjointed letters at the beginnings of the surahs. These are built on pausing: Alif Lam Mim, thus with sukun, and he did not say "Alifun Lamun Mimun" with continuity. Why? Because they are disjointed letters, and some may think them a single word, so they were separated by a pause.

Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I do not say Alif Lam Mim is a letter, but Alif is a letter, Lam is a letter, and Mim is a letter." (He said this) to affirm this meaning, and he made them with a pause, each letter on its own.

We have spoken about these letters and said: they are the raw materials (khamat) of the Qur'an, and from such letters the speech of Allah is woven. We said: if you wish to discern the skill of weaving among some craftsmen, for example, do not give one of them cotton, another wool, and another silk, because you can distinguish between them, since the materials differ, and silk by its nature is smoother and finer. But if you wish to know the skill, unify the raw material for everyone.

It is as if the Real, blessed and exalted, is saying to us: the Qur'an is inimitable, as evidence that you possess the very same letters, yet you were unable to oppose it. The Qur'an has used your very letters, your very words and expressions, and has brought them in an eloquent form that you found difficult to match.

Thus the style of the Qur'an differs, because Allah, exalted, is the One who speaks. The meaning of (Alif Lam Mim) is: these are your very letters, so bring something like them.

Or: (Alif Lam Mim) carries a meaning of its own, because Alif Lam Mim are names of letters, and the names of letters are known only to the learner. The unlettered person says "kataba," but does not know the names of its letters. And you say to a small child at school: spell "kataba," and he says to you "kaf, fatha, ka," "ta, fatha, ta," "ba, fatha, ba."

So the names of the letters are known only to the learner, and our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), was unlettered. Whence then did he pronounce the names of the letters: Alif Lam Mim, Ta Ha, Ya Sin, Qaf, etc.? Therefore his Lord must have taught him and instructed him in these letters. From here came the importance of instruction and receiving (al-talqin wa'l-talaqqi) in learning the Qur'an. Otherwise, how would the learner distinguish between (Alif Lam Mim) here and ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?(1)﴾ [Ash-Sharh], pronouncing the first as letter names with a pause, and the second connected, pronouncing the first by its letter names and the second by its referents?

Also (Alif Lam Mim) carries the meaning of alerting the listener (al-tanbih lil-sami'). The Qur'an was revealed in the style and language of the Arabs, so it must possess the characteristics of Arabic and of refined Arabic. If we read, for example, in pre-Islamic poetry, we find 'Amr ibn Kulthum saying:

"Ala, ihbi bi-sahnika fa-asbihina
wa la tubqi khumur al-Andarina"

We ask: what does "Ala" add here, when the meaning is sound without it? ("Ala") has a meaning for the Arab, because it alerts him if he is heedless, so that nothing of his interlocutor's speech escapes him when he is taken by surprise, just as you now call out to someone you do not know, saying "Listen, O...," as if you are saying to him: pay attention, for I am about to speak to you.

Alerting comes in language from the fact that the speaker speaks at will at any time, whereas the listener may be heedless and not attentive, or not prepared to listen, so he needs someone to alert him so that he understands what is said to him. But if you surprise him with the intended matter, perhaps something of it will escape him before he becomes attentive to you.

Likewise in (Alif Lam Mim) there are letters for alerting: that a precious speech is coming, listen to it well, beware lest a single letter of it be lost to you. It is also permissible that these letters have other meanings, understood by others whom Allah has granted understanding. They are thus an inexhaustible spring, from which each draws according to his capacity.

1 Najjat al-bi'r: its water rose and gushed and welled up. That is: its water flows abundantly. Naddakhah is an intensive form indicating abundance. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/270]
2 From Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites a letter from the Book of Allah, he has for it a good deed, and a good deed is multiplied tenfold. I do not say Alif Lam Mim is a letter, but Alif is a letter, Lam is a letter, and Mim is a letter." Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2910), who said: "A hasan sahih hadith."
3 He is 'Amr ibn Kulthum ibn Malik, of the Banu al-Aswad, a pre-Islamic poet of the first rank, born in the lands of Rabi'a in northern Arabia. He led his people Taghlib while still a youth, lived long, and died in the Upper Euphrates region around 40 BH. [al-A'lam by al-Zirikli 5/84]. The verse is from his Mu'allaqa.

Then the Truthful Lord says:

{Do people think that they will be left alone on saying "We believe," and that they will not be tested?¹ ²}

The verb ḥasiba (حسب), with a kasra in the past tense and a fatḥa in the present (yaḥsabu), means "to think, to suppose." With a kasra in both the past and present (ḥasiba, yaḥsibu), it means "to count."

So the meaning of ﴿Do people think...﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 2] is: did they suppose. The hamza is interrogative, and it conveys the negation and denial of this supposition, because they thought and supposed that God would leave them without trial, testing and examination.

The Truthful Lord wishes to have the message of Islam carried by people of resolve, because Islam does not take up the carrying of its call except those strong in faith, who are able to bear the hardships of the call and the trust of conveying it.

Faith is not a word that is said; it is a great responsibility. This responsibility is what prevented the disbelievers of Makkah from believing, because they knew that the statement "There is no god but God" is not merely a word; for otherwise they would have said it. Rather, it is a way of life with requirements.

It means: there is no one to be obeyed except God, and no one worshipped in truth except God; and they did not want this matter, so that their standing and worldly authority would remain for them.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, says here: ﴿Do people think that they will be left alone on saying, "We believe..."⁠﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 2]. Faith is not merely speech, because speech may be true and may be false, so after the saying there must be testing and the sifting of faith ﴿and that they will not be tested﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 2]. If one endures afflictions and trials, then he is sincere in faith.

He, glory be to Him, affirms this meaning in another verse: ﴿And among people is he who worships God on an edge; if good befalls him he is content with it, and if a trial befalls him he turns back on his face, losing both this world and the Hereafter...⁠﴾ [al-Hajj: 11].

God tested the foremost early believers with signs and miracles that contradict the cosmic order, so the believer accepted them and believed in the truthfulness of the Messenger who brought them, whereas the wavering and bewildered one denied them and considered them unreasonable.

Among this is what happened with al-Siddiq Abu Bakr in the incident of the Night Journey and the Ascension. When they told him what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had said, he said: "If he said it, then he has spoken the truth,"² whereas some apostatised and denied. It is as if the Truthful Lord, blessed and exalted, wanted through these miracles, which the intellect stands before, to distinguish between people, so that the bearing of the matter of the call would be entrusted to those strong in faith and conviction, and to those who have certainty of the Messenger's truthfulness in conveying from his Lord.

We have already shown the foolishness of those among the disbelievers of Makkah who denied the incident of the Night Journey and the Ascension, who said to the Messenger of God: "Do you claim that you went to Bayt al-Maqdis in one night, when we travel to it by camels' hearts for a month?³" They overlooked, or feigned to overlook, the text of the verse: ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night...⁠﴾ [al-Isra': 1]. He did not say, "I travelled by myself," but "He took me by night."

To answer them we said: If a man came to you and said, "I climbed with my infant child to the peak of Everest, for example," would you say to him, "How does an infant climb the peak of Everest?"

We have also spoken before on a matter that should remain in your minds all together: every action takes its share of time according to the strength of its doer. The weight that a small child carries in several trips, you carry in one hand.

Thus time is inversely proportional to strength: whenever strength increases, time decreases. For example, one who goes to Alexandria on a donkey is not the same as one who goes by car or by airplane, and so on.

Therefore: measure according to the strength of the doer. If the Night Journey was by the power of God Most High, which is the power of powers, then there is no time, and this is a matter at which the intellect halts and accepts only by faith.

Therefore, the Truthful Lord tests and afflicts you, because He wants you for a great task, for which none is fit except the champion (ṣandīd)⁴ strong in his faith and certainty.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, says in more than one place: ﴿And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger, and loss of wealth and lives and fruits. But give good tidings to the patient⁠﴾ [al-Baqarah: 155].

And He said: ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those among you who strive and are patient, and We will test your reports⁠﴾ [Muhammad: 31].

And He said: ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet known those of you who fought...⁠﴾ [Al 'Imran: 142].

These afflictions are like the examination we give to students in order to know the capacity of each of them and the task for which he is fit. It is known that afflictions are not condemned for themselves, but for their consequences; afflictions were only made to know outcomes and to distinguish the one most suited to the task to which he is appointed.

The meaning of ﴿they will be tested⁠﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 2] is: they will be examined. It is derived from the testing of gold, when we melt it in fire, in order to bring out the impurity in it and purify its best metal for what suits its task.

Among this is what God set forth to us as a parable of truth and falsehood in His saying: ﴿He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their measure, and the torrent carries a swelling foam. And from what they heat in the fire seeking an ornament or goods there is a foam like it. Thus God strikes the parables of truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum; but that which benefits people remains in the earth. Thus God sets forth parables⁠﴾ [al-Ra'd: 17].

The trial was only so that we might know the truthful in the words of faith from the liar in them: the truthful will be patient and endure, and the liar will deny and waver.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 29, verse 3:

Then the Truthful, Glorified is He, says:

{And We had certainly tried those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars.}

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, consoles the earlier members of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) who were tortured and harmed, who were beaten with whips under the heat of the sun, who had heavy stones placed on their stomachs, and who went hungry until they ate carrion and the leaves of trees. He tells them: you are not unique in these trials, so endure them as the earlier believers endured.

﴿And We had certainly tried those before them...﴾ [al-Ankabut: 3]. Consider, for example, the trial of the Children of Israel with Pharaoh. Your trial, then, is lighter and easier, and in it there is mercy from Allah toward you, since you are less than they were in strength. ﴿And Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars﴾ [al-Ankabut: 3].

You may say: did Allah not know their reality before He tested them? Yes, He, glorified is He, knows the reality of His servants. The purpose of testing them is not to gain knowledge of their reality; rather, the purpose is that the servant acknowledge what He has known about him.

An example of this, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness, is when we say to a teacher, for instance: give us the results of these students. There is no time for an examination, so he says, based on his experience with them: this one passes, this one fails, this one is first, and this one is such-and-such. Then the one who failed stands and says: If you had tested me, I would have passed; and if his own laboratory had tested him, he would indeed have failed. So: our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, tests His servants so that each of them acknowledges what He has known about him.

﴿And Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars﴾ [al-Ankabut: 3]. This is knowledge of manifestation and acknowledgment from the person concerned himself, such that he cannot deny it, since he himself will bear witness against himself when his limbs bear witness against him.

Here too: ﴿Do those who commit evil deeds think that they can outrun Us?﴾ That is, they think they can escape Our punishment. You say "fulan sabaqa fulanan" meaning he escaped from him while the other was pursuing him. So the meaning is that they will not be able to escape the torment or flee from it, even if they believe or suppose that they will. Evil is the assumption they make.

﴿Evil is what they judge.﴾ That is, their judgment is ugly and null. When We judge their assumption and their judgment to be void, We are only affirming Our proposition, namely that they will not escape Our punishment.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, then the term of Allah is surely coming. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ (29:5)

The meaning of ﴿hopes for the meeting with Allah﴾ (29:5) is: he believes in Him, awaits Him, and acts for His sake. He believes that Allah, who created him and prepared for him this universe so that he might live his good life, will after that cause him to return and will call him to account. Therefore, if he does not worship Him and obey Him in gratitude for what He has bestowed, then let him worship Him out of fear that He may visit him with evil in the Hereafter.

The people of gnosis (ma'rifah) see a difference between one who hopes for reward and hopes for the mercy of Allah, and one who hopes for the meeting with Allah for the sake of the meeting itself, neither out of fear of a Fire nor out of desire for a Garden. Therefore Rabi'ah al-'Adawiyyah(1) says:

They all worship out of fear of a Fire,
and they see salvation as a generous portion,
or that they may dwell in the Gardens and obtain
palaces and drink of Salsabil.
I have no share in the Gardens or the Fire;
I do not seek any substitute for my love.

That is: I love You, O Lord, because You are to be loved for Your own essence, not out of fear of Your Fire, nor out of desire for Your Garden. She also said: "O Allah, if You know that I love You out of desire for Your Garden, then deprive me of it, and if You know that I worship You out of fear of Your Fire, then burn me in it."

Allah, the Exalted, says in Surat al-Kahf: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾ (18:110). Had the Garden been the object, the meeting with Allah would not be the greater thing, and it is the One who is hoped for in His own essence.

The Truth, glorified is He, emphasizes this matter with more than one emphasis: ﴿then the term of Allah is surely coming﴾ (29:5). He reinforced it with inna (surely), with the lam, and with the form of the active participle, which indicates the certainty of the event, as He says: ﴿Everything perishes except His Face﴾ (28:88), and He did not say "will perish." And His words, addressing His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed they will die﴾ (39:30).

He addresses them with this form while they are still alive, because "mayyit" (one who is destined to die) is the one whose matter will end in death however long his life, whereas one who has actually died is called "mayyit" (dead).

When you judge a future thing you say "it comes" or "it will come," and when you threaten someone you say "I will do such-and-such to you." You have then gambled and spoken of something whose elements you do not possess. You cannot guarantee, for example, that you will live until tomorrow; and if you live, you cannot guarantee that he will live; and if he lives, your mind may change toward him, or you may lose the ability to carry out what you said, such as by falling ill or by some event befalling you.

But when One who holds the reins of all affairs speaks, and Allah knows that no one will escape Him, then when He judges, time has no bearing on His action. Therefore He did not say "the term of Allah will come," but rather ﴿surely coming﴾ (29:5), with certainty.

We have previously mentioned in this regard His saying about the Resurrection: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it﴾ (16:1). The superficial ones stood before this verse saying: "Does a person seek to hasten anything except what has not yet come?" They do not understand the intent of Allah, and they lack the mastery of the Arabic language. Allah, the Exalted, judges the future as if it were past, that is, certain, because nothing prevents Him from His will, and no obstacle stands between Him and it.

The word ajal (term) occurs in the Qur'an in many places, among them: ﴿For every nation there is a term; when their term comes, they cannot delay it by an hour nor advance it﴾ (7:34). And in the verse we have: ﴿then the term of Allah is surely coming﴾ (29:5).

The two terms differ with respect to the human's life-presence: the first term ends the life of this world, and the other term restores life in the Hereafter for the meeting with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So the two terms are linked.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, when He presents us with an unseen matter, makes us familiar with it through something sensory and known to us, so that the intellect may pass from the sensory to the unseen that is not witnessed. You see that the lifespans of the children of Adam in this life vary: one whose mother's womb miscarries him, so he never comes out into life; another who breathes a single breath and dies, and so on.

At every moment of time we witness death: one dies after a single breath, and another dies after a hundred years. Therefore there is no regularity in the expiry of the term, neither in age nor in cause: this one dies of illness, that one by drowning, and that one dies in his bed.

Thus the poet says:
"Do not reckon sickness a cup of death,
even if it be a grievous illness with a severe effect;
for many an invalid you see recover,
and many a healthy man you see at the point of death."
Another said:
"The one full of health has passed away,
while the sick one has recovered and did not pass away."

You find the common cause in the epidemics that afflict people: one dies and another lives. There is no regularity in death, and when the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿For every nation there is a term; when their term comes, they cannot delay it by an hour nor advance it﴾ (7:34), we find the reality of life confirming this: there is no uniformity in lifespan, nor uniformity in cause.

The truth of the first term, which we witness, calls us to affirm the other term, that the term of Allah is surely coming. The term that ended life with variation is the one that brings life back with uniformity. By a single blast we shall all rise, alive, for reckoning. If we differ in the first, we shall agree in the Hereafter, because the souls with Allah, from Adam (peace be upon him) until the Hour is established, will all rise at a single blast.

We have said before: time is of three kinds: a present that we witness, a past absent from us whose circumstances we do not know, and a future whose circumstances we do not know. The Truth, glorified is He, gives us in the observed existence a proof of the truth of the unobserved. For example, we do not know how the first creation was made except through what Allah has told us: that the origin of man is dust mixed with water until it became clay, then black mud moulded, then clay like pottery, and so on.

Then He made the offspring of man from a drop that becomes a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh, then the bones are clothed with flesh. Although modern science has shown us the drop, the clot and the lump, and how the embryo forms, the first creation from dust remains unseen, known to no one.

Do not believe one who says, "I know it," for Allah has warned us against these misleaders in His saying: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor their own creation, and I would not take the misleaders as helpers﴾ (18:51) — no, rather (28:51).

They have no knowledge of the creation of man, nor knowledge of the creation of the phenomena of the universe. So do not listen to them; take your information from the Book of your Lord, who created, glorified is He. The existence of misleaders who say that the earth is a piece of the sun that separated from it, or that man's origin is an ape, establishes, by their theories, the truth of what the Truth, glorified is He, has informed us.

Otherwise, how can we believe a theory that an ape ascended to become a man? And why did the ape of (Darwin) ascend while the rest of the apes did not?

If the believer affirms His saying: ﴿So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down in prostration to him﴾ (15:29), because he believes in Allah and believes in what the Messenger of Allah brought, how then can one who does not believe or affirm? Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, makes these minds that seek to know the realities of things familiar with what they witness: if you do not affirm the matter of creation, you undoubtedly witness the matter of death and see it every day, and death is the undoing of life, and the undoing of a thing is the reverse of its building.

The Creator, Mighty and Majestic, informed us that the soul is the last thing in the building of man; therefore it is the first thing undone at death. So your witnessing of how you die confirms for you the truth of Allah concerning how you came into being.

The term of the Hereafter is a necessity, so that the obedient may be rewarded and the disobedient punished. Do you not see that social systems, even among non-believers, adopt this principle for the soundness of the movement of life? How then with the method of Allah in His creation: would He leave the wrongdoer and the criminal to escape punishment in the Hereafter after escaping punishment in this world?

We used to answer the Communists with this argument: "You have punished those criminals whom your hands reached, so how about those who died and you did not punish them? Does the Hereafter not resolve this dilemma for you?"

Then the verse concludes with His saying: ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ (29:5). Do you not see that if He had said only "the All-Knowing," it would have included the heard as well, since knowledge encompasses all perceived things? Why then did He say ﴿the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾?

They said: because the Arabic language, when speaking of deed, action and speech, divided the limbs into parts: the tongue has speech, and the rest of the limbs have action, and both together are deeds. Thus speech is the deed of the tongue, and action is the deed of the rest of the limbs; so the tongue took one half of the deed, and the rest of the limbs took the other half.

Through the tongue is known your faith, when you say: "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," and it is the noblest thing a human does, and through it the Messenger conveyed from Allah to His creation. Thus the legal actions of the limbs arise from the tongue and from hearing; therefore He made speech, which is the deed of the tongue, half of the whole deed.

Because of the importance of speech, the Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ (61:2). Every action arises from submission to a saying or from hearing a saying; therefore He concluded this verse with His saying:

﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ (29:5)

(1) She is Rabi'ah bint Isma'il al-'Adawiyyah, Umm al-Khayr, a client of the family of 'Atik, of Basra, a well-known righteous woman from the people of Basra, born there. She is noted for accounts of worship and asceticism; she died in Jerusalem in the year 135 AH [al-A'lam of al-Zirikli 3/10].

The word ﴿jāhada﴾ [al-'Ankabut] corresponds to success in trial. Jihad means exerting effort to carry out one's aim, and from it comes ijtahada fulan fi kadha, meaning he exerted the utmost of his ability in seriousness and striving so as to deduce the ruling (istinbat).

Jihad has two arenas: one within the self, which one struggles against so that, through striving against one's own self, one becomes strong enough to strive against one's enemy.

Jahada is a form of mufa'ala, as if the thing you want is difficult and requires effort and attempt from you. Mufa'ala occurs from both sides: from you and from the thing that opposes you. The first arena of jihad is the human soul, because your Lord created in you instincts and emotions for a task you must perform. Then the divine methodology comes to restrain these instincts and refine them, so that you do not rush with them toward what is not permitted.

Curiosity, for example, is a praiseworthy instinct in scientific research and beneficial discoveries; but if it turns into spying and tracking the faults of people, it is forbidden. Eating and drinking are instincts so that you may sustain yourself and the capacity to work is generated in you; but if they turn into gluttony and excess, you have taken the instinct out of its purpose and its aim.

Strange is the way people handle food. A car, for example, we do not give a mixture of fuels; it is one type only. But a human being is not satisfied with many kinds, each of which has a reaction in the body; when these reactions accumulate, they harm more than they benefit.

Therefore: these instincts require from you struggle, so that they remain within the bounds of moderation, in accordance with the saying: "We are a people who do not eat until we are hungry, and when we eat we do not become full; and we do not drink until we are thirsty, and when we drink we are not satisfied."

If we acted by this hadith, we would have defeated the atomic bomb of economy in our countries. How sweet a morsel is after hunger, however simple and inexpensive it may be; therefore they say: "Hunger is the best condiment." Then, when you eat, do not fill the stomach; leave room, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A third for his food, a third for his drink, and a third for his breath."(1)

With this wise dietary method we secure bodies that are sound and free from illness.

The instincts, then, Allah created in you for a task, so you must keep them to their task. Like the instincts are the emotions: love, hatred, compassion, sorrow, and so on. These have no law except that you stop them at the limits of emotion and do not let them exceed into action. Love whom you wish and hate whom you wish, but do not transgress, and do not base a ruling upon the emotion.

We have given an example of this matter with our master 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him). He had a brother named Zayd who was killed, and then his killer embraced Islam. Whenever 'Umar saw him he would say: "Turn your face away from me," meaning: "I do not love you." The man would say: "Does your not loving me prevent me from one of my rights?" He said: "No." He said: "Only women weep over love." Meaning: love and hatred are matters that women concern themselves with, while what matters is action and what follows from these emotions.

Among struggle is the struggle against a tyrant or the like who is set over you: you strive against him and endure his harm. Your love for the truth makes you patient with it. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We will surely test you until We make evident those of you who strive and are patient, and We will test your reports.﴾ [Muhammad 31]

All of these are trials requiring struggle. If you have an adversary, then if you can repel his harm by what is better, do so; and if you wish to retaliate, retaliate with its equivalent. This is a difficult matter, because you cannot determine or control the equivalence so that you do not exceed it. For example, if your opponent strikes you one blow, can you return it with its like without addition?

Therefore, do not put yourself into this maze; it is better for you to take the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And those who restrain anger and pardon people﴾ [Al 'Imran 134], and the matter ends.

If the calamity has no adversary behind it, such as sickness, death, and other matters of decree that Allah makes to pass over you, then say: "My Lord intends good for me." By it sins and misdeeds are expiated, by it I attain the reward of the patient; and perhaps I had become heedless of my Lord or blessings had deceived me, so Allah tested me to turn me to Himself and remind me of Him.

Among struggle is the struggle of the self in receiving the methodology of "do" and "do not." Obligation is usually hard on the self and requires struggle. Beware of transferring the meaning of "do" into "do not," or the meaning of "do not" into "do."

When you survey "do" and "do not" in the methodology of Allah, you find that it takes about seven percent of your movements in life, and the rest are permissible; you have the freedom to do them or leave them.

An upright person may be exposed to mockery and ridicule even from those of his own religion, because the deviant always feels a deficiency, shrinks and diminishes before himself, and tries to drag others down to his own level so that all become equal. Otherwise, how could you be guided and upright while he is disobedient and astray? Therefore you see him mocking you and belittling your standing. Why? To make you averse to obedience, so that you become like him.

If you wish, read the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they exchanged winks. And when they returned to their people, they returned jesting. And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are misguided." But they had not been sent as observers over them. So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, upon couches, observing. Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 29–36]

There is no doubt that such a matter requires from you patience with its harm and struggle of the self so that you do not fall into the trap set for you.

Whisperings may come to you from Satan, adorning evil for you and making sin beloved to you; at that moment, remember the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from Paradise, stripping them of their clothing to show them their private parts...﴾ [al-A'raf 27]

Therefore, you must remember the first enmity between your father Adam and Satan, so that you may be wary of him. We have previously explained how to distinguish between the sin that comes from the self and the sin that comes from Satan's whispering: the self holds you to one specific sin and wants no other; but Satan, if you refuse him in one direction, moves you to another, for his concern is only that he bring you down in any state. So: your enemies are many, and they require from you strength of will and struggle. The coming of this verse that mentions jihad after the saying of Allah, ﴿Whoever is hoping for the meeting of Allah — indeed, the term of Allah is coming. And He is the Hearing, the Knowing﴾ [al-'Ankabut 5], asks the person who believes that the term of Allah, meeting in the Hereafter, is coming — and that is undoubted — to prepare himself for this meeting.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever strives only strives for himself. Indeed, Allah is Free of need from the worlds.﴾ [al-'Ankabut 6] Because man has arrived in a universe prepared to receive him, with its sky, earth, sun, moon, water, and air; everything in the universe serves you, and you add nothing to the dominion of Allah. All your effort and thought is for the comfort of your own life. When you do good, no one benefits from it but you, and your Lord is free of need from your giving.

So if you strive, you strive for yourself, like when a servant grants you a favor by serving you, and you say to him: "Rather, you served yourself and served your dependents when you served, in order to secure for yourself the means of living; and I am the one who toiled and sweated to provide you with the money you receive."

Likewise, the Almighty says to us: ﴿And whoever strives, he strives only for himself.﴾ [al-'Ankabut 6], that is, when he applies the methodology and walks by its guidance. The Almighty affirms this matter in many verses: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for himself; and whoever does evil, it is against himself. And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants.﴾ [Fussilat 46]

And the Almighty says: ﴿If you do good, you do good for yourselves; and if you do evil, it is for them.﴾ [al-Isra' 7]

And the Almighty says: ﴿It has what it earned, and it bears what it has earned.﴾ [al-Baqarah 286]

Therefore, the matter is from you and to you, and we have no role in it except our concern for the goodness and safety of creation, like the craftsman who wants his craft to be of the best quality and most complete form. Therefore I pour upon him some of My power, some of My knowledge, some of My expansiveness, some of My majesty, and I give him of My attributes.

Thus some of the knowers said: "Take on the character of Allah."

For the help lies in bestowing attributes, and the domain of attributes in action is not that I do for you, but that I help you so that you do it yourself. One of us, when he sees a weak person who cannot carry his goods, what does he do? He carries them for him, meaning he extends the effect of his strength to him; but the weak remains weak and the feeble remains feeble, whenever he wants something he needs someone to do it for him.

As for the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, He pours upon you from His strength and bestows upon you from His power and His self-sufficiency so that you act by yourself. Therefore whoever takes on the character of Allah says: "Do not give the poor a fish; teach him how to fish, so that he does not need you at all times. Pour upon him what keeps him benefiting from it continually."

Therefore: the Truth, glorified is He, grants the capable capability, grants the rich richness, the scholars knowledge and the wise wisdom. This is among the manifestations of His greatness, exalted is He: that the effect of an attribute is not transferred to His servants as the attribute itself, but a portion of the attribute is transferred to them, so that it becomes innate in them.

Rather, He, glorified is He, gives even more than that: He gives you the will by which you act, merely by your thinking about the action. By Allah, what do you do so that you stand up from your place? What do you do when you want to lift something or move one of your limbs? Did you command it? Did you say to it, "Do such-and-such"?

When you look at a bulldozer, for example, or a crane, how it moves, and how each movement in it has a button that activates it and complex mechanical operations, reflect on yourself: when you want to stand up, for example, merely by thinking of standing, you find yourself standing. Your will in your limbs is that they act and are acted upon for you.

So when your Lord says to you: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ [Ya-Sin 82], then believe Him, for you have witnessed it in yourself and in your limbs. So what of your Lord, the Mighty and Majestic — would He be unable to do what you do? What do you do if you want to sleep or to strike with your hand?

Nothing but the will within you; for your Lord has clothed you with some of His power, given you some of His word "Be," and a portion of His power. But He did not will to make it innate in you, so that you would not be deceived by it.

Therefore, if He, glorified is He, wills to take it from you — as in His saying: ﴿No! Indeed, man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient.﴾ [al-'Alaq 6–7] — then you come to move your arm, for example, and it does not obey you; it becomes paralyzed and refuses you after it had been under your will. That is so you know that it is a gift from Allah: if He wills, He takes it, for it is not innate in you.

Thus struggle encompasses many arenas: the struggle against instincts and emotions, the struggle against the hardship of the methodology of "do" and "do not," the struggle against the devils of mankind and jinn, and the struggle against the enemies of Islam who want to extinguish the light of Allah.

Al-Bukhari related that Khabbab ibn al-Aratt came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are in hardship. Will you not seek victory for us? Will you not supplicate for us?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among those before you, a man would be made to dig a pit, he would be placed in it, then a saw would be brought and he would be sawn in two, then his flesh would be combed from his bones with iron combs, yet that would not turn him from the religion of Allah."

Then the Messenger of Allah reassured him that this period, the period of trial, would not be long, and he said: "By Allah, Allah will surely complete this matter, until a rider travels from San'a to Hadramawt fearing none but Allah and the wolf concerning his sheep."(2)

The Prophet (ﷺ), the Seal of the Prophets, was visited by Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) suffering from the heat of fever. He placed his hand on the blanket with which the Messenger of Allah was covered, and felt its heat from beneath the blanket. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, how severe it is upon you!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Sa'id, indeed the trial is doubled for us, just as the reward is doubled for us."(3)

This is to establish that trial comes not only from enemies, but may also come from Allah, the Exalted. Why? Because Allah boasts to His angels of His obedient, humble, patient creatures, and they say: "How would they not love You and turn to Your obedience, when You have bestowed upon them such-and-such?" and they mention the grounds of this obedience. Then He, the Exalted, says: "Remove all of that from them, and they will love Me," meaning: they will love Me for My own sake.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 29, verse 7:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

{Those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely remove from them their misdeeds and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do.} (29:7)

He, glory be to Him and exalted, mentions to us the results: ﴿Those who believe...﴾ (29:7), that is, in Allah as Lord, who possesses all absolute perfect attributes, possesses absolute freedom of power, possesses absolute freedom of will, is the Guardian (al-Muhaymin), is the Judge... etc.

Then ﴿and do righteous deeds...﴾ (29:7), because righteous action is a result of faith and one of its fruits. And the ṣāliḥ (righteous, wholesome) is that thing which remains upon the way of its goodness without changing. So you have received a world that Allah created for you in the form of wholesomeness, so do not corrupt it. This is the least of faith: that you keep the wholesome upon its wholesomeness. If you wish to ascend, then increase it in wholesomeness.

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are only reformers."﴾ (2:11)

Allah has prepared the earth for us wholesome, with all its laws (nawāmīs) and regulations. Do you not see the regions where rain does not fall? Allah compensates them for it with groundwater within the depths of the earth. The excess rainwater Allah channels as springs in the earth and makes it stored for the time of need. And storing sweet water within the depths of the earth so that the sun does not evaporate it. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Say, "Have you considered: if your water should become sunken (ghawran), who would bring you flowing water?"﴾ (67:30)

And we have struck an example of leaving the wholesome upon its wholesomeness with the well from which the people of the desert drink. We may throw into it filth that spoils its water, and we may see someone pouring dirt into it so that it is obliterated. All of this is corrupting the wholesome. Perhaps someone comes who builds a wall around it to protect it, or places upon it a lifting apparatus that raises the water and relieves the people who come to it. If you are not among these, then at least leave it in its condition.

So the wholesome, then, is every action and thought that increases the wholesomeness of society in all the movements of life. Beware of saying that there is an action more noble than another action. Every action, however lowly you see it, so long as it provides a service to society and offers good to people, is a noble action. The value of actions is the value of the doer who performs them well and benefits people through them. That is: there is no action better than another action; rather, there is a better doer than another doer. Therefore they say: "The worth of every person is what he does well."

I have previously struck an example for this, and I still do, although it concerns non-Muslim people: the leader (naqīb) of the workers in France used to demand the rights of the workers, defend them, and secure benefits for them. When he assumed the ministry, they said to him: "Give us now the rights that you used to demand for us," and perhaps he had been demanding for his workers what the ministry's capacities and budgets could not bear. Now he had become a minister. On one occasion, one of the workers insulted him and said: "Do not forget that you were once a shoe-shiner." He said: "Yes, but I used to do it well."

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, mentions the reward of faith and righteous action: ﴿We will surely remove from them their misdeeds...﴾ (29:7). Here the divine greatness becomes manifest, as He began with the removal of misdeeds and placed it before the bestowal of good deeds.

Because clearing (takhliyah) precedes adorning (taḥliyah), and the principle says: averting harm takes precedence over securing benefit. Suppose one person wants to throw a stone at you, and another wants to throw you an apple. Which do you receive first? Undoubtedly, you will first ward off the harm of the stone from yourself.

The Creator, mighty and majestic, knows the nature of His servants and what occurs from them of heedlessness and turning away from the method that leads them into disobedience. Since the Law makes known to us the crimes and legislates the punishment for them, this is thus a declaration from Him that they will occur.

Therefore He says to His servants: Be reassured; I will purify you of these sins first, before I give you the good deeds. That is because man by nature is more inclined to evil than to good. So He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿We will surely remove from them their misdeeds...﴾ (29:7)

Indeed, and more than that, in another verse He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Except one who repents and believes and does righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their misdeeds with good deeds. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (25:70) So what generosity is there after Allah replaces the misdeed with a good deed! The matter does not stop at mere removal of it; it is as if it were a "sale" (ūkāzyūn) of forgiveness: you need only seize it.

In another place He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove misdeeds.﴾ (11:114) And in the noble hadith: "...and follow the bad deed with a good deed, which will erase it..." (2)

Then He, glory be to Him, mentions the good after that: ﴿and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do.﴾ (29:7) We have said: when the Truth, glory be to Him, wishes to give to the poor, He borrows on their behalf from their wealthy brothers: ﴿Who is it that would lend to Allah a goodly loan...﴾ (2:245)

Although He, glory be to Him, is the bestower of all blessings, He respects the ownership of His servants, and respects their efforts and their sweat. So He honors work and honors the fruit of work, just as a father treats his children: he takes from the wealthy to help the poor, on condition that he return their wealth at a time of ease. Just as you do not retract your gift, so your Lord, mighty and majestic, does not retract His gift.

I recall that when we were in America, an orientalist asked us, saying: there is a contradiction between the Qur'an's saying: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like...﴾ (6:160) and the saying of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "It is written on the gate of Paradise: charity is rewarded tenfold and a loan eighteenfold." (3)

So Allah willed to inspire me with two words to answer him, so that the disbelievers would have no path over the believers. I said to the translator: Yes, the good deed is rewarded tenfold when you give charity; but in a loan, for example, if you lend a dollar, it is ten dollars with Allah, yet your dollar returns to you again, so it is as if you have nine dollars. Thus when it is doubled, it becomes eighteen.

3 On the authority of Abū Umāmah, may Allah be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: "A man entered Paradise and saw written upon it: charity is rewarded tenfold, and a loan eighteenfold." Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 29, verse 8:

After that, Allah the Glorified and Exalted moves to the first circle in the formation of society, which is the circle of the family, consisting of: the father, the mother, and the children. Allah wanted to reform the first building block so that the whole society would be reformed, so He, blessed and exalted is He, said:(١)

﴿And We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents. But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.﴾

The parents serve the son until he grows up and becomes strong, while they themselves become weak and in need of someone to serve them. When we look at the situation of Westerners, for example, and how children leave their parents without care, and sometimes place them in homes for the elderly, in the case of dutifulness toward them, and in most cases leave them without even asking about them; therefore the greatness of Islam and the wisdom of God's method in the society of Muslims become evident to us.

For this reason one of the wise men said: "Early marriage is the best method – not for producing a child, but for producing a father for you who will support you in the childhood of your old age." Therefore Allah wanted to build the family on sound building blocks, which guarantee the safety of the believing society, so He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents..﴾ [al-'Ankabut], and in another place He, glorified is He, said in the same charge: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents..﴾ [al-Ahqaf, 15].

There is a difference between the two meanings: ﴿husnan..﴾ [al-'Ankabut, 8], meaning: I charge you to do the good itself for them, as you say: "So-and-so is just" and "So-and-so is justice," so He enjoined the good itself. As for ﴿ihsanan..﴾ [al-Ahqaf, 15], it is an injunction to show kindness to them both.

But why did He enjoin the good itself here, and kindness there? They said: He enjoined the good itself in the verse that mentions the contention of faith, where He said: ﴿But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me..﴾ [al-'Ankabut, 8]. Disbelief requires enmity and estrangement, and calls to quarrel, so He emphasized the necessity of extending good to them, not merely kindness, because the matter requires the strength of obligation.

As for when there is no disbelief from them, then kindness toward them suffices for dutifulness to them; therefore He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And accompany them in this world with kindness..﴾ [Luqman, 15].

And Allah, when He enjoins the parents, who are the direct cause of existence, does so only to make them a means of clarifying the origin of existence. Just as He charged you concerning the direct cause of your existence, which is your parents, so likewise and all the more, He charges you concerning the One who bestowed upon you the origin of this existence.

Thus Allah, by this charge, makes His servants feel at ease and draws their attention to what they owe to the Giver of the original existence, and what He deserves of worship and obedience; for He is the true Creator, whereas the parents are a causal existence.

This is a comfort through faith, which He explained in His saying: ﴿Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and be good to parents..﴾ [al-Nisa', 36], because they are the cause of partial existence, and Allah, the Exalted, is the cause of total existence.

This is also one of the places at which the orientalists have stopped, seeking a point of criticism, and imagining a contradiction between the verses of the Qur'an, in His saying: ﴿And accompany them in this world with kindness..﴾ [Luqman, 15], and in another place: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers..﴾ [al-Mujadila, 22].

This contradiction exists only in the minds of these people, because they do not understand the language of the Qur'an, and do not distinguish between love (wadd) and kindness (ma'ruf): wadd is the inclination of the heart, and from this inclination arises the doing of good toward the one to whom one is inclined; whereas ma'ruf is what you do with the one you love and the one you do not love, and it is the preservation of life.

Here Allah says: ﴿And if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.﴾ [al-'Ankabut, 8], meaning: remember this ruling; I will ask you about it on the Day of Resurrection. In another place: ﴿And accompany them in this world with kindness, and follow the way of those who turn back to Me. Then to Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.﴾ [Luqman, 15].

So the disbelief of the parents does not mean permission for you to insult or neglect them. Beware of that, for you will be asked about it before Allah: Did you do kindness toward them or not?

The grounds for the charge concerning parents: the father and the mother are mentioned in the other verse: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents. His mother bore him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, and his carrying and weaning were thirty months..﴾ [al-Ahqaf, 15]. We notice that all the grounds mentioned are for the mother, and no single ground is mentioned for the father except in His saying: ﴿And say, "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up when I was small."﴾ [al-Isra', 24], and this will be in the Hereafter.

They said: All the grounds were mentioned for the mother because the mother's hardships were in early childhood, and the child does not have the awareness by which he knows the mother's favor and her bearing of hardships for his sake; and when he grows up and his understanding develops, he finds that the father is the one who provides for him all that he needs.

Therefore: the grounds of the father are known and observed, whereas the grounds of the mother need explanation.

(1) Occasion of revelation of the verse: The exegetes said: It was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. When he embraced Islam, his mother Jamila said to him: "O Sa'd, it has reached me that you have turned away from your religion. By God, I will not be shaded by the roof of a house from the sun and wind, and I will neither eat nor drink until you disbelieve in Muhammad and return to what you were upon." She was the dearest of her children to her. Sa'd refused, so she remained for three days without eating, drinking, or seeking shade, until he feared for her. Sa'd came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and complained of that to him, so Allah revealed this verse and the one in Luqman and al-Ahqaf. [Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 195].

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds—We will surely admit them among the righteous.ﴩﷺﴪ

Wait, I should not reproduce the verse marker oddly. Here is the translation:

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds—We will surely admit them among the righteous.﴾

So He placed faith first, because it is the foundation, and then righteous deeds. Entering among the righteous is a great matter, and that is indeed so; it is sufficient that it is something the prophets themselves longed for.

Then the Almighty says:

{And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah, he regards the trial of people as the punishment of Allah. And if a victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "Indeed, we were with you." Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds?}

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah"…﴾ is evidence of saying something with the tongue while lacking patience in the face of trial. Here the speech is not supported by action. To such people the Exalted says: ﴿O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do?﴾ [al-Saff]

And the Exalted says concerning the attributes of the hypocrites: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are liars.﴾ [al-Munafiqun] So Allah does not call them liars regarding whether Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; rather, He calls them liars regarding their testimony that he is the Messenger of Allah, because testimony requires that the heart agree with the tongue, and this is not available to them.

The meaning of ﴿So when he is harmed for the sake of Allah…﴾ is: because of his belief in Allah, and he has done nothing that would warrant being harmed except that he believed. ﴿…he regards the trial of people as the punishment of Allah…﴾ means: their torment of him for his faith is like the punishment of Allah.

So he feared the punishment of people and equated it with the punishment of Allah which befalls him if he disbelieves. This is folly in equating the two punishments, because the punishment of people will end, even by the death of the one harmed and tormented, whereas the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter is lasting and does not end. People are punished according to their capacity, while Allah, glorified is He, punishes according to His power and might. Therefore, the analogy here is a faulty analogy.

And although this verse was revealed concerning ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah, the principle of jurisprudence says: the consideration is the generality of the wording, not the particularity of the cause. ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah was the brother of ʿAmr ibn Hisham (Abu Jahl) and al-Harith ibn Hisham through the mother, who was Asma'.

When ʿAyyash embraced Islam and then migrated to Medina, his mother Asma' grieved and said: "No roof shall shelter me, I shall not eat food, nor drink drink, nor bathe until ʿAyyash returns to the religion of his fathers." She remained in this state that was described for three days until hunger overcame her, and she returned.

Her two sons, al-Harith and Abu Jahl, had set out for Medina to persuade ʿAyyash to return in order to appease his mother, and they kept enticing him and softening his heart towards her. ʿAyyash agreed to go to his mother, but he refused to renounce Islam. When the three left Medina heading for Mecca, they bound him on the road, and Abu Jahl struck him a hundred lashes, and al-Harith a hundred lashes.

But Abu Jahl was more compassionate towards him than al-Harith; therefore ʿAyyash swore by Allah that if he ever caught him he would surely kill him, while he was still outside the Sacred Precinct. After ʿAyyash had appeased his mother, he returned to Medina and met his brother al-Harith at Quba'. He did not know that al-Harith had embraced Islam, so he attacked him and carried out the threat he had made, killing him. The news reached the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and the verse was revealed: ﴿And it is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake…﴾ [al-Nisa': 92]

And the verse was revealed: ﴿And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah, he regards the trial of people as the punishment of Allah…﴾ meaning: he wished to flee from the punishment of people, so he disbelieved, and he did not wish to flee from the punishment of Allah and believe.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if a victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "Indeed, we were with you"…﴾ means: give us a share of the spoils. ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds?﴾ So Allah, glorified is He, knows what passes in their breasts and what they wish for us. Therefore He, glorified is He, says of them: ﴿Had they gone out among you, they would not have increased you except in corruption.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 47]

1 Al-Suddi reported via Ibn Abi Hatim concerning the verse ﴿And among the people…﴾: some believers had believed and migrated, then Abu Sufyan caught up with them, and some of them were returned to Mecca, where they were tortured and they wavered, so Allah revealed this concerning them. [al-Durr al-Manthur 6/453]. Al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (7/5218) said: "It was also said: it was revealed concerning ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah, who embraced Islam and migrated, then was harmed and beaten and apostatized. It was only Abu Jahl and al-Harith who tortured him, and they were his maternal brothers."

2 Ibn Hajar said in his book al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah (biography no. 6118): "He was known as Dhu al-Rumhayn, a cousin of Khalid ibn al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. He was among the earliest foremost (Muslims) and made both migrations. Then Abu Jahl deceived him until they returned him from Medina to Mecca, where they imprisoned him. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to supplicate for him in the qunut. He died in the year 15 AH in al-Sham during the caliphate of ʿUmar; it was also said that he was martyred at al-Yamamah, and it was said at al-Yarmuk."

3 She was Asma' bint Makhrabah, also said to be the daughter of ʿAmr ibn Makhrabah ibn Jandal. Al-Baladhuri reported from Abu ʿUbaydah Mamar ibn al-Muthanna: Hisham ibn al-Mughirah came to Najran, saw Asma' bint Makhrabah, was attracted to her, married her and brought her to Mecca, where she bore him Abu Jahl and al-Harith. Then he died, and she married ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Rabi'ah ibn al-Mughirah, who fathered ʿAyyash, so ʿAyyash was a maternal brother of Abu Jahl and al-Harith. He also said: Muhammad ibn Sa'd said: she died in disbelief before her son ʿAyyash migrated to Medina. It is also said that she embraced Islam and lived to see the caliphate of ʿUmar, and this is more established. (al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah, Ibn Hajar, 8/10)

4 Al-Wahidi al-Naysaburi cited this story in (Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 97) concerning the occasion of revelation of ﴿And it is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake…﴾ [al-Nisa': 92]. In it: Abu Jahl and al-Harith ibn Hisham went out seeking their maternal brother ʿAyyash, came to him while he was in the atam (a fortified stone building in Medina), and said to him: "Come down, for your mother has not been sheltered by a roof since you left, and she has sworn not to eat food or drink until you return to her. God is our witness that we will not compel you to anything nor come between you and your religion." When they mentioned his mother's distress to him and bound him, he came down to them, and they took him out of Medina, bound him with a rope, and each of them lashed him a hundred lashes.

5 The truth of this matter: ʿAyyash did not kill his brother al-Harith; rather, he killed al-Harith ibn Yazid ibn Unaysah, who had been with his brothers Abu Jahl and al-Harith when they bound and beat him. Ibn Hajar said in al-Isabah in the biography (no. 1504): "He used to harm them in Mecca while he was a disbeliever. When the Companions migrated, al-Harith embraced Islam, but they did not know of his Islam, and he set out as a migrant. When he reached the outskirts of al-Harrah, ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah met him, thought he was still upon his polytheism, and struck him with the sword until he killed him, and this verse was revealed." See also al-Wahidi's Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 97) and Ibn Kathir's tafsir (1/534).

Then the Truthful, Glorified One says:

﴿And Allah will surely make evident those who have believed, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites﴾ [29:11]

Yes, Allah, glorified is He, knows the condition of His servants even before they are created, and He knows what will happen to them. However, there is a difference between prior knowledge of an event and knowledge after the event itself has occurred. For if He, glorified is He, had said, "I will do such-and-such to them, because I know what will proceed from them," they would have said, "No, by Allah, nothing from us would ever have happened." Therefore He leaves them until the act actually proceeds from them.

And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins." But they will not bear anything of their sins at all; indeed, they are liars. (29:12)

This is one form of harm: those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Follow our way..." (29:12), meaning: follow what we are upon of the religion of the fathers and forefathers, and what we are upon of worshipping idols and images. We worship gods who impose no obligations and make no demands, while you worship a God who has a method (manhaj) and makes demands: "Do this, and do not do that."

So the meaning of "Follow our way" is: take your ruling from us. "And we will bear your sins" means: act on our responsibility, and if there are sins upon you, we will bear them for you. Look here at the foolishness of the disbeliever: he himself believes that this is a sin, yet he exposes himself to bearing it. But how can he bear it, and how can he be the one held responsible for it before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, when my Lord calls me to account for it and reproaches me for following him? Does the disbeliever have any intercession or any power by which he can defend me in the Hereafter?

Therefore, the Exalted says after it: "But they will not bear anything of their sins at all; indeed, they are liars" (29:12). And He, glorified is He, confirms their lie for us also in His saying: "When those who were followed disown those who followed, and they see the punishment..." (2:166).

And the followers say: "Our Lord, show us those who led us astray of the jinn and mankind, that we may put them under our feet so that they will be among the lowest" (41:29).

So the affection that existed between them in the world turns into enmity, because they gathered in the world upon misguidance and then separated in the Hereafter, as He, glorified is He, said: "Close friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous" (43:67). The righteous person, when on the Day of Judgment he sees the one who was righteous, thanks him and acknowledges his favor, because he took him by the hand in the world and prevented him from the causes of destruction; so he loves him and praises him, and perhaps he had considered him his enemy in the world. As for the people of misguidance, some of them curse one another and some of them disown one another.

So the foolishness of the disbelievers is clear in their saying: "And we will bear your sins" (29:12), just as it is clear in their saying: "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down stones upon us from the sky or bring us a painful punishment" (8:32).

And just as it is clear in their saying: "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse" (63:7). They know that he is the Messenger of Allah, yet they prevent people from spending on the poor who are with him; it is foolishness even in confrontation.

In another place: ﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and from the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge. Unquestionably, evil is what they bear.﴾ [An-Nahl 16:25]. So the "atqal" (burdens) are the awzar (sins). Thus ﴿they will surely bear their own burdens, and burdens along with their burdens﴾. The first burdens are due to their own misguidance, and the other burdens are due to their misleading others(1). ﴿And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate﴾ [Al-Ankabut 29:13]. And al-iftira' (fabrication): deliberately telling lies.

1 Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ibn al-Hanafiyyah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Abu Jahl and the chieftains of Quraysh used to intercept people when they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) to embrace Islam, saying: "He forbids wine, he forbids fornication, and he forbids what the Arabs used to do. So turn back, and we will bear your burdens." Then this verse was revealed: ﴿And they will surely bear their burdens and burdens along with their burdens...﴾ [Al-Ankabut 29:13]. [Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 6/454].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 29, verse 14:

After the Truthful One (al-Haqq, subhanahu) spoke about the preliminaries in general, He wished to speak about them specifically concerning the messengers, so He said, glorified is He:

{And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years, and the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers.} (29:14)

The scholars say: Noah, peace be upon him, is the first of Allah's messengers to mankind. As for those who preceded him, such as Adam and Idris, peace be upon them, they were prophets to whom Allah revealed a law by which they acted, so they served as a model of faith and an example of good conduct, which those who saw them would imitate. Yet whoever did not follow them is not considered a disbeliever. But whoever followed them and then deviated from their path is a disbeliever.

Therefore we distinguish between the prophet (nabi) and the messenger (rasul): the prophet is one to whom a law was revealed by which he acted, but he was not commanded to convey it; the messenger is one to whom a law was revealed and who was commanded to convey it. Each of them is sent (mursal). Thus the Most High says: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet...﴾ (22:52).

So, the prophet is also one who is sent, but he is sent for his own self.

But why was this [mission] specifically before Noah? They said: Because the human sphere was narrow before Noah, and people were recently created, deviations had not spread among them. When the sphere expanded and the affairs of life became intertwined, creation needed Allah to send messengers to them.

The Most High gives this concise snapshot of the story of Noah, peace be upon him, even though he has a surah of his own and has many scattered snapshots in the Mighty Book. But this snapshot gives us only the beginning and the end, as if it were a telegram (telegraphic) regarding the matter of Noah:

﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people...﴾ (29:14)

So, the messenger came from among the people, and this means they knew him before he became a messenger; they tested his conduct and movement in life, knew his character, and knew all his behaviour. The messenger was not distant from them or unknown to them.

Therefore, when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, openly proclaimed the call, those who knew him closely believed in him without asking him for a miracle to confirm him, but merely upon his saying, "I am the Messenger of Allah," they believed in him, affirmed him, and followed him.

Did Sayyidina Abu Bakr hear from the Messenger of Allah before he believed in him? No. Rather, as soon as they said to him, "Your companion has claimed to be a prophet," he said, "I believed in him."(2) Why? Because he knew of his past conduct upon which he built his faith in his companion. Muhammad would not be a man of great character among people and then lie about Allah.

So, in the fact that the messenger is from his people there is reassurance for creation. Therefore, when they said, "We will not believe unless a messenger comes to us as an angel," he replied to them: ﴿Are you angels that an angel should descend to you?﴾

﴿Say: If there were in the earth angels walking calmly, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger.﴾ (17:95)

Even if We had sent him as an angel, would they see the angels? They do not see them. How then would the angel convey to the people? He would have to come to them in the form of a human, and if he came to them in the form of a human they would say, "We want an angel."

As for the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years...﴾ (29:14), this number can convey many meanings, for He did not say, "He remained among them nine hundred and fifty years."(3) There are many secrets in the numbers of the Qur'an. Read, for example: ﴿And We appointed for Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten, so the appointed time of his Lord was completed as forty nights...﴾ (7:142)

And in the verse of Surat al-Baqarah the Most High said: ﴿And when We appointed for Moses forty nights...﴾ (2:51)

In Surat al-Baqarah there is summary, and in the verse of al-A'raf there is detail. The wisdom in this is that as soon as Moses, peace be upon him, went to the appointed time with his Lord, his people worshipped the calf during the period of the thirty nights. Allah did not wish to leave Moses to return to his people after the thirty nights, so He completed them with ten more, so that Moses would not return and see what his people had done. Thus the ten were added to the thirty nights, so as to give you the final image found in Surat al-Baqarah.

The matter is most precise. If He had not included the exception in His saying, ﴿less fifty years...﴾ (29:14), the listener might think the matter is approximate. But approximation is in the counting of human beings; in the reckoning of the Most High, it is utmost precision. It is as if you were asked, for example, about the time, and you say, "Ten o'clock less one minute and a half," meaning: the utmost of what you are capable of in reckoning time.

If you ask: Why this quick snapshot of the story of Noah, peace be upon him? We say: It is to console the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, because his people stood against him in hostility, arrogance, and denial, harmed his companions, and constricted the pressure upon his call. This matter lasted until it took thirteen years of the age of the call, so his Lord consoled him: "Be patient, O Muhammad, for a colleague of yours in the call has been patient a thousand years less fifty years." That is, the period of hardship you have endured is trivial and easy, and the messengers of firm resolve endured even more than that.

We note here ﴿a thousand years...﴾ (29:14), then He made an exception from it: ﴿less fifty years...﴾ (29:14), and He did not say "fifty years." He made the exception of years from years, to indicate that "sanah" (year) means any "'am" (year), and to remove disagreement, because some say that "sanah" is what begins from the first of Muharram to the end of Dhu al-Hijjah. Whereas the year is not necessarily to begin with Muharram and end with Dhu al-Hijjah; rather it begins at any time and ends at a similar time after a full year.

So when we say, "So-and-so is, for example, twenty years old," we mean: from the day of his birth to a similar day twenty times. Likewise the year. Therefore, the sanah, the 'am, and the hijjah are all the same, whether you calculate by the solar year, the lunar year, or any other, as you wish.

It is known that our time-reckoning is by the lunar Arabic months, because from the movement of the sun we know only the day; we do not know the month from it. We know the month by the movement of the moon when the crescent is born, and by the month we calculate the year, which is twelve lunar months and exceeds the solar year by eleven days.

It is as if the Most High wished to teach us that the sanah is the 'am; there is no difference between them, and there is no need for dispute on this matter.

Then the Most High mentions the end of these people who denied: ﴿So the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers.﴾ (29:14) The cause of their seizure was not that they were enemies, but that they wronged themselves by disbelief. Thus the story, or snapshot, ends in one verse, the purpose of which is to console the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, if his victory over the disbelievers is delayed.

The word ﴿seized them...﴾ (29:14) — the seizing (akhdh) here is evidence of severity and strength of grasp. Was it with violence or without violence? If the seizing is of an adversary, it is seizing with violence and severity; if it is of a non-adversary, it is with gentleness.

And the tufan (flood): that the water exceeds the regular need of people, so that what was a means of life, and from which every living thing came, becomes a means of death and destruction. It is as if the Most High wishes to draw our attention to the opposites in creation, so that we do not think creation proceeds in a monotonous way.

Sayyidina Musa, peace be upon him, struck the sea with his staff, and the water in it congealed until it became like a mountain, and he struck the rock with it and water gushed from it.

It is the absolute power that does not depend on causes. The causer is Allah, glorified is He, who does what He wills. Things are not by their causes; rather they are by the will of the causer in them. Therefore Ahmad Shawqi says in his poem "The Nile":

From what era does it flow through the villages, and by what hand does it pour abundantly in the cities? Did it descend from the sky, or upon the gardens as rippling streams?
Until he says: He pours the water and it becomes gold(4), and He drowns the earth and the drowned one lives.

The ones seized here are the deniers of Noah, peace be upon him, who wronged themselves when they denied their messenger and did not listen to guidance. Then Allah saved Noah, peace be upon him, by the ship, of which He said in Surat Hud: ﴿And he said, "Board it; in the name of Allah is its course and its anchorage."﴾ (11:41)

Allah had commanded him to build the ship: ﴿And construct the ark under Our eyes and Our revelation, and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned.﴾ (11:37) So Noah, peace be upon him, had knowledge of the outcome of the deniers and wrongdoers among his people, and he kept it within himself while he built the ship as his Lord commanded him.

But was the ship something known to these people, and did they have prior acquaintance with it? No. They did not know ships, as evidenced by their wonder at Noah's deed and their mockery of him while he was building it: ﴿And whenever a chief of his people passed by him, they mocked him.﴾ (11:38) So he would answer them in himself: ﴿If you mock us, indeed we mock you as you mock.﴾ (11:38) He knew their end and what Allah had prepared for them.

The Most High gives us this snapshot of the story of Noah, peace be upon him, so that we roam through all the snapshots and recall the places of lesson in them. There are many matters to benefit from the story of Noah. The people worshipped idols: Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq, and Nasr. From this we learn that the love of the prophets is love of values and method, and love of deeds and emulation, and that their lineages are lineages of piety and scrupulousness.

The prophethood of Noah did not prevent his errant son from drowning, even after he called upon Allah: ﴿My Lord, indeed my son is of my family, and indeed Your promise is true...﴾ (11:45) So Allah gives him the judgment on this matter and corrects him: ﴿Indeed, he is not of your family; indeed, he is one whose work was other than righteous...﴾ (11:46)

This does not mean that a woman brought him from unlawful relations, God forbid; for Allah would not deceive any of His prophets. Rather, she was of the treacherous ones, and her treachery was that she disclosed his secrets to his opponents and tested them with his news.
