Therefore, concerning her, the Most High says in Surat al-Tahrim: ﴿Allah presents an example for those who disbelieved: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot...﴾ (66:10)

The Most High states the cause in His saying, ﴿Indeed, he is not of your family,﴾ (11:46) by His saying, ﴿indeed, he is one whose work was other than righteous,﴾ (11:46) so that our thoughts do not wander concerning the wife of the prophet of Allah. The cause is that he did other than righteous work, and the kinship of the prophets is kinship of deeds, not kinship of lineage.

1 Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated in his book "Dhamm al-Dunya" (p. 88, Maktabat al-Qur'an), from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Angel of Death came to Noah, peace be upon him, and said: "O longest-lived of the prophets, how did you find the world and its pleasure?" He said: "Like a man who entered a house with two doors; he stood in the middle of the doorway for a moment, then left by the other door." Al-Suyuti also cited it in "al-Durr al-Manthur" (6/456).
2 Al-Bayhaqi cited it in "Dala'il al-Nubuwwah" (2/164) that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "I have not called anyone to Islam except that he had a hesitation, reluctance, and consideration, except Abu Bakr; he did not delay upon hearing it from me, and did not hesitate about it." He attributed it to Ibn Ishaq.
3 Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/5222): If it is said: Why did He say, ﴿a thousand years less fifty years﴾ (29:14), and not say "nine hundred and fifty years"? There are two answers: The first: that the purpose is to multiply the number, so mentioning the thousand is greater in wording and greater in number. The second: what is related, that he was given a lifespan of a thousand years, then gave fifty years of his life to some of his offspring, and when death came to him he returned to complete the thousand; so Allah mentioned it as a reminder that the shortfall was on his part.
4 Al-'Asjad: gold. It is said: it is a comprehensive term for all jewels, including pearls and rubies. [Lisan al-'Arab, entry: '-s-j-d]

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

{So We saved him and the companions of the ark, and made it a sign for the worlds.}

That is, We saved Noah, peace be upon him, ﴿and the companions of the ark...﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:15]. They are those who rode with him in it. They are its companions, and it was made for their sake. Noah did not build it for his own sake; he built it for his people, who marvelled at his craftsmanship, mocked him and ridiculed him. They are its companions in reality: whoever among them believed boarded it, and whoever disbelieved refused and turned away, so his end was drowning.

From this matter we understand that when Allah, exalted is He, asks the believer for something and gives it to someone who does not have that thing, whether it is knowledge, wealth or ability, etc., you should know that it is a right due to him, and not a favour bestowed upon him. When Noah built the ark, Allah made it the right of the people, saying ﴿and the companions of the ark...﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:15]. So it is their right. The intention is not that he should build it, for example, and rent it to them; rather, he builds it for their sake.

Likewise is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And those in whose wealth there is a known right (ḥaqq ma'lum)...﴾ [al-Ma'arij 70:24]. This right in wealth has been mentioned twice in the Noble Qur'an: once as ﴿a known right﴾ [al-Ma'arij 70:24], and once as ﴿a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾ [al-Dhariyat 51:19], without specifying its amount and without being described as known.

Allah has called both of them a right. The known one is the obligatory zakat in the station of faith, and the unknown one is voluntary charity (sadaqah), because it is not bound to a fixed amount, but is according to the believer's generosity and love of acts of obedience, and his entry into the station of excellence (ihsan), concerning which Allah said: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs, taking what their Lord has given them. Indeed, they were before that doers of good. They used to sleep little of the night, and in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness, and in their wealth was a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾ [al-Dhariyat 51:15–19].

This increase in acts of worship is a sign of love for obligation, love of obedience, and confidence that Allah, exalted is He, has only imposed upon us less than what He deserves of worship. Therefore the scholars say: beware of moving to this station and obliging yourself to it, or making it a vow, for if you do, it becomes a duty upon you from which you cannot reduce anything.

Rather, make it for your energy and capacity, for if you accustom yourself to a method and oblige yourself to it, then withdraw from it, it is as if you say a word that should not be said. It is as if you—God forbid—tested your love for Allah and did not find yourself a true lover, so you abandoned it.

Thus His saying, glory be to Him, ﴿and the companions of the ark...﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:15] shows us that it was made by the command of Allah for their sake, and that when Noah finished building it, it became their right, not his possession, peace be upon him.

But how do we understand ﴿and the companions of the ark...﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:15] when Noah, peace be upon him, carried in it two of every kind? They said: the pair of non-human creatures has no companionship, because they are owned by the companions (human beings).

As for His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿and made it a sign for the worlds﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:15], that is, a marvellous matter with no precedent in people's lives. Noah, peace be upon him, built it by revelation from his Lord, without any previous model. The meaning of it being a sign is that Allah informed him of it and taught him how to build it, because it had a faith-related purpose in His sight: in it was the salvation of the believers and the drowning of the disbelievers. And this sign is for ﴿the worlds﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:15], all of them.

(1) Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/5223): "The hā' and alif in ‘jaʻalnāhā’ refer either to the ship, or to the punishment, or to the deliverance — three opinions."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 29, verse 16:

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq) subhanahu mentions Ibrahim (peace be upon him), saying:

{And Ibrahim, when he said to his people: "Worship Allah and fear Him. That is better for you, if you only knew."} [16]

The waw here is for coordinating sentences (waw al-'atf lil-jumal), so the verse is conjoined to ﴿And We had sent Nuh...﴾ [14] (al-'Ankabut). Thus Nuh and Ibrahim are both objects of the verb "We sent" (arsalna). Someone may ask: why is Ibrahim not given tanwin as Nuh was? The word Ibrahim is not given tanwin because it is a diptote (ism mamnu' min al-sarf), that is, prevented from tanwin, because it is a non-Arabic (a'jami) name.

We note on this matter that all the names of the prophets are non-Arabic names that are prevented from declension (mamnu' min al-sarf), except the names that begin with these letters (sa, nun, shin, mim, lam, ha — "sin shamlah" mnemonic): Salih, Nuh, Shu'ayb, Muhammad, Lut, Hud. These names are declined with tanwin, upon them all be prayer and peace.

The meaning: ﴿And Ibrahim...﴾ [16] means: mention Ibrahim, ﴿when he said to his people: "Worship Allah and fear Him..."﴾ [16]. We have said that worship (ibadah) is that the worshipper obeys the one worshipped in His commands and prohibitions. Thus, if someone who claims divinity comes, and he has no command that we carry out, nor prohibition that we refrain from, he is not fit to be a god.

Therefore those who said: ﴿We only worship them so that they bring us nearer to Allah in position﴾ [az-Zumar: 3] were lying, because they worshipped idols only because these have no commands or prohibitions. Their divinity is (mandhariyyah, i.e. merely theoretical/ imagined) without obligation, so the first of the proofs of the falsehood of worshipping these claimed gods is that they are gods without a method (manhaj).

Then the command ﴿and fear Him﴾ [16] is conjoined to ﴿worship﴾ [16]. Among the meanings of taqwa is that you obey the commands and avoid the prohibitions, so it is synonymous with worship. But if it is conjoined to worship, it means: carry out the command so that you may guard against the anger of Allah; make between yourselves and the attributes of majesty (sifat al-jalal) a shield.

We have said before that Allah the Exalted has attributes of majesty, such as al-Qahhar, al-Jabbar, al-Muntaqim, al-Mudhill, etc., and attributes of beauty, such as al-Ghaffar, al-Rahman, al-Rahim, al-Tawwab. By taqwa you attain the objects of the attributes of beauty, and you protect and shield yourself from the objects of the attributes of majesty.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That is better for you, if you only knew﴾ [16]: "That" refers to what has preceded of the command to worship and to fear Allah; it is better for you. If you do not know this matter, then there is no good in your knowledge, as He, Exalted, said: ﴿But most of mankind do not know. They know an outward appearance of the worldly life...﴾ [ar-Rum: 6–7].

True knowledge is the knowledge of the matters of the Hereafter, the knowledge of the rulings and of the method which gives you true good of long duration, unlike the knowledge of this world; if you obtain some good from it, it is a good limited by your lifespan in it.

We have said before that knowledge is the perception of a cosmic matter that you can demonstrate, and this includes every piece of information in life; that is, empirical material knowledge and its effects in this world. But the lofty, supreme knowledge is that you know what Allah wills for you, and this is for the Hereafter.

Read in this regard, for example, His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth thereby fruits of varying colors. And among the mountains are streaks, white and red, of varying shades, and black, extremely dark. And among men and creatures and cattle are those of varying colors. Only those who have knowledge among His servants fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might, Forgiving.﴾ [Fatir: 27–28]

He, subhanahu, mentioned the knowledge of plants and minerals; "among men" [28] means the knowledge of humanities (al-insaniyat); "and creatures" [28] means the knowledge of animals; and thus He gathered all kinds and genera. Then He said, subhanahu: ﴿Only those who have knowledge among His servants fear Allah﴾ [28], although He did not mention here any legal ruling (hukm shar'i).

So the intended meaning here is the scholars who derive certain truths in existence, like these discoveries which serve the movement of life, direct people to the power of Allah and the wonder of His creation, and remind them of Him, subhanahu.

Consider, for example, the placement of the windpipe (al-qasabah al-hawa'iyyah) beside the pharynx (al-balqum), and how, if you choke on half a grain of rice, you are not at ease until it is expelled. Consider the placement of the uvula (al-lahat) and how it works automatically without intention from you or control over it.

Consider the flaps at the windpipe, how they move upward to expel what enters of food if the balance of the uvula is disturbed, so that you do not control the closing of the windpipe during swallowing.

Consider when you are sitting calm, nothing troubling you, then in a moment you find yourself in need of the toilet. What happened? That is because in the intestinal tract there is something like the (siqqatah, flush mechanism) that expels waste in measure; when it exceeds what you can bear, the need to relieve oneself and expel this excess waste becomes necessary.

Consider the nose and what is in it of hairs at the entrance of the air and mucus inside: they were made thus for a wisdom. The hairs trap the dust that clings to the air, then the mucus catches the fine dust that does not stick to the hairs, so that the air enters the lungs pure and clear. Consider the ear from the outside and the various winding passages in it, of differing directions, to ward off the air and prevent it from striking the ear's opening.

The signs in the human body are many, beyond counting, and there is no way to know them except through the derivation of scholars and their uncovering of them. This is one of the activities of the human mind. But knowledge that goes beyond the scope of the human mind descends from above; it is the law of preservation which the Creator, subhanahu, set to protect creation. Whoever takes only worldly empirical knowledge is deprived of the lasting good, because the most that the knowledge of matter gives you in humans is to make your material life comfortable, whereas the knowledge of the Hereafter makes your worldly life comfortable and remains for you in the Hereafter.

So His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That is better for you﴾ [16] means: the divine law of preservation, "do this and do not do that"; and beware of transferring the meaning of "do" into "do not do," or the meaning of "do not do" into "do." We have likened this law to the (catalogue/manual) which the manufacturer provides to protect the material product so that each performs its task in the best way. Likewise is Allah's method with respect to creation. If you do not know this matter, then no knowledge will benefit you afterward.

He, subhanahu, says: ﴿Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We will increase him in his harvest; and whoever desires the harvest of this world, We will give him from it, but he will have no share in the Hereafter.﴾ [ash-Shura: 20]

So the lasting good is the good in the Hereafter.

1 The reason for the accusative case of the word Ibrahim in the verse has three opinions, mentioned by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (7/5224):
Al-Kisa'i said: it is governed by "anjayna" (we saved), meaning it is conjoined to the pronoun (the ha').
Al-Kisa'i also permitted that it be conjoined to Nuh, and the meaning would be: and We sent Ibrahim.
A third opinion: that it is accusative by the meaning: "and mention Ibrahim..."
2 Al-jaddah from the mountain: a piece of it. Al-jaddah from a thing: a part of it whose color differs from the color of the rest. Allah says: ﴿And among the mountains are streaks, white and red, of varying shades, and black﴾ [Fatir: 27], meaning: among the mountains are parts of varying colors. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/118].
3 Al-gharabib: plural of gharib, meaning intensely black. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/50].

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

{Indeed, you worship idols instead of Allah, and you invent a lie.
Indeed, those whom you worship instead of Allah do not possess for you any provision. So seek provision from Allah, worship Him, and give thanks to Him. To Him you will be returned.} [29:17]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, you worship...﴾ [29:17] means: according to their claim, and according to their saying: ﴿We only worship them so that they may bring us near to Allah in position.﴾ [39:3]. Otherwise there is no worship for these deities, since they have no command, no prohibition, and no method. Their worship, then, is void.

They worship idols instead of Allah. When the noose tightens around them, they say: ﴿We only worship them so that they may bring us near to Allah in position.﴾ [39:3]. Thus they are polytheists, and whoever does not say this is a disbeliever.

The wathan (idol) is whatever is set up for veneration, of stone, whatever its type: limestone, granite, or marble; or of metal: gold, silver, copper, etc.; or of wood. Some of them used to make it from dates (ajwa), so that when they were hungry they would eat it. Sayyidina ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) related this in a tone of astonishment.

By what intellect or logic do you go to the mountain, choose a stone from it, carve it into a particular shape, then take it as a god to worship instead of Allah, when it is the work of your own hand? If the wind knocks it down, you raise it up again; if you break it, you go about repairing and restoring what you broke. What intellect could accept such an act?

For this reason the Qur'an addresses them: ﴿He said: Do you worship what you carve?﴾ [37:95]. And whenever the world advances, this phenomenon fades away, because it is a matter that no longer suits the intellect in any way.

The meaning of ﴿and you invent a lie﴾ [29:17] is: you bring into existence (tukhliqun). Bringing into existence is from non-existence. They bring things into existence from nothing. But do they bring into existence in truth, or in falsehood? They bring into existence ﴿a lie﴾ [29:17]. Ifk (lie) is the deliberate falsehood that gives things a false name, and from it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the overturned cities He overthrew﴾ [53:53], meaning the towns that Allah overturned upon themselves.

We have already explained that truth (haqiqa) is a true proposition that corresponds to reality. If you say, for example, "Muhammad is generous," then there must be a person named Muhammad who has the quality of generosity. If reality differs, so that no Muhammad exists, or one exists but does not have the quality of generosity, then the proposition is false, because it contradicts reality. This is ifk.

The Truth, glorified is He, does not reproach them for creating, since He Himself affirmed creation for the servants, saying: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾ [23:14].

The difference is that you create from something existing, while the Truth, glorified is He, creates from nothing. You make cloth from cotton, for example, a glass cup from sand, and a plough from iron, etc. You bring a non-existent thing from a prior existing thing. But the Creator, glorified is He, brings a non-existent thing from no existence at all.

We have already explained that human craftsmanship stays fixed in its state: a knife, for example, remains a knife and does not grow, until it becomes a cleaver, for instance, and a cup does not give birth to other cups. But the creation of Allah, glorified is He, has the qualities of growth, life, reproduction, etc. For this reason Allah has done you justice by describing you as a creator, but He, glorified is He, is the best of creators.

So the Truth, glorified is He, does not fault them for creating; rather, He faults them for creating falsehood and lies.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed, those whom you worship instead of Allah do not possess for you any provision. So seek provision from Allah﴾ [29:17]. Elsewhere the Truth, glorified is He, has shown them that they worship gods that neither harm nor benefit. Here He mentions an important matter: the sustaining of human life by sustenance, which we call rizq (provision). Those gods you worship instead of Allah do not possess for you any provision. Had rain been withheld from you and the land become barren, you would have died of hunger.

So you should have reflected: from where do the foundations of your life come, and who is the one who bestows favor in them, so that you turn to Him in worship and obedience? As we say in the proverb: "He who eats my morsel should listen to my word." Does He feed you, and you listen to others?!

Provision is the preoccupation of people. At first, all of us strive to eat, drink, and live. Then, when affairs improve, we desire to store for the future: the employee, for example, saves for a month, and the farmer saves for the whole year.

Among the wonders of this matter is that you find man, the mouse, and the ant to be the only creatures among Allah's creatures that store for the future. As for the rest of the animals, they take only their needs of food and leave the remainder, never concerning themselves with this matter, nor preoccupied with tomorrow's provision at all. None eats more than its capacity, nor saves anything for its morrow.

For this reason Allah reminds His servants of the matter of provision because of its importance in their lives. And among the wonders of provision is that it knows your place and address better than you know its place and address. If provision has been decreed for you, it comes knocking at your door; and if you are deprived of it, its pursuit wearies you.

Among the clearest examples that provision is apportioned and decreed by Allah for each of us is that when a woman conceives, the menstruation that used to come to her periodically before pregnancy stops. Where has this blood gone? This blood is the provision of the fetus in its mother's womb; no one else takes it or benefits from it, not even the mother.

If the fetus is decreed, this blood turns into nourishment specifically for it. If the mother is not decreed to conceive, this blood comes out from her in a repulsive form; it must be expelled, because it is harmful to the mother if it remains, so it must come out. It is not her provision, but the provision of her child in her womb. Had this blood not been the provision of the fetus, the mother would weaken every time this periodic bleeding recurred in this way. So for each of us there is a provision that no one else takes.

For this reason one of the righteous said: "I marvel at the son of Adam, who strives for what has been guaranteed to him, and neglects what has been demanded of him."

Your Lord has guaranteed your provision, so look at what He has demanded of you, and occupy yourself with what Allah wills for you. Therefore we marvel at those beggars whom we used to see, for example, in the seasons of Hajj, the worst of whom display their afflictions and the afflictions of their children to people, begging with them, as if they complain of the Creator to the creation and grumble at Allah's decree. Allah, exalted is He, does not like His servant to complain of Him to His creatures.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If you are afflicted, then conceal it." By Allah, if the afflicted concealed their affliction and sat in their homes, Allah would bring their provisions to their doorsteps.

So provision is guaranteed by Allah; for this reason He bestows it upon His servants as a favor, and negates it from these false deities: ﴿they do not possess for you any provision. So seek provision from Allah﴾ [29:17]. Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Worship Him, give thanks to Him. To Him you will be returned﴾ [29:17]. If you do not worship Him because He provides for you and feeds you, then worship Him because your return is to Him and your standing before Him.

It would have sufficed that His blessings upon you precede His obligations upon you. He left you to flourish in His bounties without imposing anything upon you, until you reached the age of maturity, the age of ripeness, puberty, and the ability to beget someone like you. Then, after that, do you answer His obligation to you with denial? Worshipping Allah and obeying Him, even if it were nothing but thanks to Him for what He has bestowed upon you, would still be obligatory upon you.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and give thanks to Him﴾ [29:17], because your Lord, mighty and majestic, wants to increase you, so He made thanks for blessings the key to this increase. He, glorified is He, said: ﴿If you give thanks, I will surely increase you﴾ [14:7]. Your Lord awaits from you the word of thanks; the moment you receive a blessing with your saying "Praise be to Allah," increase has become due to you.

Some of the knowers hold that praise is not only for the countless blessings of Allah, but that praise is due to Allah for the fact that there is no god but Allah. Otherwise, if there were another god, we would be perplexed as to which of them to follow. Oneness is among the greatest blessings of the One, glorified is He, which necessitate thanks.

The Truth, glorified is He, has given us an example of this matter in His saying: ﴿Allah presents a parable: a man in whom are partners at odds with one another, and a man belonging wholly to one master. Are the two equal in comparison?﴾ [39:29]. That is, one owned by partners who disagree, and would that they agreed. And a man belonging wholly to one man, i.e., owned by one master. Are the two equal as an example? Likewise, the monotheist to Allah and the one who associates others with Him.

For this reason one of the righteous says, regarding His saying: ﴿O you who believe, eat of the good things We have provided for you﴾ [2:172]: the thief who eats from the unlawful eats his provision, yet it is provision from the unlawful. Had he been patient and refrained from theft, he would have eaten from the lawful, and Allah would have brought it to him.

The meaning, then, is that Allah created you and provided for you, and this does not mean that you should escape from Him. If you do not observe the prior grace, then fear what is yet to come.

¹ The complete text of this hadith: "If you are afflicted with sins, then conceal them," cited by al-ʿAjlūnī in Kashf al-Khafa (1/87) (hadith 1/211), who said: "Al-Bayhaqi and al-Hakim related it from Ibn ʿUmar." The hadith more fitting as evidence here is that which al-Hakim recorded in his Mustadrak (1/349) from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah the Exalted said: When I afflict My believing servant and he does not complain of Me to his visitors, I release him from his captivity, then replace for him flesh better than his flesh and blood better than his blood, then he begins the deed anew." Al-Hakim declared it sound according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), and al-Dhahabi affirmed it. And Allah the Most High knows best.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 29, verse 18:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if you deny...﴾ [18] (al-'Ankabut): that is, what We told you and what Our Messenger brought you. For believing him will bring you under the obligation of responsibility (taklif), will burden you with the hardship of the method, and will constrict for you the sphere of choice. Yet Allah, glory be to Him, has honored you when He gave you freedom of choice, whereas the whole cosmos has no choice, for it has surrendered its choice to the choice of its Lord.

As He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it, and man bore it. Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant.﴾ [72] (al-Ahzab)

So the whole cosmos is subjected, performing its duty, as He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And there is not a thing but that it exalts His praise...﴾ [44] (al-Isra')

And He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Have you not seen that to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the moving creatures, and many of the people? But upon many the punishment has been justified...﴾ [18] (al-Hajj). The rule is general, with no exception, except for man, among whom are the obedient and among whom are the disobedient.

So the meaning of ﴿And if you deny...﴾ [18] (al-'Ankabut) is: you are not unprecedented in denial, ﴿for [many] nations before you denied﴾ [18] (al-'Ankabut). But it is incumbent upon you to take heed of what was done to the denying nations and how their end turned out, so beware lest there befall you what befell them. This is the matter to which you ought to be attentive.

Here some quibblers have stopped and said: How does the Qur'an say, in addressing the people of Abraham, ﴿And if you deny, then [many] nations before you denied﴾ [18] (al-'Ankabut), when no community preceded them except one community, the people of Noah, peace be upon him? They imagine they have found a point against the Qur'an.

We say: Yes, the community of Noah was the community of the message intended by faith, but before it came Adam, Seth and Idris, and they were all among past nations relative to Abraham. Or we say: because Noah's stay among his people was long, lasting a thousand years of the span of time, and this period includes about ten generations, and a generation, as they have said, is a hundred years, each of which is a nation in itself.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And the Messenger's duty is only the clear delivery [of the message]﴾ [18] (al-'Ankabut). So his mission is merely delivery. Whoever believes believes, and whoever disbelieves disbelieves. We will not give the Messenger a reward or commission for each person who believes in him. So beware lest you think that by your disbelief you diminish the Prophet's reward, especially since they were averse to him. The meaning is: [his duty is] delivery only, and he has delivered, so he will receive his recompense and reward from his Lord. You do not plot against me by your disbelief; rather, you plot against yourselves.

Therefore our Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would grieve most intensely and suffer if one of his community slipped from his hand and disbelieved, until his Lord addressed him: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [272] (al-Baqarah).

And He addressed him saying: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they will not be believers﴾ [3] (al-Shu'ara').

When there was revealed to him, peace and blessings be upon him: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested [you]. And the Hereafter is better for you than the first. And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ [1-5] (al-Duha), the Prophet seized the opportunity and supplicated his Lord: "Then I will not be content while one of my community is in the Fire"(1). This is because he, peace and blessings be upon him, loved his community, was eager for them, and was kind and merciful toward them: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer; [he is] concerned over you and to the believers, kind and merciful﴾ [128] (al-Tawbah)(2).

Allah, glory be to Him, described the delivery as "clear" (mubin), meaning: evident and manifest, because some delivery is merely a presentation of the matter without confirming and making manifest the proof that supports the delivery.

1 Al-Khatib narrated in "Talkhis al-Mutashabih" from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: Muhammad will not be content while one of his community is in the Fire. Al-Bayhaqi narrated in "Shu'ab al-Iman" from Ibn 'Abbas also that he said: His contentment is that all of his community enter Paradise. See al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti (8/542).
2 Al-'Anat: hardship. That is: they loved and wished for the continuation of your hardship and the continuation of difficulties upon you. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/38].

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

{Have they not seen how Allah originates creation, then repeats it? Indeed that is easy for Allah. (19)}

The address here is directed to the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ): those who denied before, and you who deny now. So where are your minds? If you had used your minds to contemplate the universe in which you live, into which you have been thrown, and which has been prepared for you with every requirement of your life.

﴿Have they not seen how Allah originates creation...(19)﴾ [al-'Ankabut]. Here "ra'a" (to see) means " 'alima" (to know), as in His saying, ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant? (1)﴾ [al-Fil], meaning: have you not known? This is because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not witness the incident of the elephant, and the expression shifted from "ta'lam" (you know) to "tara" (you see) to draw our attention to the fact that Allah's informing His Messenger (ﷺ) is more certain for him than seeing it with his own eyes.

From this is the saying of the Companion Abu Bakr al-Siddiq when he heard of the event of the Isra' and Mi'raj: "If he said it, then he has told the truth."

The hamza in ﴿Have they not seen...(19)﴾ [al-'Ankabut] is an interrogative for confirmation (istifham li-taqrir), just as you say to your son: "Have you not seen what so-and-so, who neglected his lessons, did?" You want to deny to him that he too should neglect, so you have him acknowledge the consequence of neglect, and you leave him to state it with his own tongue, and he says to you: "The one who neglected his lessons failed."

And just as you say to one who denies your favour: "Did I not do good to you with such and such?" and he acknowledges it himself, instead of you enumerating it for him; this is more eloquent in acknowledgment.

So when a negation comes after the hamza, they call it an interrogative of denial (istifham inkari): you deny what they are upon, and you want to confirm them in what contradicts it. And a negation after a denial is a negation of a negation, and the negation of a negation is an affirmation.

So the meaning is: Do they deny while they have not seen what happened to the earlier denying nations? Do they deny while they have not seen the signs of Allah, and His power spread throughout all existence? They should have looked with a glance of consideration so that they might know who created this creation. And if you were to ask them, "Who created this universe?", they would find no answer, and could only say, "Allah," as the Qur'an relates: ﴿If you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, Allah...(25)﴾ [Luqman].

But how do they acknowledge this truth and confess it, while they are disbelievers in Allah? They said: because it is a matter too evident for any denier to deny. Every craftsman, however small his craft, takes pride in it and attributes it to himself, and even attributes to himself what he did not make. So what of a universe prepared with such precision and such grandeur, which no one has claimed for himself? A claim establishes its claimant's right when no opposing claim stands against it.

Therefore we say: the Truth, glorified is He, before He says "there is no god but I," and before He asks us for it, bore witness to it for Himself, exalted is He: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He...(18)﴾ [Al 'Imran]. For this testimony is what will make Him say to a thing, "Be," and it is. Had He not believed that He is God, He would not have said it.

And the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿Have they not seen how Allah originates creation, then repeats it...(19)﴾ [al-'Ankabut]. How, when we have not seen the repetition, let alone seen the beginning?

They said: we see the beginning and the repetition in the manifestations of existence around us. We see it in the crops, for example, and how Allah, exalted is He, revives the earth with vegetation; then the time of harvest comes, it is reaped, and the grain or seeds scatter from it, which renew the cycle anew. And the rose: you find in it moisture, freshness, marvellous colours and a pleasant fragrance; then when it is plucked, its water evaporates, so it dries and crumbles, and its fragrance departs into the air, then another new rose follows it, and so on.

Consider, for example, the cycle of water in the universe: has the quantity of water that Allah created in the universe increased when He prepared it for human life since He created Adam and Eve? The water is the same until now, despite the increase in the number of inhabitants; because the elements of the universe are the same since Allah created them, but they have a cycle in which they move between beginning and repetition.

And read, if you wish, His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days, and you set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed in it firm mountains above it, and blessed it, and measured in it its sustenance...(10)﴾ [Fussilat].

It is as if the sustenance of the world, of crops and other things, has been prepared since the beginning of creation, and until the Hour arrives it does not increase, but it circulates in natural cycles.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed that is easy for Allah (19)﴾ [al-'Ankabut]. Which is it: the creation or the repetition? As for the creation, they have acknowledged it, and there is no dispute about it. So the discussion is about the repetition: is He who created from nothing unable to repeat what He created? The first creation was from nothing, whereas the repetition is from something existing. So which is easier in your estimation and according to your own logic?

For this reason the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And He it is who originates creation, then repeats it, and it is easier for Him...(27)﴾ [al-Rum]. Although it is not said of the Truth, glorified is He, that this is easy or that this is easier; but He addresses us in terms that our minds can grasp.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 29, verse 20:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, addresses Muhammad (ﷺ):

{Say: "Travel in the earth and see how He began creation; then Allah will bring about the last creation. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent."} (29:20)

Al-sayr (travel): moving from one place to another. But do we travel in the earth or upon the earth? The truth is that we, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Say: "Travel in the earth..."﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:20], meaning: we travel within it. The atmosphere surrounding the earth is part of the earth; without it life on it cannot be sustained. So when you travel, you travel in the earth: it is beneath you, and its atmosphere is above you, so you are, as it were, inside it.

The reason for travel is ﴿and see how He began creation...﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:20], and in another verse ﴿Then look...﴾ [al-An'am 6:11]. This is because travel from one land to another has two motives: either for tourism, contemplation and taking lessons, or for trade and investment, if one's livelihood is constricted in one's own country. So His words ﴿Travel in the earth and see...﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:20] mean: look with consideration and contemplation.

As for ﴿Then look...﴾ [al-An'am 6:11], the particle thumma (then) indicates sequence and delay: it is as if He, glory be to Him, is saying to us: travel in the earth for investment, then look with the gaze of contemplation and lesson-taking. There is no obstacle to combining the two purposes.

You will recall that the Truth, glory be to Him, said in the preceding surah (al-Qasas): ﴿Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an will surely return you to a place of return...﴾ [al-Qasas 28:85], and the meaning of that is the Hijra. In this surah comes: ﴿O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is vast, so worship Me alone﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:56].

The meaning is: if your livelihood is constricted in one place, seek it in another place; or: if the manifest signs before you are not sufficient to satisfy your desire for lesson and contemplation, then travel in the earth, for you will find in it many signs and lessons in the diversity of peoples, environments, fruits, climates, etc.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Was not the earth of Allah spacious so that you could emigrate therein?﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:97]

The earth, all of it, belongs to Allah; there are no boundaries in it and no dividing lines between it. But when people divided it and made for it borders that prevent movement within it, many problems arose, and it became difficult for people to travel for tourism or to seek livelihood if one's sustenance was constricted.

And here is Sudan beside us, with vast stretches of fertile land which, if cultivated, would meet the needs of the whole Arab world. Could we go to cultivate it? At that time they would say: "They have come to colonize us."

Therefore, when I had the opportunity to speak at the United Nations, I said: the present problems of the world cannot be solved unless we apply the principle of the Creator, glory and majesty be to Him, and return to His method which He laid down to organize our lives. And how do we place between us these iron borders and barbed wire, when our Lord says: ﴿And the earth He has set for the creatures﴾ [al-Rahman 55:10]?

So the whole earth is for all creatures(1), and on the day we realize this principle, sustenance will not be constricted for anyone, for if it is constricted for you here, you seek it there. Therefore most complaints in today's world are either from a land without people or from people without land. Why do we not bring about the complementarity which Allah willed in His creation?

So: travel here entails consideration, ﴿how He began creation, then Allah will bring about the last creation﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:20]. And since we have believed that Allah, exalted is He, is the Creator at the beginning, then re-creation is easier, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Were We then incapable with the first creation?﴾ [Qaf 50:15]. So would they doubt the final creation? Therefore the Creator, glory be to Him, affirms this power by His saying:

﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:20]

1. al-Anam: whatever appears upon the earth of all creation. The exegetes said: they are the jinn and humankind. [Lisan al-'Arab, root: a-n-m].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 29, verse 21:

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq) Almighty says:

{He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned.} [21]

Why did the Almighty begin here with mention of punishment, while in another verse He placed forgiveness first: ﴿He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills...﴾ [18] [Al-Ma'idah]?

They said: Because the discourse here concerns those who deny and turn away, and the disbelievers, so it was fitting to begin with them by mentioning punishment: ﴿He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills...﴾ [21] [Al-'Ankabut]. If you say: Why then does He mention mercy to the disbelievers after threatening them with punishment? We say: Because the Lord threatens His servants first with punishment so that they may refrain and believe, then He shows them His mercy, Glorified is He, to encourage them to obey Him and to draw their attention to belief in Him.

It is authentically reported in the Hadith Qudsi: "My mercy has preceded My wrath" (1). So at the same time He threatens with punishment, He shows His servants, even the disbelievers, that His mercy, exalted is He, has preceded His wrath.

His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿And to Him you will be returned [turned over]﴾ [21] [Al-'Ankabut]: that is, you will be returned. He used the form "tuqlabun" (you will be turned), which indicates compulsion and submission by force, to tell them: however far your transgression, arrogance and haughtiness toward the blessings of God may reach, you must return to Him and stand before Him. So reflect well on this matter, for there is no escape from it for you. Therefore it was fitting that He say after it:

{And you cannot escape Him in the earth or in the heaven, and you have no protector or helper besides God.} [22]

(1) On the authority of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When God created the creation, He wrote in a book which is with Him above the Throne: Indeed My mercy has overcome My wrath." Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3194, 7404, 7422), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (2751), Kitab al-Tawbah.

(Mu'jizin): the plural of mu'jiz, meaning one who prevents another from succeeding, from a'jaztu fulanan, "I made so-and-so unable." The meaning is that you will not escape from God, nor will you be able to resist Him when He wills to bring you to stand before Him; rather you will come humbled.

We notice here that the Exalted said: ﴿And you cannot escape [Him] in the earth or in the heaven.﴾ [al-'Ankabut 22], and He did not say, for example, "You will not make Me unable when I seek you," because negating an act is not the same as negating an attribute. When you say, for example, "You do not sew a garment for me," this means that he is able to sew a garment for you but does not want to; the capacity exists, but he lacks the willingness to carry out the act. However, when you say, "You are not a tailor [khayyat]," you have negated the very root of the matter.

Therefore He did not negate the act from them, lest we imagine that it could occur from them. Fleeing and escaping from meeting God in the Hereafter is simply not a possibility that comes to mind at all. Rather, He negated the attribute from its foundation: ﴿And you are not able to escape in the earth or in the heaven.﴾ [al-'Ankabut 22]

Then the Exalted says: ﴿And you have not, besides God, any protector or helper.﴾ [al-'Ankabut 22], lest someone say: "If they cannot escape, perhaps their protectors are those who can overpower God, or there are those behind them who intercede for them or defend them." So He negated these as well, for nothing overpowers Him, and nothing can frustrate Him.

Accordingly He addressed them with His words: ﴿What is [the matter] with you that you do not help one another?﴾ [al-Saffat 25]: where are the mighty champions who would help you?

He negated from them the protector (wali) and negated the helper (nasir), because there is a difference between them: the wali is one who draws near to you with affection and love, and he can help you, but by kindness and diplomacy, and he intercedes for you if you need his intercession; as for the nasir, he helps you by force and by (al-futuwwa, chivalrous strength).

Thus He negated from them the capacity to escape, and negated from them any protector and helper. But the mention of ﴿besides God﴾ [al-'Ankabut 22] means: it is possible that they could have a protector and helper from God, Exalted is He. So if they seek the true protector and the true helper, let them believe in Me, for I am their protector and I am their helper.

It is as if the Exalted is saying to them: if you repent and return from what you were in of disbelief, and apologize for what came from you, then I am your protector and I am your helper.

In another place He said: ﴿And you do not have any helpers [nasirin]﴾ [al-'Ankabut 25], and He did not say "besides God," because the situation is in the Hereafter, and in the Hereafter there is no repentance, no apology, and no return; so His words ﴿besides God﴾ [al-'Ankabut 22] apply only in this world.

{ And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and in His meeting – those have despaired of My mercy, and those will have a painful punishment. }

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

{ Those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and in His meeting – it is they who have despaired of My mercy, and for them is a painful punishment. }

So if the disbeliever persists in his disbelief and in his worship of idols, which neither benefit nor harm, and no admonition or reminder has reached him, then he has no refuge and no way out to the mercy of Allah; for he has worshipped protectors who cannot benefit him in anything, and he has disbelieved in Me. So there is none who can shield him from Me, nor any who can help him from the idols he worshipped. Thus there remains for him only despair.

Yaʾs (despair): the cutting off of hope regarding a matter. The disbelievers have cut off their own hope, because they worshipped what neither benefits nor harms, and they disbelieved in the One in whose hand is benefit and harm.

We have said: the intended meaning of "the signs of Allah" is either the cosmic signs which establish the power of Allah and draw attention to the wisdom of the Creator, may He be Mighty and Majestic, such as the night and the day, the sun and the moon; or the signs of miracles which accompany the messengers, so that Allah may confirm them thereby and manifest their truthfulness in conveying from Allah; and they disbelieved in the signs of the Qur'an, which carry the rulings.

These people disbelieved in all of these signs, and did not accept any of them as true. And since they disbelieved in these signs, and also disbelieved in meeting Allah in the Hereafter, the mercy of Allah is far from them, and they are despairing of it.

Therefore their end was: {And those – for them is a painful punishment.} [Al-ʿAnkabut]

The Almighty then says:

{So the answer of his people was only that they said, "Kill him or burn him." But Allah rescued him from the fire. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.} (29:24)

We were expecting from them a logical answer, after he (Abraham) had called them to worship Allah alone, without partner, and had shown them the falsehood of worshipping their idols, and that they neither harm nor benefit. They should have debated with him, defended their gods, and shown their proof for their worship.

Instead, their answer comes indicating their bankruptcy: ﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said, "Kill him or burn him..."﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 24]. Is this an answer to what was said to you? It is merely an escape from confrontation and bankruptcy in argument. It is the answer of one who has found no answer, who has nothing but threats and the brandishing of force and brutality. This is the language of one who has no proof.

But why did the Qur'an call it an "answer"? They said: because if they had not spoken these words, it would have been said of them that they had paid no attention to the words of their prophet and did not care for them, and that his speech had no weight and was not answered. So although their speech does not count as an answer, it takes the form of an answer, and though it is a corrupt answer, it is an answer.

As for their saying ﴿Kill him...﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 24]: we know that killing (qatl) is the destruction of the structure, in a way that is followed by the departure of the soul, because the soul finds no sound structure to inhabit. Death (mawt), however, is when the soul departs first, and then the structure is destroyed when it decomposes in the earth. Thus both are, in the end, the same in being destruction.

We have previously clarified this matter with the example of the electric bulb that gives light. Electricity does not exist in the bulb; it is in something outside it. But the effect of electricity appears in the bulb if it is intact and fit to receive the current. If you break it, no trace of electricity is found in it and it does not light; and electricity may be withheld from it while it is intact.

Then they said ﴿or burn him...﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 24]. Is burning after killing an escalation of punishment? There is no doubt that killing is more complete than burning, for a person may be burned and then rescued and treated and not die. Killing is a confirmation of death, whereas burning does not necessarily mean death. So why did they not just say "kill him" and the matter would end, or escalate the punishment by saying: "burn him or kill him"?

They began with the greatest punishment they had, because of their intense rage against him, saying ﴿Kill him...﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 24]. Then another opinion occurred to them: why not burn him with fire? Perhaps he will return and renounce his call when he feels the pain of burning, and this would count as a gain for them, and the round would be reckoned in favour of their side.

But who said ﴿Kill him...﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 24]? Who is the one commanding the killing, and who is the one commanded? They all agreed together on killing him, so the commander and the commanded are equal, and this is clear from the verse: ﴿So the answer of his people...﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 24]. The people as a whole colluded in this matter. Or the commanders are the chiefs and elders of the people whose orders the masses follow, while carrying out the task is the duty of the followers.

We see the outrage and agitation of the masses when a crime occurs, for example: everyone gets angry and says, "Kill him! Imprison him!" They are all speakers, and all are addressed.

Then He says ﴿But Allah rescued him from the fire...﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 24]. Here the philosophers object: how can this be, since fire by its nature burns? How can this law be violated? But how could it be a miracle if it did not come in this form?

Allah the Almighty created creation and placed in it laws that perform their function and carry out their task automatically. For example, when you plough the earth, cast seed in it, and then water it, the law is that it grows. And so that no one supposes that the universe proceeds according to these laws alone, and not by the power of Allah, we find that He, glory be to Him, breaks these laws to establish for us His sustaining over His creation and the absoluteness of His power over it.

Therefore, if there is no provision for you in this tilling, the plant does not grow, or it grows and then a blight or a whirlwind strikes it and destroys it before it reaches maturity. Thus the matter is the sustaining of Allah, exalted is He, and not "mechanics."

Allah broke the laws of the universe for Moses, peace be upon him, when he struck the sea, so that every part became like a mighty mountain, and the flowing water turned into solid rock. And He broke the laws of the universe for Abraham when He said to the fire: ﴿O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 69]

He breaks the laws to establish the miracle, and to establish that the hand of Allah the Almighty still controls His kingdom, not that He created the laws and left them to operate in the universe without any intervention from Him, as the philosophers say. Allah created the laws to act, but His sustaining and His power, exalted is He, render the laws ineffective.

﴿So Allah rescued him from the fire. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 24] We mention in the story of the ship that Allah, exalted is He, said of it: ﴿And We left it as a sign for the worlds.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 15] Here He said ﴿signs...﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 24], and there He said ﴿for the worlds﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 15], and here He said ﴿for a people who believe﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 24]. The difference between the two contexts is therefore in two matters:

In the ship's case He said ﴿a sign...﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 15], because the wonder of the ship's matter lies not in its construction, for whoever sees it could build its like; rather the sign in it is that Allah informed him of it before he needed it, and then He withheld from it the whirlwinds and storms that would toy with it and drown its passengers.

As for the matter of burning, there are many wonders and various signs. It would have been possible that they not be enabled to seize him, and it would have been possible, after they had seized him and thrown him into the fire, for Allah to send down rain that extinguishes their fire and saves Abraham, or to subject to him from among the people folk of compassion and mercy who would rescue him from being thrown into the fire.

But none of this happened; rather, Allah enabled them over him until they threw him into the fire while it was blazing, and he was bound with ropes, yet the fire did not harm him at all, and the signs appeared clear and manifest before the eyes of all.

The second matter: there He said ﴿for the worlds﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 15], because when the ship came to rest and its passengers were saved, the ship remained in its place, seen and contemplated by all people; it had a lasting, visible trace.

As for the matter of Abraham, peace be upon him, He said ﴿for a people who believe﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 24], because the rescue of Abraham, peace be upon him, was a lesson only for those who witnessed it. We believe in it because Allah informed us of it, and we are believers in Allah. So these are signs for those who believe in Allah, not for the worlds.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

{And he said, "You have only taken idols besides Allah as a means of affection among yourselves in the worldly life. Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will deny others and curse one another, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers."} (29:25)

The meaning: If you did not believe in the cosmic signs that demonstrate the power of Allah, and did not believe in the miracle you witnessed when my Lord saved me from the Fire, and it was incumbent upon you to believe that none can do that except Allah, then why do you persist in disbelief?

Certainly you disbelieved in Allah and worshipped idols, not because you were convinced of worshipping them, nor because they deserve to be worshipped, but you worshipped them ﴿as a means of affection among yourselves in the worldly life..﴾ (29:25), meaning: hypocrisy by which some of you feign to one another, and flattery; because you saw the leaders of the people among you worshipping them, so you imitated them without conviction in what you worship, or out of affection for your forefathers and following their way, as the Qur'an relates: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers following a religion, and indeed we are, upon their footsteps, guided.﴾ (43:23)

And in another verse: ﴿They said, "Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers."﴾ (5:104)

But this affection, this flattery, and this hypocrisy have their lifespan only in ( the worldly life ), and in the Hereafter your bonds of affection will be severed: ﴿Close friends, that Day, will be enemies to one another, except the righteous.﴾ (43:67), meaning: this affection and this flattery will turn into enmity, and even into a quarrel that the Qur'an relates: ﴿Our Lord, show us those who misled us from the jinn and mankind; we will put them under our feet so they will be among the lowest.﴾ (41:29)

And He said: ﴿When those who were followed disassociate themselves from those who followed, and they see the punishment, and their means of connection are cut off.﴾ (2:166)

Here too He affirms this truth: ﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will deny others and curse one another, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers.﴾ (29:25). This is because the premises that preceded it required that you believe, yet they did nothing but persist in disbelief.

At the time when the affection of the disbelievers turns into enmity, the enmity of the believers who cooperated in obedience turns into love and affection; so the believer says to his brother who led him to obedience and compelled him to it, despite his reluctance and discomfort: "May Allah reward you with good, for you have saved me."

The matter does not end with this punishment they inflict upon themselves through disavowal and cursing, but they proceed to a more severe punishment: ﴿and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers.﴾ (29:25). We note here that the Truth, glorified is He, did not say: "and you will have none besides Allah," because the discourse concerns the Hereafter, where there is no repentance or return for them, so it has been negated that they have any guardian or helper from Allah.

Likewise, they have no helper from their allies whom they worshipped besides Allah, since they seek help from stones and idols, which neither speak nor respond.

Thus this brief glimpse of the story of our master Ibrahim (peace be upon him) concludes. He has a long history; he is the shaykh of the messengers and the father of the prophets. If you wished to narrate his story, it would take a long time, and it suffices that Allah the Exalted said of him: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was a nation.﴾ (16:120)

(1) Al-Ummah: the man who combines all goodness; and the ummah: the man who is distinct in his religion, with no one sharing it with him. [Lisan al-Arab – root: a-m-m]

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

{So Lot believed him, and he said, "Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord. Indeed, He is the Almighty, the Wise." (26)}

That is: the people of Abraham, peace be upon him, remained in their disbelief. The one who believed in him was Lot, peace be upon him, who was his nephew (his brother's son). They were in Iraq, and afterwards they would move to al-Sham (the Levant).

As for the phrase ﴿So Lot believed him...(26)﴾ [al-'Ankabut]: when we trace the word āmana (آمن) in the Noble Qur'an, we find that it revolves around security, tranquility, comfort and calm, but its meanings differ according to its grammatical position (i'rab). Here, ﴿So Lot believed him...(26)﴾ [al-'Ankabut]: did Lot believe Abraham? We say "he believes in God" (yu'minu bi-llah), and since the context is ﴿So Lot believed him...(26)﴾ [al-'Ankabut], the meaning must be different, and it does not mean faith in God here.

The meaning of (āmana) here is as in His saying about Quraysh: ﴿And He gave them security from fear (4)﴾ [Quraysh]. Here the verb is transitive: the one who gave security is God, who secured Quraysh from fear. Likewise in His saying: ﴿Shall I trust you with him... (64)﴾ [Yusuf]. The meaning of ﴿So Lot believed him...(26)﴾ [al-'Ankabut] is: he affirmed him (ṣaddaqahu).

From it is His saying: ﴿And you will not be believed by us even if we were truthful (17)﴾ [Yusuf], meaning: you will not be one who is believed (musaddiq). As for "āmantu billah" (I believed in God), it means: you hold that He exists with absolute perfect attributes.

Lot would not affirm Abraham unless he was a believer in a God who had sent him; so it is as if he believed in God and then affirmed him regarding what he brought. The story of Lot, peace be upon him, has another place where it is explained in detail; his mention here is only because he is the outcome of the dialectical and combative exchange between Abraham and his people. After he called them to God, none believed in him except Lot, his nephew.

I recall that Sheikh Musa, may Allah have mercy on him, who taught us tafsir, came to the story of Lot, peace be upon him, and I said to him: "Why do we attribute the vice of the people of Lot to him, saying lūṭī (لوطي)? Lot came only to fight this vice and eliminate it."

The Sheikh said: "Then what shall we say of it?" I said: "The Arabic language is wide in derivation. For example, when forming the relative adjective from ʿAbd al-Ashhal they said Ashhalī; for ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz they said ʿAbdizī; for Bukhtanaṣr they said Bukhtī. And now we say, in the relative form of Dār al-ʿUlūm, Dar'amī, etc. So why not follow this method? Take the open qāf and the sukūn wāw from qawm, take the ṭā' from Lūṭ, then the relative yā', and say (qawṭī), and spare the Prophet of God, Lot, peace be upon him, from being attributed to what is not fitting for him to be attributed to."

I once attended a ceremony honouring Ṭāhā Ḥusayn, and among what was said in his honour was: "You have in knowledge a principle, Ṭaḥsanī" (لك في العلم مبدأ طحسني), because among scholars one often finds the names Ṭāhā and Ḥusayn together.

So His saying ﴿So Lot believed him...(26)﴾ [al-'Ankabut] is a parenthetical sentence within the story of Abraham, peace be upon him, because it is the final result of Abraham's call to his people. Therefore the context returns again to Abraham: ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord..(26)"﴾ [al-'Ankabut], that is: turning away from this place, because it was not suitable for the establishment of the call.

The root h-j-r and what derives from it indicate leaving one thing for another, but hajara means that the cause of the leaving is from you and by your own desire; hājara in it is the form of mufā'ala, like sharaka and qātala. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not "hajara" Makkah; rather, he emigrated (hājara) from it to Madinah.

This means that he did not emigrate by his own desire; rather, his people harmed him and compelled him to leave his land. So they have a share in the emigration, and they are a second party in it.

Therefore al-Mutanabbi says:
"When you depart from a people who have decided that you must never leave them, it is the departing ones who are they."

And from the precision of the Qur'anic expression in this matter: the Prophet's move from Makkah to Madinah is called hijrah from the triliteral root, and not muhājarah, because at the moment one emigrates one dislikes the place one has left. But here, with the verb, he said hājara, and with the noun he said hijrah, and did not say muhājarah.

We have previously mentioned that the first emigration of the believers to Abyssinia was an emigration to a land of security only, not a land of faith, because the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he directed them specifically to Abyssinia, said: "Because in it is a king under whom no one is wronged" (2).

It is as if the map of the whole earth was spread before him, and he chose this region from it, because it had become clear to him that it was a land of security for those of his companions who believed. As for emigration to Madinah, it was an emigration to a land of faith, as evidenced by what we saw of the stance of the Helpers towards the emigrants.

Here Abraham, peace be upon him, says: ﴿Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord..(26)﴾ [al-'Ankabut]. So the place is not his intended goal; rather, the direction of my Lord is what is intended. Otherwise you might say: how can you emigrate to your Lord, when your Lord is in every place, here and there?

So the meaning is: I emigrate in compliance with the command of my Lord and head toward a direction He commands, because it is possible for you to move from one place to another by the command of your superior, for example; and you may have had a desire to move to this place, so you welcome the matter because it fulfils a desire in yourself. You, then, do not go because of an order issued to you, but because of a desire you have.

Therefore a hadith says: "Whoever's emigration was to Allah and His Messenger, his emigration is to Allah and His Messenger; and whoever's emigration was for worldly gain that he might obtain, or a woman he might marry, his emigration is to what he emigrated for" (3).

So the meaning of ﴿Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord..(26)﴾ [al-'Ankabut] is: the move is not according to my own will and whim, but according to the direction into which my Lord directs me. I recall that this matter had a reality in our own history: we were a group of seventy men, and something was done by us that did not suit our leader, so he issued a decision to transfer us all and scatter us from our places. When it came to implementation we went to him, pleading, perhaps he would reconsider his decision, but he insisted on it and said: "How can I be a leader if I cannot enforce my command over those under me?"

One of us, who was bold, said to him: "We will go wherever you wish, but know that you will not take us to a place where God is not."

This was the true word that struck the man and restored his right judgment; truth has its sway, and indeed matters went as we wanted, and the leader withdrew from his decision.

So the meaning of ﴿emigrating to my Lord..(26)﴾ [al-'Ankabut] is that my Lord is the one who directs me, and He, glorified is He, is in every place. What confirms this is His saying: ﴿Wherever you turn, there is the Face of God..(115)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. It is as if Allah, glorified is He, is saying to us: know that I only directed you in your prayer toward the Ka'bah to affirm this meaning, because you face it from wherever you are, and from whatever direction you come, wherever you turn, that is your qiblah.

Then He says: ﴿Indeed, He is the Almighty, the Wise (26)﴾ [al-'Ankabut]. The Friend, Abraham, peace be upon him, chose from the attributes of his Lord ﴿the Almighty..(26)﴾ [al-'Ankabut], that is, the One who is not overcome, while He overcomes. This attribute suits the attempt to burn him, as if he were saying to the people: "I am going to the embrace of One who is never overcome."

And ﴿the Wise (26)﴾ [al-'Ankabut], that is, in His dispositions; so He will surely transfer me to a place that suits my call, and to people who deserve this call, through what they have of listening ears open to the truth, and hearts and minds longing for it, awaiting the word of truth from which you have turned away.

1 Found in Lisan al-'Arab, entry l-w-ṭ: "Lāṭa al-rajul lawṭan and lāwaṭa, meaning he did the deed of the people of Lot. Al-Layth said: Lot was a prophet whom God sent to his people, and they denied him and did what they did; so people derived from his name a verb for one who does the deed of his people."

2 From Umm Salamah, who said: "When Makkah became too strait for us, and the companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, were harmed and tried, and they saw what afflicted them of trial and tribulation in their religion, and that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, could not repel that from them, and he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was under the protection of his people and his uncle, so nothing reached him of what they disliked which reached his companions, he said to them, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: 'In the land of Abyssinia there is a king under whom no one is wronged; so join his country until Allah makes for you a relief and a way out of what you are in.'" A long hadith, narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (2/301), and mentioned by Ibn Hisham in al-Sirah in similar form (1/321).

3 A hadith agreed upon (Muttafaq 'alayh). Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (1), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (1907), from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, beginning: "Actions are only by intentions, and every person shall have only what he intended."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 29, verse 27:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

{And We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and We placed in his offspring prophethood and the Scripture, and We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed he is in the Hereafter among the righteous.}

The time of recompense came, so that Ibrahim, peace be upon him, might receive from his Lord the reward for his patience under trial and his steadfastness in faith. Did he not say to Jibril, when Jibril came to him as he was on his way to the Fire, offering him assistance: "O Ibrahim, do you have any need?" Ibrahim said: "As for you, no" (1). Therefore his Lord rewarded him, breaking for him the laws (nawamis), and favoured him with blessings and bounties, until He praised him, glorified is He, saying: {Indeed, Ibrahim was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah...} [al-Nahl: 120].

He, peace be upon him, was an obscure man among his people, as is shown by their saying about him when he smashed their idols: {They said: "We heard a young man mention them, called Ibrahim."} [al-Anbiya': 60]. So he was not famous among them, his mention was neglected, and no one knew him. But when he submitted to Allah and Allah befriended him, He said: "I will make you a friend of Allah (khalil Allah) and the chief of the messengers, and I will make your remembrance endure, after you were obscure on every tongue." And here we are, mentioning him, peace be upon him, in the tashahhud in every prayer.

Read Ibrahim's supplication to his Lord to confirm this meaning: {And make for me a tongue of truthfulness among the later generations} [al-Shu'ara': 84]. It is as if he is saying: "O Lord, my people belittle me, so make for me a remembrance with You."

It is known that procreation and multiplication have their laws. When Hajar, the lady, bore Isma'il, peace be upon him, the free woman Sarah became angry: how can Hajar bear, being a slave-woman, and be preferred over her? But how is there a way to bearing children when her age was ninety years and Ibrahim's age at that time was a hundred?

The law of nature and the laws of creation say there is no childbearing at this age. But I will break the law for you and make you bear a gift from Me: {And We gave him Isaac...} [al-'Ankabut: 27], then {and Jacob...} [al-'Ankabut: 27].

In another verse He said: {And Jacob as an additional gift} [al-Anbiya': 72].

That is: an addition, because he had patiently accepted the sacrifice of Isma'il, and his Lord said to him: "Raise your hand, you have fulfilled what was upon you and succeeded in the test. I will ransom him for you, and moreover I will give you a brother for him, and I will give you from his offspring Jacob."

And I will make them, beyond that, messengers: {And We placed in his offspring prophethood and the Scripture...} [al-'Ankabut: 27]. Therefore, when we survey the procession of the prophets, we find that most of them are from the offspring of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, every one who came after him from his offspring (4).

The offspring mentioned here is intended to refer to Isaac and Jacob, who were the two gifts from Sarah. As for Isma'il, he came by the general natural law in which Ibrahim and others share.

It is as if the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, in this matter, demonstrates the all-encompassing power through causes in which the power of the Causer appears. He says to Ibrahim: even if your people have disbelieved in you and not believed, I will give you offspring who are not only guided but guiding to all people.

If the offspring of Isaac and Jacob took four thousand years of the procession of prophethood, then from the offspring of Isma'il came the Seal of the Prophets and the Imam of the God-fearing, Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. His message will remain enduring and eternal until the Day of Resurrection. The messengers from the offspring of Isaac were scattered among the nations and had specific times, whereas the message of Muhammad is general for all time and all place; there is no successor to him with a messenger after him until the Day of Resurrection.

His, the Exalted's, saying: {and the Scripture} [al-'Ankabut: 27] means: the books that were revealed to the prophets from his offspring, namely: the Qur'an, the Gospel, the Torah and the Psalms.

Then He, glorified is He, says: {And We gave him his reward in this world} [al-'Ankabut: 27]. They said: he was obscure in renown, then his affair became prominent and his mention rose; he was poor, then Allah enriched him, so much so that those who narrate about him in the biographies say he owned so much livestock that a person would tire of counting them, and he had twelve guard dogs... etc. This is his reward in this world only (5).

{And indeed he is in the Hereafter among the righteous} [al-'Ankabut: 27]. That is: We will not say to him "you have used up your good things in your worldly life"; rather, he is in the Hereafter among the righteous, and this is the wish of the prophets. So his reward has not been diminished from his reward in the Hereafter.

But why did Allah describe His prophet Ibrahim in the Hereafter as among the righteous? They said: because three statements are attributed to Ibrahim, which those who hunt for errors call three lies or sins: the first is his saying to the king of Egypt when he asked him about Sarah: "She is my sister." The second is when he said to his people when they invited him to go out with them to their festival: "Indeed, I am sick" (6). The third is his saying: {Rather, this was done by their chief, so ask them, if they can speak} [al-Anbiya': 63], that is, when he smashed the idols.

Those hunters of errors say: these are statements contrary to the infallibility of the prophets. But what is your view if the Lord of the affair and the judgement bore witness to his righteousness in the Hereafter?

Furthermore, one who reflects on these statements will find them to be of the kind of ma'arid (indirect expressions) about which the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Indeed, in indirect expressions there is a substitute for lying" (7). So his saying about Sarah, "she is my sister," is indeed his sister in faith; and perhaps had he said "my wife," the king would have killed him so that he himself might marry her.

As for his saying {I am sick} [al-Saffat: 89], it is an excuse to avoid a scene of disbelief which the believer should not attend. Also, sickness may be of the body, and may be of the heart, so it is plausible that his intention was sickness of the heart due to the disbelief of the people that he saw.

As for his saying {Rather, this was done by their chief} [al-Anbiya': 63], he intended by it to show the proof and establish the evidence of the invalidity of worshipping idols; he wanted to make them themselves speak what he wanted to say, so as to make them acknowledge that they are idols which neither harm nor benefit nor move.

1. Ibn Jarir reported from Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman al-Taymi, from some of his companions, who said: Jibril came to Ibrahim while he was bound to be cast into the Fire, and said: "O Ibrahim, do you have any need?" He said: "As for you, no." [Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 5/641].
2. Qunut: obedience and supplication. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/134]. Ibn Sayyida said: the qanit is one who stands in carrying out all of Allah's commands. Ibn Manzur said: qunut is humility and acknowledgement of servanthood and standing in obedience with which there is no disobedience [Lisan al-'Arab, root q-n-t].
3. The Torah mentions this: "Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, mocking. So she said to Abraham: Drive out this slave-woman and her son, for the son of this slave-woman shall not inherit with my son Isaac. The matter was very grievous in Abraham's eyes because of his son. But God said to Abraham: Do not let it be grievous in your eyes because of the lad or because of your slave-woman. Whatever Sarah says to you, listen to her voice, for through Isaac shall your offspring be called. And the son of the slave-woman also I will make a nation, because he is your offspring." [Genesis 21:9-13].
4. Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/5229): "Allah did not send any prophet after Ibrahim except from his loins, and He made the Scripture singular, because He intended the verbal noun, like prophethood; and the intended meaning is the Torah, the Gospel and the Furqan, so it is an expression of the plural. The Torah was revealed to Musa from the descendants of Ibrahim, the Gospel to 'Isa from his descendants, and the Furqan to Muhammad from his descendants, peace and blessings be upon him."
5. Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (3/411) something close to this without detail, saying: "He had in this world wide and pleasant provision, a spacious dwelling, a sweet watering place, a good righteous wife, a beautiful praise, a good remembrance, and everyone loves him and takes him as ally." As for al-Qurtubi, he said in his tafsir (7/5229): "That is: the gathering of the people of the religions upon him; said by 'Ikrimah." Ibn 'Abbas said: "Allah is pleased with the people of the religions with His religion, so there is no people of a religion except that they take Ibrahim as ally and are pleased with him." In another report from him: "the righteous child and praise." Both are mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/459).
6. Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Zayd ibn Aslam, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: their king sent to him, saying: "Tomorrow is our festival, so go out." He looked at a star and said: "Indeed this star has never risen except with a sickness for me." So they turned away from him, retreating. [al-Durr al-Manthur fi al-Tafsir bi al-Ma'thur 7/100].
7. Reported by Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil fi Du'afa' al-Rijal (3/96) from the hadith of 'Imran ibn Husayn, in which is Dawud ibn al-Zabriqan. al-Bukhari said: "close to the hadith." al-Nasa'i said: "not trustworthy." Ibn 'Adi said: he is among the weak narrators whose hadith is written.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:
