{And Lot, when he said to his people: "Indeed you commit an abomination that no one in the worlds has preceded you in."}

Here the context shifts from the story of Abraham to the story of his nephew Lot. We note that in speaking of Noah, Abraham and Lot, the Qur'an mentions the prophet first. The Qur'an's usual practice, when speaking of the messengers, is to mention the people first, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And to 'Ad their brother Hud...﴾ [al-A'raf], ﴿And to Thamud their brother Salih...﴾ [al-A'raf], ﴿And to Madyan their brother Shu'ayb...﴾ [al-A'raf].

They said: because the people of Noah, the people of Abraham and the people of Lot had no well-known name, their prophets are mentioned first. As for 'Ad, Thamud and Madyan, they are names of well-known peoples who had known towns, so the principle is that the people are the intended recipients of the message and guidance; therefore they are mentioned first, for they are the origin of the message. As for the messenger, the message is not a function that Allah assigns to one of the people.

﴿And Lot, when he said to his people: "Indeed you commit an abomination that no one in the worlds has preceded you in."﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:28] He called the vileness of his people's deed "fahisha" (abomination). Therefore the scholars said regarding its punishment: whatever punishment applies to fornication applies to it, because Allah the Exalted called adultery "fahisha," saying ﴿Indeed, it was an abomination...﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:22], and stoning was prescribed for adultery; similarly, the penalty for one who commits the deed of the people of Lot is stoning.

And His saying ﴿that no one in the worlds has preceded you in﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:28] does not mean that no one had committed it before them; rather, if it is committed, it is an individual act, not a widespread plague as it was with these people.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 29, verse 29:

His saying: ﴿Indeed, you approach men...﴾ [al-Ankabut 29] is an indication of the deviation of the sexual instinct among them. God placed the sexual instinct in man for the preservation of the species, so its wisdom is procreation, and procreation can only occur between a male and a female, where the female receives the male sperm, which is embraced by the female ovum, adheres to the wall of the womb, and forms the embryo. Therefore God Most High called the woman a tilth (harth), because she is the place of cultivation, and He made it a condition for approaching women that it be in the place of cultivation.

Therefore, those groups who called for legislation for women permitting a man to approach her however he wishes, argued with His saying Most High: ﴿Your women are a tilth for you, so approach your tilth as you wish...﴾ [al-Baqarah 223]

We say to these: you have erred in understanding the verse. The tilth is the crop cultivated from the earth, so the meaning of ﴿as you wish﴾ [al-Baqarah 223] is that they are a tilth. Thus their argument is false, and its falsehood comes from their failure to understand the meaning of tilth. Accordingly, the meaning is: approach them in whatever manner you like, on condition that it be in the place of the tilth.

For the wisdom of the Truth, glorified be He, linking the preservation of the species to the sexual instinct, and giving it a pleasure and enjoyment exceeding any other pleasure in life: for example, you see a beautiful sight and your eye is delighted by it, and you hear a sweet sound and your ear is made happy by it... and so on. Every channel of perception you have has things that gratify it.

But by which of these senses do you perceive sexual pleasure? And which faculty of yours is gratified by it? All the senses and all the faculties enjoy it. Therefore a person cannot resist it, to the point that they said: it is the only moment in which a person can become heedless of his Lord; therefore He commanded us after it to perform ghusl (ritual washing).

Had the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, not linked the matter of the preservation of the species to this pleasure, many people would have renounced it, because of its consequences, responsibilities and problems, which are unavoidable in raising children.

We have previously mentioned the saying: "Permissibility (al-halal) cuts off the nose of jealousy (al-ghayrah)." A man becomes jealous over his daughter, for example, and does not accept even the mere gaze of strangers upon her, and becomes enraged if anyone approaches her. But when a young man comes knocking at his door to propose to his daughter, he welcomes him, and the people of the house receive him with zaghareed (ululation) and with open arms, they serve sherbet and set up decorations. So what is the difference between the two states? In the first, his blood was boiling; now, the words of God in the marriage contract descend upon his heart as coolness and peace.

As for the baseness of the people of Lot, ﴿Indeed, you approach men...﴾ [al-Ankabut 29], it is a deviation from the sound natural disposition, with no preservation of the species in it, and similar to it is approaching a woman in a place other than the place of tilth.

His saying Most High: ﴿and cut off the road...﴾ [al-Ankabut 29], means: you cut off the road of the preservation of the species. For adultery, even if it produces a child, does not secure for him a noble and honorable existence in society. Therefore the Truth, glorified be He, made for the preservation of the species one single path, so do not take any other path, neither with a man nor with a woman.

The word sabil (road) is an absolute term meaning the way, whether it is the physical road, i.e., the street we walk in, or the immaterial, which is the manner we follow, such as His saying Most High: ﴿Say: This is my way...﴾ [Yusuf 108], i.e., my path and my method. Therefore the moral path is one, so that we do not clash or quarrel in the movement of moral life; whereas the physical path is many, so that we do not crowd one another in the movement of material life.

The physical road along which we travel is a mark of the civilization of any nation. We recall that Hitler, before he entered the war in 1939, made his whole concern the building of a network of roads, because the unusual movement of war requires additional roads in wartime. Among them, for example, is the road they call the Treaty Road, that is, the treaty of 1936.

So, whenever there is additional movement, it requires additional roads, and these roads are proportionate to the place in which they are made. Roads in cities we call streets (shawari'), and in open country we call them roads; they are proportionate to the space within buildings, from which the alleys (haarat) branch off, which are smaller, and from the alley branch the lanes (atfah), which are smaller than the alley. Whenever countries become crowded, people resort to expanding the system of movement to facilitate the interests of the people.

As we see in Cairo, for example, tunnels and bridges, so that movement is not obstructed and so that flow is provided for the people.

Tunnels are more suitable for beauty in cities, and bridges are more beautiful in open spaces, where with the height of the bridges you see wider horizons and more beautiful views. But if the opposite happens, and bridges are built inside the streets, they diminish the beauty of the place, turn the street into something resembling a workshop hall, and also harm the residents of the buildings adjacent to them.

The state must take these matters into account when planning. Have we not read His saying Most High: ﴿Then the road He has made easy﴾ [Abasa 20]? We must make the roads easy for those who travel, because people's livelihoods and movement depend on movement along these roads.

As for His saying: ﴿and cut off the road...﴾ [al-Ankabut 29], among the people of Lot there were highway robbers like those who attack people during their journeys and movements, taking their wealth and plundering what they have, and if they resist, they kill them. And after they cut off the road to people, they cut off the road to the preservation of the species.(1)

He says about them: ﴿and commit the evil in your gatherings﴾ [al-Ankabut 29]. They did not refrain from doing what is ugly or saying it. They would sit in the roads mocking passersby and harming them, like those who now sit at cafés and loiter in the streets, harming God's creation, and openly declaring ugliness in speech and deed; no one escaped their harm.

Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) taught us the etiquette of the road, when he said to one who asked him:

"What is the right of the road, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Lowering the gaze, removing harm, and returning the greeting."(2)

Bad character spread among the people of Lot, to the extent that none of them forbade another, as He, glorified be He, said about the Jews, that they: ﴿used not to forbid one another from wrongdoing they committed﴾ [al-Ma'idah 79].

Al-nadi (the gathering place): a place where people assemble, and from it His saying: ﴿then let him call his council﴾ [al-'Alaq 17], i.e., the place where the leaders and elders of the people gather, as we now see: "the club of so-and-so" and "the club of so-and-so." The public place, which is the al-nadi, is the final stage of the discipline of conduct that must prevail in society. For example, you have a room in your house that is especially yours, and in it you have a particular discipline for yourself; likewise in the living room of the house you have a wider discipline, and in the street you have a wider discipline still.

Discipline is proportionate to the reality you live in; when you are, for example, among people who do not know you, your discipline is not at the same degree you maintain among those you know, like an employee in his office or a student in his school.

So these people cut off the road of the preservation of the species, as they came to what is not to be approached and deviated from the sound nature, and they cut off the physical road, frightening people, terrifying them, plundering their wealth, and seizing them from the road for the sake of this abominable deed. Then they would boast of these acts and openly declare them in their clubs and gathering places.

So how did his people answer him?

﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said: Bring us the punishment of God, if you are among the truthful﴾ [al-Ankabut 29], i.e., among the truthful in that you are a messenger from God. "We are among the disobedient; show us the punishment with which you threaten us." Their saying ﴿Bring us the punishment of God...﴾ [al-Ankabut 29], although punishment is a painful thing, and no one asks to inflict pain upon himself, is evidence of their failure to understand this speech, and that they were not certain of its truthfulness; otherwise, had they trusted its truthfulness, they would not have asked for punishment.

In another place, the Qur'an relates of them: ﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said: Expel the family of Lot from your town; indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾ [al-Naml 56].

So two positions and two answers occurred from them: the first is ﴿Bring us the punishment of God...﴾ [al-Ankabut 29]. When he did not comply with this foolish request, and continued his call to them, not despairing of them, they resorted to another stratagem, and said ﴿Expel the family of Lot from your town...﴾ [al-Naml 56]. The reason given is ﴿indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾ [al-Naml 56], because purity in the view of these people is a defect, and uprightness is a crime; this is evidence of the corruption of their minds and the corruption of their reasoning in judgment.

(1) Three opinions have been given on the meaning of ﴿and cut off the road...﴾ [al-Ankabut 29]:
They were highway robbers; said by Ibn Zayd.
They would seize people from the roads to commit the foul deed; related by Ibn Shajarah.
It means cutting off offspring by turning away from women to men; said by Wahb ibn Munabbih, i.e., they dispensed with women by means of men.
Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/5230), after mentioning these opinions: "Perhaps all of them were present among them, so they would cut off the road to seize wealth and for fornication, and would dispense with women thereby."

(2) A hadith agreed upon (Muttafaq 'alayh), related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2465), (6229), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (2121), Kitab al-Salam, and Ahmad in his Musnad (3/36, 47), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may God be pleased with him).

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿He said, "My Lord, support me against the corrupting people."﴾ [29:30]

And there is a difference between one who is corrupt in himself and one who corrupts others. Would that they were merely corrupt in themselves! Rather, they were corrupt and corrupting, whose corruption extends to others.

Al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 29, verse 31:

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) appears here in the context of the story of Lut, just as Lut appears in the context of the story of Ibrahim. The meaning of ﴿our messengers﴾ [al-Ankabut: 31] is: from among the angels, because Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind﴾ [al-Hajj: 75].

The angels came to Ibrahim with good news, and the content of the good news is not mentioned here. It is the good news of Ishaq, Ya'qub, and righteous offspring from them. They also came to him with a warning that Allah would destroy the people of this town. Good news and warning bring about balance: we give Ibrahim righteous offspring who will be a benefit in the universe, and we destroy the people of the town who deviated from the method of Allah.

You notice in the verse that it does not mention the reason for the good news. It does not say "because he was a believer, a striver, and just." Rather, it mentions the reason for destroying the people of the town: ﴿Indeed, its people were wrongdoers﴾ [al-Ankabut: 31]. Why? Because the one who bestows a favour does not remind of his favour as if it were a payment for work, but the one who punishes states the cause of the punishment.

So what was Ibrahim's first reaction, peace be upon him, when he heard the good news and the warning? He did not ask about the good news, although he was eager for it. What occupied him was the matter of the destruction of the town, in which was his nephew Lut. Therefore he said:

{He said: "Indeed, in it is Lut." They said: "We are most knowing of who is in it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife(1); she was of those who remain behind." }

1 Al-Dahhak said: her name was Hayshfa'. And she was turned into a stone. Al-Dahhak said this, as transmitted by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari. [Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 7/120].

Ibrahim did not look eagerly for the glad tidings; rather, he became concerned with the matter of destroying the town of Lut's people, because Lut was in it. This shows that a person's concern for good for himself does not distract him from evil befalling others. Here the angels replied: ﴿Indeed, We are most knowing of who is in it﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:32]. This is a matter that is not hidden from us.

Then they reassure him concerning his nephew: ﴿We will surely save him and his family﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:32]. "His family" (ahl) includes all of his relatives; therefore they made an exception from them: ﴿except his wife; she was of those who remain behind﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:32].

Al-ghabirun (الغابرون) is the plural of ghabir, and the word has two uses in the language. We say: al-zaman al-ghabir, meaning the past time; and ghabir also means remaining, staying. So the word carries the meaning and its opposite. This is because they came to destroy this town, and Lut's wife remained to be destroyed along with them, and she goes the way of those who will be destroyed; so she is remaining in the punishment. Thus the word ﴿of those who remain behind﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:32] came to express both of these meanings.

The Almighty then says:

{And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed on their account and felt powerless to protect them. They said, "Do not fear, nor grieve. We will save you and your family, except your wife, who will be among those who remain behind."} [29:33]

Al-Sha'rawi witnessed this scene with Abraham and with Lot, and he knew the reason for their coming to him. But why was he distressed on their account, given that they were messengers of God, angels who came to him in the most beautiful form? They said: because the angel comes in the most beautiful form; so when we want to praise someone for beauty we say: "like an angel." Among this is the saying of the women to the wife of the Al-Aziz about Joseph, peace be upon him: ﴿This is no mortal; this is none but a noble angel﴾ [12:31].

So when Lot saw them in this form, he feared for them, instead of rejoicing at their beautiful appearance, because his people were a people of evil, people of vice, and they would surely harm his guests. Therefore ﴿he was distressed on their account﴾ [29:33], meaning: evil befell him because of them. ﴿And felt powerless to protect them﴾ [29:33]. The dhar' (ذرع) is the length of the forearms; we say, "So-and-so's reach is long," meaning he obtains things easily, because his hand is long. So the meaning of "felt powerless" is: his effort was not sufficient to protect them from the people.

We note here the difference in context between the two verses: ﴿And when Our messengers came to Abraham...﴾ [29:31]. But in the case of Lot it says: ﴿And when Our messengers came to Lot...﴾ [29:33], because they had delayed somewhat at Abraham's place, peace be upon him.

So when evil befell him at their sight, instead of being made happy by them, and he feared for them, they reassured him: ﴿Do not fear, nor grieve. We will save you and your family, except your wife, who will be among those who remain behind﴾ [29:33]. Do not fear for us from these vile people; we are not mortals, we are angels, and we have come only to relieve you of them and to cut off the roots of this wicked deed. We will save you and your family from the punishment descending upon them.

Then they make an exception from his family: ﴿except your wife﴾ [29:33], for she often troubled him, disclosed his secrets, and directed the people to his guests, ﴿who will be among those who remain behind﴾ [29:33], those left behind in the punishment.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 29, verse 34:

But, what means will you use to overcome these people?

{ Indeed, We will send down upon the people of this town(1) a punishment (rijz) from the sky because of their defiance. }

Al-rijz: the punishment that descends upon them from the sky, and the stones with which Allah rains down upon them. ﴿Because of their defiance﴾, i.e., because of their wickedness and their departure from the way of Allah.

1 This town is Sodom, the town of the people of Lot, on the road between Madinah and Syria. Narrated by ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim from Qatadah. [Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 7/120].

Because this punishment uprooted them, brought their end, and made them a lesson for every thoughtful person who reflects, and a sign in the world for every passerby, as Allah the Glorified said: ﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning﴾ [As-Saffat 37:137]. So the lesson remains with the people of Sodom whenever people pass by their settlements.

That is why Allah said of it: ﴿a clear sign..﴾ [Al-Ankabut 29:35]. The āyah: the wondrous thing that calls for reflection. ﴿clear..﴾ [Al-Ankabut 29:35], evident like a lasting proof, and manifest so that it is hidden from no one. ﴿for a people who use their reason﴾ [Al-Ankabut 29:35], meaning: they investigate and reflect because of what befell these settlements and the punishment of Allah that descended upon them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 29, verse 36:

Then the Truthful One, glory be to Him, says:

{And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb, and he said: "O my people, worship Allah and hope for the Last Day, and do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief."}

Madyan: a name of one of the sons of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and the tribe was named after him, because they were accustomed to name a people after its most prominent person. The name passed from the person to the tribe, and then to the place, as evidenced by His saying, exalted is He, in another passage: {And when he arrived at the water of Madyan…} [al-Qasas 28:23]. So Madyan became a proper name for the territory, and it was said that it extends from al-Tur to the Euphrates.(1)

This is a concise account of the story of Madyan and their brother Shu'ayb, which is also mentioned in the story of Musa (peace be upon him). His saying {their brother} [al-'Ankabut 29:36] tells you that when Allah chooses someone for prophethood, He chooses one who has goodwill among the people, who is known to them with respect to his character and conduct, and whom they have tested before. Thus he is, in their eyes, a reformer and not a corrupter, so that when he conveys to them what is from Allah they believe him, and he has preliminaries that make the path of guidance easy for him.

His saying {So he said: "O my people, worship Allah…"} [al-'Ankabut 29:36]. The word {O my people} [al-'Ankabut 29:36]: "qawm" (people) is said only of men, because they are the ones who take charge of important matters and bear hardships. Therefore He, exalted is He, says: {O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule a people; perhaps they may be better than them, nor let women ridicule women; perhaps they may be better than them…} [al-Hujurat 49:11]. Here "qawm" is used for men as opposed to women.

And worship ('ibadah): we have said it is obedience to command and prohibition. {Worship Allah…} [al-'Ankabut 29:36] means: obey Him in what He commands, and refrain from what He forbids, since you have believed in Him as God and Creator. It is necessary that you listen to His words concerning what He advises you, in the form of directives: "do" and "do not."

You know that He, glory be to Him, with the attributes of perfection, brought you into existence and brought things into existence for you. So by worshipping Him you add no new attribute to Him: He is God before you existed, and Creator in perfect power before you existed, and He created the universe for you before you existed.

Then, after that, you disobey Him and disbelieve in Him, yet He does not deprive you of His goodness nor withhold His blessings from you. Therefore, He, glory be to Him, deserves worship and obedience from you, because His obedience returns to your own benefit.

For this reason we have previously said that the word "servitude" ('ubudiyyah) is a reprehensible word from which the soul recoils, if it is servitude to human beings, because in human servitude to humans the master takes the good of his servant; but in the servitude of human beings to Allah, the servant takes the good of his Master. Servitude to Allah is glory, strength and protection, while servitude to humans is humiliation and disgrace. Therefore we see that all reformers fight servitude to human beings and call slaves to liberation.

So the first thing Shu'ayb commanded his people was {worship Allah…} [al-'Ankabut 29:36]. Likewise Ibrahim said to his people {Worship Allah and fear Him…} [al-'Ankabut 29:16], but Lut (peace be upon him) did not command his people to worship Allah; rather he was concerned with the matter of the abomination that had spread among them, although all the messengers came to command the worship of Allah.

We say concerning this matter: Lut did not command his people to worship Allah because he was of the followers of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and a believer in his religion, as evidenced by His saying {So Lut believed him…} [al-'Ankabut 29:26]. He was thus a follower of his, and so he implemented the teachings that Ibrahim brought. He did not command worship because Ibrahim had commanded the people to it, but he undertook another matter, and Allah singled him out with a new task: to bring his people out of practising the abomination that had spread among them.

His saying, exalted is He: {And hope for the Last Day…} [al-'Ankabut 29:36]. The Last Day must not have been in their minds, and they did not reckon with it, as if they would escape from Allah and would never return to Him. Therefore he reminds them of this day and urges them to act for its sake.

And how should we not reckon with the Last Day, when in this world we treat ourselves by the same logic as the Last Day? For example, you toil and labour in cultivating the land, bearing the hardships of ploughing, sowing and irrigating, etc., throughout the year. But when you gather your crop on the day of harvest, and on the day you fill your storehouses with it, you forget the days of toil and hardship. At that time the idle one who sat back from work and striving will regret, for on the day of harvest you will see that the ardabb of wheat you took from the storehouse, and thought had reduced your account, has returned to you as ten ardabbs. Your taking did not diminish it, but increased it.

Likewise, we understand the Last Day by this logic: we bear the hardships of worship and acts of obedience in this world so that we may attain the everlasting bliss of the Hereafter, because whatever the bliss of this world may be, two things spoil it for you: either you lose it through death, or it loses you through poverty.

But in the Hereafter, its bliss neither escapes you nor do you escape it. Therefore it is more fitting for you to sow for the Hereafter and to reckon for it a thousandfold. If worship involves hardship and faith has its consequences, then look at the greatness of the reward. When you bring to mind the reward for obedience, the hardship of obedience becomes light for you; and when you dread the punishment for disobedience, you turn away from it and keep far from it.

Therefore, what causes a person to persist in sin is that he does not bring to mind its punishment, and he is averse to obedience because he does not bring to mind its reward.

For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A fornicator does not commit fornication while he is a believer, and a drinker does not drink wine while he is a believer." (2) The meaning is: if he had brought his faith to mind, he would not have done it; rather, he was heedless of his faith and so fell into sin.

Whoever brings to mind the reward of obedience finds sweetness in it within himself, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning prayer: "Relieve us by it, O Bilal." (3)

His saying: {And do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief} [al-'Ankabut 29:36]. al-'Athw: hidden corruption, while fasad (corruption) is said of the apparent. So the meaning is: do not commit corruption on the earth as corruption; the absolute object (al-maf'ul al-mutlaq) carries the sense of the verb. Thus His saying {do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief} is like our saying: "sit down in a sitting."

The fa' in His saying {So he said: "O my people, worship Allah…"} indicates that it links this speech to a preceding statement. The implied sense is: "And We sent to Madyan their brother Shu'ayb, and he said: 'O my people, I am the messenger of Allah to you,'" then He mentions what is required of them: {So he said: "O my people, worship Allah…"} [al-'Ankabut 29:36]. The combination of worship of Allah and hope for the Last Day means: do not separate worship from its purpose and its reward, and do not separate disobedience from its punishment.

His saying: {And do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief} [al-'Ankabut 29:36]: I do not tell you "reform," but at least do not leave what is sound in its soundness and corrupt it, because the Creator, mighty and majestic, has prepared the universe for us in the form of soundness, and it is incumbent upon us to keep it in its soundness.

The Nile, for example, is one of the gifts of the Creator and an artery of life flowing with sweet water. You remember the day when the flood came bringing silt, and the water looked exactly like tahina; we used to fill the zir (water jar) from it, and after a little while the silt settled, taking the impurities with it, and the water remained clear and sweet. But now it has been afflicted with pollution, and its water has been corrupted by the waste thrown into it, and we have become the first to suffer the effects of this pollution.

For this reason, the city dweller, however many means of civilisation are available to him, finds no rest except when he leaves the city for the embrace of untouched nature, which has remained as Allah created it: no noise, no pollutants, no electricity, no city.

1. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: they are of the lineage of Madyan ibn Ibrahim, and Shu'ayb is the son of Mikil ibn Yashjur. His name in Syriac is Yuthrun. I say: Madyan is applied both to the tribe and to the city, which is near Ma'an on the Hijaz road. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2/231]
2. A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh). Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2475), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (57), Kitab al-Iman, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).
3. Recorded by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (5/364), and Abu Dawud in his Sunan (4985), from a man among the Companions.

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

{So they denied him, and the earthquake seized them, and they became prostrate in their homes [29:37].}¹

Why do people deny the call to good?

They said: None denies a call to good except those who profit from evil, for good will cut off their path, strip them of their standing, authority and lordship. All those who opposed the messengers of Allah were the great men and chiefs of their people; they had become accustomed to dominance and greatness, and had grown used to people being their slaves. How, then, would they clear the way for the messengers to take this standing from them?

And if not, why did Abdullah ibn Ubayy hate the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? On the day the Messenger of Allah arrived in Madinah, they were preparing a crown for Abdullah ibn Ubayy, to crown him king over Madinah. When the Messenger of Allah came to it, they were occupied with this great event and turned away from that matter.

But what did Shu'ayb say to his people that they denied him? He said to them two things: ﴿Worship Allah and hope for the Last Day..﴾ [29:36], and one prohibition: ﴿And do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief﴾ [29:36]. It is known that a command and a prohibition are speech that does not admit of truth or falsehood, because it is an act of utterance (inshā') and not a report (khabar). For what is the meaning of lying? Lying is that you say of a thing that occurred that it did not occur, or of a thing that did not occur that it occurred; this is what they call a report (khabar).

If your speech agrees with reality, it is true; if it contradicts reality, it is false. So how can we judge as true or false something to which no relation of reality has yet attached? When you say, for example: "Stop!" Do we tell you that you are lying? No, because the reality of an utterance (inshā') does not come about except after you speak. That is why the Arabs divided speech into report (khabar) and utterance (inshā').

To simplify this matter for the learner, we say: the speaker, when he speaks, produces a relation which is called a verbal relation (nisba kalāmiyya); before he speaks it, it has moved in his mind. Before I say, "Zayd is diligent," this matter has circulated in my mind, and in reality there exists a person named Zayd who is indeed diligent.

So we have a mental relation (nisba dhihniyya), a verbal relation, and a real relation (nisba wāqi'iyya). If the real relation exists before the mental and verbal, then the speech here is a report which may be described as true or described as false.

So: the real relation does not come as a result of the verbal relation; rather, when you say "Stop!" the real relation comes as a result of the verbal relation. And since the real relation comes later than the verbal, the utterance cannot be described as either true or false.

Returning to the words of the prophet Shu'ayb, we find them to be two commands: ﴿Worship Allah and hope for the Last Day..﴾ [29:36], and one prohibition: ﴿And do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief﴾ [29:36]. Commands and prohibitions belong to utterance, which is not described as true or false. So how then do they deny him?

Here is the first difficulty: ﴿So they denied him..﴾ [29:37]. The source of this difficulty is the lack of the Arabic faculty by which they understood the speech of Allah. Allah, the Exalted, says here ﴿So they denied him..﴾ [29:37] because he commanded them to worship Allah, and he is a messenger from Allah, so he commands them to worship Him, because worshipping Him is obligatory upon them. He only commanded them so that they would fulfil what is obligatory upon them; the Last Day is certain to come, so hope for it; and corruption on the earth is forbidden.

So: the meaning carries the sense of a report. The two commands, and the prohibition which is a binding command, so they denied him on account of the two commands and the reason for the prohibition.

The meaning of ﴿Worship Allah..﴾ [29:36] is: single Him out, glorified is He, for worship, which is obedience in carrying out commands and refraining from what is forbidden. This worship is required of all, and it is the law of all the prophets and messengers: ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We revealed to you, and that which We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus: that you establish the religion and do not become divided therein..﴾ [42:13].

So: the matter of worship and belief in the Last Day is among the general matters in which the revelations do not differ; as for the laws — "do this, and do not do that" — these differ from one prophet to another.

The meaning of ﴿and hope for the Last Day..﴾ [29:36] is: do what suits your hope for the Last Day. And why do you love the Last Day, and why do you hope for it? No one loves it or hopes for it except one who has done a righteous deed and so awaits it to attain the reward of his work and the recompense of his striving. Otherwise, if it were the other way, he would have said: "and fear the Last Day."

So: hope means: do what qualifies you to hope for the Last Day, for a person hopes only for what benefits him. And here you may ask: if a person believes and carries out the commands and prohibitions of his Lord, is their reward in the Hereafter a hope that he hopes for, or a right that is due to him? It would be expected that He say to the obedient: "Enter the Garden because of what you used to do," for it is owed to him and is his right. So how does the Qur'an call it hope when it is actually realised?

They said: because our reward in the Garden is a bounty from Allah, since He, glorified is He, created us and created for us, and supplied us with capacities and blessings before He imposed anything upon us. So when you worship Allah with due worship, you do not repay the price of His kindness to you, nor do you fulfil for Him what He deserves; so if He rewards you in the Hereafter, it is by the pure bounty of His generosity.

Therefore He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Say: "By the bounty of Allah and by His mercy — in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate."﴾ [10:58]

It is like if you employed a labourer at, say, one hundred pounds a month, and before he did any work for you, you gave him his wage: would he then demand another wage from you? But if you came at the end of the month and gave him ten pounds, that is a bounty and a kindness from you.

Therefore He said ﴿and hope for the Last Day..﴾ [29:36], because on careful examination and reasoning, the reward in the Hereafter is pure bounty from Allah. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "None of you will enter the Garden by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy."²

The prohibition in ﴿And do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief﴾ [29:36] means: do not cause manifest corruption, or: do not do deeds which you think are beneficial but which are harmful. You remember the time when cotton was the main crop in Egypt and the source of income, and the cotton worm used to threaten it, and we fought it by hand, until the Americans came out to us with pesticides, and we used a substance called D.D.T., which destroyed the worm at first, and the peasant thought this problem had been solved.

But after some years the worm grew accustomed to this substance and developed immunity to it, as if D.D.T. had become like candy to it, and we began to suffer gravely from the effects of these pesticides in the water, in the soil, in the crops, and in the health of humans and animals. So: one must consider the consequences before beginning a thing, and weigh harm against benefit.

Likewise when they invented cars, and said: they will ease people's travels and the carrying of their goods. After what the world has reached of a revolution in means of transport, if we compared their benefit with their harm, we would find their harm greater because of the pollution they cause; and if we returned to primitive means and used beasts, it would be better.

I remember when we came to Egypt in 1936–1938 we found in the public squares parking places for donkeys, like car parks now, and that was the only means of transport; and it suffices that donkey dung fertilises the land, whereas car exhaust causes the most dangerous diseases and leads to death.

So what happened after the people of Shu'ayb denied their prophet?

The custom of Allah concerning the prophets before Muhammad (ﷺ) was that the messenger would convey the message of his Lord, but he was not commanded to bear the sword against the disbelievers; rather, if they denied the signs, the Lord of Might, glorified is He, would punish them, and the matter would be settled by the destruction of the deniers.

That the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, does not command people to fight the disbelievers is a logical matter, and the proof of it we saw among the Children of Israel when they asked Allah to impose fighting upon them, and He said: ﴿Is it possible that if fighting is prescribed for you, you will not fight? They said: "What is with us that we should not fight in the way of Allah, when we have been expelled from our homes and our children?" But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except a few of them..﴾ [2:246]

And none was commanded to fight to spread the call except the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); because he (ﷺ) and those who believed with him are secure in this, and because he (ﷺ) is the last of the messengers and prophets, so he must fulfil all the conditions.

The result of the denial: ﴿So the earthquake seized them, and they became prostrate in their homes﴾ [29:37]. This is the punishment of Allah, because He, glorified is He, takes charge of the denier. In (al-Hijr) and in (Hud) He said (al-Sayha, the cry).³ And so that the verses are not accused of contradiction, we say: al-sayha is a severe, alarming sound, and we do not hear this sound except through the violent agitation of the air; and if the agitation of the air were gentle, it would not be called a sayha.

So: the sayha disturbs the air violently; it must result in a rajfa, that is, a severe shaking, like that which demolishes houses and buildings as a result of a bomb, for example. So the sayha existed first, followed by the rajfa; but the Qur'an sometimes mentions the origin and says "the sayha," and sometimes mentions the result and says "the rajfa."

﴿So they became prostrate in their homes﴾ [29:37]. He said "they became" (fa-asbahū) and did not say, for example, "they were," to specify the time of their seizure as morning. The custom is that a raid is at the time of morning, before your opponent prepares to meet you, for he is still sluggish in the aftermath of sleep; and to this day war leaders and commanders prefer that war begin in the morning, when the enemy is surprised by it.

This time has become a general matter, and violating it is counted as a kind of trickery and deception in war, as our leaders did in the October War of '73, when they surprised their enemy at noon; the surprise succeeded, and they took their enemy unawares, because they changed the usual time, which is the morning.

So: a person should not make a fixed routine of his affairs, but should adapt his affairs to what suits them.

Among the anecdotes: a man was keen to wake his son early to go to his work and attend to his affairs. His father said to him: "The son of so-and-so woke early and found a wallet containing one hundred pounds." The son, who was lazy and did not want to wake early, said: "That wallet fell from someone who woke before him."

The meaning of ﴿prostrate (jāthimīn)﴾ [29:37] is: lifeless, without movement.

¹ Rajfa in the Qur'an: every punishment that seized a people is a rajfa, a sayha, or a ṣā'iqa. So said al-Layth. Ibn al-Anbari said: the rajfa involves the shaking of the earth. Rajafat al-ard and arjafat mean the earth quaked. [Lisan al-'Arab, root r-j-f].
² A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh): recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6463), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (2816), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).
³ The word (al-sayha) occurs as a punishment regarding: the people of Thamud (Surah Hud, verse 67; Surah al-Qamar, verse 31); the people of Lut (Surah al-Hijr, verse 73); the people of Shu'ayb (Surah Hud, verse 94).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 29, verse 38:

Then the verses carry us to other brief snapshots from the processions of the messages, as if they were telegrams:

{ And [We destroyed] 'Ad and Thamud, and it has become clear to you from their dwellings. And Satan made their deeds appear pleasing to them and barred them from the way, though they were discerning. }

We notice in these swift telegrams that they mention the introduction, then the ending directly: ﴿And 'Ad and Thamud...﴾ [al-'Ankabut 38]. This is the introduction: ﴿...and it has become clear to you from their dwellings...﴾ [al-'Ankabut 38]. This is a summary of what befell them, and it is as if the Truth, glorified is He, is saying to us: "I will not recount to you what befell them, because you witness their homes and pass by them night and day": ﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning, and by night. Will you not then reason?﴾ [al-Saffat 137-138].

Now, with the scientific revolution, they have been able to photograph what is beneath the earth, and many remains of these villages, 'Ad, Thamud and al-Ahqaf (a region of sand dunes) (2), have appeared. Read His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, [the people of] Iram of the pillars?﴾ [al-Fajr 6-7].

It is natural now that we find the traces of earlier peoples beneath the dust, and we must dig to reach them, because erosion has buried them with the passing of time. Why not? Each of us, if he is absent from his house for a month, returns to find dust covering the surfaces of things, even though he closed the doors and windows. You may calculate the proportion of this dust over thousands of years in open places.

They relate that whirlwinds and violent sandstorms in the sands of al-Ahqaf, for example, used to cover an entire caravan. So how can we expect the traces of these villages to remain on the surface of the earth? Today we observe, for instance, on desert roads, that if a single storm blows, it covers the roads so that traffic movement is obstructed until this layer of sand is removed from them.

So we must say: "Yes, O Lord, we have seen their dwellings and passed by them, even if through the modern photographs taken of these villages." ﴿And Satan made their deeds appear pleasing to them...﴾ [al-'Ankabut 38], meaning: he led them astray into disbelief and persuaded them that it was the sound and best method in the course of life. ﴿...and barred them from the way...﴾ [al-'Ankabut 38]. Since the path of Satan had been made attractive to them, he was bound to bar them from the path of faith. ﴿...though they were discerning﴾ [al-'Ankabut 38], meaning: We did not seize them unawares.

Because the principle that Allah, the Exalted, chose for His creation is ﴿And We would never punish until We sent a messenger﴾ [al-Isra' 15], a messenger who would make things clear to them, warn them, and caution them against the consequence of disbelief. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, did not seize them until after He had sent to them a messenger, and they denied him.

1 'Ad, the people of Hud, peace be upon him, used to dwell in al-Ahqaf, which is near Hadramawt in the land of Yemen. Thamud, the people of Salih, used to dwell in al-Hijr near Wadi al-Qura, and the Arabs knew their dwellings well and passed by them frequently. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3/413]..
2 'Ad, the people of Hud, peace be upon him, used to dwell in al-Ahqaf, which is near Hadramawt in the land of Yemen. Thamud, the people of Salih, used to dwell in al-Hijr near Wadi al-Qura, and the Arabs knew their dwellings well and passed by them frequently. (Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3/413)..

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

{And Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman. Moses had certainly come to them with clear proofs, but they acted arrogantly in the land, and they were not ones who could escape.} (29:39)

The verses are still telling us about the processions of the messages, but they speak of the deniers: 'Ad and Thamud. And here: ﴿And Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman..﴾ [al-'Ankabut]. The proof of His saying, glorified is He, in the previous verse ﴿and they were discerning [people]﴾ [al-'Ankabut] is His saying, exalted is He, here: ﴿Moses had certainly come to them with clear proofs..﴾ [al-'Ankabut]. That is: with the matters that are evident, which leave no room for doubt about the truthfulness of the Truth, glorified is He, and about the truthfulness of the Messenger in conveying from God.

﴿...they acted arrogantly in the land..﴾ [al-'Ankabut]. Istakbara (to act arrogantly, to take on pride): it means iftaʿala from al-kibr (pride), so He did not say takabbara; rather istakbara, as if in his own essence he should not have been arrogant. For the one who is proud is proud of something in himself, but what is bestowed? Because it may be taken from him, so how can he be proud of it?

Therefore we say to the arrogant person: his eye has been heedless of the sight of his Lord in the traces of His creation. Had his Lord been in his mind, he would have been ashamed to be arrogant.

So if a person were to observe the majesty (kibriyaʾ) of his Lord, he would feel small in himself, and would be ashamed to be arrogant. Likewise, the one who is arrogant because of his strength and health is foolish, for he has not considered the state of the weak whom he looks down upon; perhaps that weak person surpasses him in something else, or has a genius in a matter more important than youthful vigour and strength. Moreover, has this youthfulness not considered that it is an incidental matter, which passed to him from others and will pass from him to others?

So: Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman, when Moses came to them with the evident signs of God, acted arrogantly in the land, and they disdained to follow, not by their nature or the nature of such a quality existing in them, but by fabrication without right. ﴿And they were not ones who could escape﴾ [al-'Ankabut]. So He negated from them that they could be those who escape, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And We are not ones who are outdone﴾ [al-Waqi'a].

Sabq (precedence, outstripping) is neither praised nor blamed in itself, but by its outcome: to what did one get ahead? As we now hear them say: "So-and-so is a reactionary (rij'i)", and reactionism is not blamed in itself; perhaps a person was wasteful toward himself, then returned to the way of his Lord, and what a fine reactionism that is. So outstripping is not blamed for its own sake. And read, if you wish, His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord..﴾ [Al 'Imran] — that is, race one another.

The meaning here, ﴿and they were not ones who could escape﴾ [al-'Ankabut]: that there is a racecourse (mudmar sibaq), and whoever gets ahead, they say: "he has won the prize of precedence (ahraza qasab al-sabq)." If this racecourse is in the Hereafter, will anyone outstrip us so as to escape the one from whom we took them? They will not outstrip us, nor will they slip from our grasp, nor will they frustrate our power to overtake them.

The Almighty says:

{So each We seized for his sin. Among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of pebbles, and among them were those seized by the Cry, and among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and among them were those We drowned. And Allah was not one to wrong them, but they were wronging themselves.}

The discussion here concerns the deniers and disbelievers mentioned earlier: the people of 'Ad, Thamud, Madyan, the people of Lut, Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman. It was fitting for the Almighty to mention a comment that encompasses all of them, since they are one group. So He said: ﴿So each...﴾ (Al-'Ankabut 40). That is, each of the deniers mentioned above. The tanwin (nunation) in ﴿So each﴾ is a substitute for everyone previously mentioned, like the tanwin in ﴿And you at that time are watching﴾ (Al-Waqi'ah 84), which substitutes for the whole clause ﴿Then why not, when it reaches the throat﴾ (Al-Waqi'ah 83).

His saying ﴿We seized for his sin﴾ (Al-'Ankabut 40): seizing corresponds to the power and capability of the one who seizes. For this reason He says of His seizing of the deniers: ﴿a seizing by One Mighty, Capable﴾ (Al-Qamar 42). Al-'Aziz (the Mighty) is the one who overcomes and is not overcome, and al-Muqtadir (the Capable) is the one able to seize, such that no one can prevent Him. So He is Mighty.

The seizing here, due to their sins, ﴿for his sin﴾ (Al-'Ankabut 40), is not oppression, tyranny, or arbitrariness. Rather, it is a recompense for their sins and an act of justice. Therefore, at the close of the verse, comes:

﴿And Allah was not one to wrong them, but they were wronging themselves﴾ (Al-'Ankabut 40).

Then the Almighty details the means of His seizing of these deniers: ﴿Among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of pebbles...﴾ (Al-'Ankabut 40). Al-hasib: it is small pebbles thrown not to wound, but heated so that they burn and sting, when the wind hurls them at them. He did not say here, "We sent upon them fire," for example, because fire may burn a person so that he dies and his pain ends. But pelting them with heated stones stings them and prolongs their pains. As we hear people say: "I will burn him, but over a cold fire," so as to prolong his suffering.

Then the Almighty says: ﴿And among them were those seized by the Cry...﴾ (Al-'Ankabut 40). This is the intense sound by which the earth is shaken, and they are Thamud. ﴿And among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow...﴾ (Al-'Ankabut 40), that is, Qarun. ﴿And among them were those We drowned...﴾ (Al-'Ankabut 40), and they are the people of Nuh and Pharaoh.

These are four means of destroying the deniers: fire in the pebble-storm, air in the Cry, earth in the swallowing, then water in the drowning. May Allah have mercy on Fakhr al-Din al-Razi (ﷺ)(2), who said regarding this verse that it encompasses the elements by which human existence is achieved, and the basic elements are four: water, fire, earth, and air. In the past they used to call them "the four elements," but science later distinguished between the element and the substance.

A substance decomposes into elements, but an element does not decompose into anything smaller than it. It is a collection of repeated atoms from which nothing else comes. Air is a substance that we can analyse into oxygen and so on. Likewise water is a substance composed of several elements and atoms, until Mendeleev came and laid out a table of the elements, giving each a number which they called the atomic numbers. So this element, for example, is number one, meaning it consists of one atom, and this is number two, meaning it consists of two atoms, and so on, until he reached number 93. But among these numbers he found missing numbers, which scientists discovered later.

For example, Madame Curie came and discovered the element radium. They found indeed that its number was one of the missing numbers in Mendeleev's table, so they placed it in its position. This shows that the universe was created with ordered elements, which, with scientific progress, have now reached 105 elements.

When scientists analysed the elements of fertile soil from which we eat crops, they found 16 elements, beginning with oxygen as the highest proportion and ending with manganese as the lowest proportion, since it does not reach one part in a thousand. When they analysed the elements of the human body, they found these same sixteen elements.

It is as if the Almighty established even the disbelievers as proof of His truth regarding the creation of man from clay, so that we know that when the Almighty wishes to reveal a secret of His universe, He brings it about even through the hands of disbelievers.

The first to speak of the four elements of which the universe is composed was the Greek philosopher Aristotle, who died in 384 BC. On the basis of these four elements they used to calculate the astrological fate (najm). For example, regarding marriage, they would calculate the astrological fate of the husband and wife according to these elements. They found that the husband's fate was air and the wife's fate was fire, so they said: "They will make it a conflagration." At another time they found the wife was watery and the marriage earthy, so they said: "They will make it a dough."

It is well known that the Almighty, in the expansiveness of His power, makes the elements of survival the very elements of annihilation. He is the One able to save and destroy by one and the same thing, as He destroyed Pharaoh by water and saved Musa (peace be upon him) by water.

Likewise, when we reflect on these four elements, we find they are the elements of human composition, for Allah created him from water and earth, so he became good (clay), then dried by heat until he became dry clay like pottery. Then after that he breathes air. So by these very elements from which creation came, destruction can occur.

The Almighty desires that His creatures turn to the universe in all its manifestations and signs with alertness, so that they may deduce from it the places of lessons and secrets. For this reason we find that all discoveries came as a result of precise observation of the phenomena of the universe.

Our Lord draws our attention to the importance of experimental science, saying: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth they pass by, while they turn away from it﴾ (Yusuf 105). It is therefore necessary that we reflect on what we see. Man did not arrive at the age of steam, nor at Archimedes' law of buoyancy, nor at electricity, gravity, and penicillin, except through careful reflection on the phenomena of things. Therefore observation is the foundation of every experimental science, first, then experimentation second, then repeating the experiment so that the scientific result emerges.

Air is a fundamental cause of human life, and by it balance occurs in the universe, unless the Almighty wills to make it a whirlwind or a destructive hurricane. We have already said: you can endure without food for a month, and without water for ten days, but you cannot endure without air beyond the measure of an inhalation and exhalation. Air is therefore the most important cause of the continuation of life. For this reason we hear them say, in intense plotting: "By God, I will suffocate his breath," because it is the direct path to death. Therefore air is a fundamental factor among the means of destruction mentioned.

By air, things maintain their balance. High mountains and towering buildings did not stand by the strength of steel and concrete, but by the balance of air, as is evident in that if you empty one side of them of air, they would collapse on that side immediately.

By this same principle destruction occurs through bombs, because they depend on the theory of evacuating air, and what they call the "suction reactor" and "pressure reactor." Things around you stand only because air surrounds them from all their sides.

We have said that when the Noble Qur'an speaks to us of air, it speaks of it with the precision of the All-Knowing Creator. Every singular "wind" came for destruction and annihilation, and every "winds" in the plural form came for growth, goodness, and prosperity. Recite, if you wish, His saying: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing...﴾ (Al-Hijr 22).

And His saying: ﴿And as for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a furious, raging wind﴾ (Al-Haqqah 6), because it was one wind blowing from one direction, destroying.

Then the verse concludes with this truth: ﴿And Allah was not one to wrong them, but they were wronging themselves﴾ (Al-'Ankabut 40), because the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, honoured the human being ﴿And We have certainly honoured the children of Adam...﴾ (Al-Isra 70). He honoured him above all creatures with intellect and choice. So if you look at the universe and survey the kinds of existence, you will find that man is the master of this whole universe.

The kinds in the universe are ranked: man, and below him the rank of animals, then plants, then inanimate matter. When inanimate matter takes a manifestation of the favour of the Truth upon it, namely growth, it becomes a plant. And when a plant takes a manifestation of the overflow of the Truth upon creation, giving it, for example, sensation, it becomes an animal. When the Almighty manifests Himself to it by His grace and gives it the blessing of intellect, it becomes a human.

But does the plant, when it takes the property of growth and so surpasses inanimate matter, leave inanimate matter? No, the inanimacy remains in it, as evidenced by the fact that when growth stops, it returns to being inanimate like a stone. Likewise the animal takes the manifestation of sensation and is distinguished from the plant by it, but the vegetative nature remains in it, as it grows and matures.

And man, the master of the universe, whom his Lord has honoured with intellect, still has inanimacy in him, as evidenced by the effect of gravity upon him. If he throws himself from a high place, he cannot hold himself in the air. Likewise the vegetative and animal natures remain in him. Thus in him are all the properties of the other kinds below him, and he surpasses them with intellect.

For this reason Allah does not charge him except after his intellect matures and he reaches puberty, and on condition that he is free of defect in his intellect, such as madness, and that he is one who chooses. The coerced person bears no obligation, because he is not choosing.

Man, whom his Lord has honoured with intellect and choice, and preferred above all kinds of existence, is not fit to submit or worship except to one higher than himself in rank. As for abasing himself to worship what is lower in rank, this is something strange and unbefitting. The worshipper must be lower in rank than the worshipped. You, by judgement, are higher in rank than what is beneath you of animals, plants, and inanimate matter. So how can you let it dispose of you, when among your own actions is that you shape it by carving, place it where you want, and if it breaks you repair it?!

So: your Lord honoured you, and you dishonoured yourself, and you accepted for it a lowly state. He made you a master, and you made yourself a slave to the basest of creatures. For this reason the Almighty says in the sacred hadith: "O son of Adam, I created you for My sake, and I created the whole universe for your sake, so do not busy yourself with what belongs to you at the expense of that for which you were created."(4)

So: ﴿And Allah was not one to wrong them...﴾ (Al-'Ankabut 40). That is, it is not fitting for Allah, the Exalted, to wrong them. So when you hear "it was not for you to do such-and-such," the meaning is that you are capable of this, but it is not right for you. Thus the Almighty negates oppression from Himself, not because He is incapable of it, but because it is not befitting for Him to oppress, since oppression means taking the right of another, while Allah, the Exalted, is the owner of everything, so why would He oppress?

An example of this is the negation of the suitability of poetry from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as the Almighty said: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him...﴾ (Ya-Sin 69). The Prophet (ﷺ) was able to compose poetry, for he had all its tools, but it was not befitting for the Messenger to be a poet, because "they are liars, wandering in every valley." So there is a distinction between the unsuitability of a thing and its actual existence.

This meaning is confirmed by His saying: ﴿And your Lord is not a wrongdoer toward the servants﴾ (Fussilat 46), using the intensive form ẓallām, and not ẓālim. Why? Because if Allah, the Exalted, were to permit oppression for Himself, it would come in proportion to His might, so He would not be called "oppressor" but "very oppressive"; exalted is Allah far above this.

When we spoke of intensification (mubalagha) and its forms, we said that intensification may be in the act itself, as when you eat one loaf in a single meal while someone else eats five, for example, or in the repetition of the act, as when you eat three meals and someone else eats six. So we say: "So-and-so is a eater" (akil), and "So-and-so is a glutton" (akul or akkal). Intensification therefore arises either from magnifying the act itself or from repeating it.

In His saying: ﴿And your Lord is not a wrongdoer toward the servants﴾ (Fussilat 46), He did not say "to the servant." So the multiplicity of people would entail a multiplicity of oppression, if it were conceivable. Therefore He came with the intensive form (ẓallām).

There is a linguistic issue in the matter of intensification which says: negating the intensive form does not negate the base form, and affirming the base form does not affirm the intensive form. For example, when we say "So-and-so is a glutton," he is an eater a fortiori. But when we say "So-and-so is an eater," this does not mean he is a glutton. Thus the negation of intensification in ﴿And your Lord is not a wrongdoer toward the servants﴾ (Fussilat 46) does not negate the base (ẓālim), and far be it from Allah that He should be an oppressor.

And His saying, the Exalted: {But they were...

Following the first verse of the passage, after the verses have told us about the disbelievers who took partners alongside Allah, and about those who denied the messengers and what punishment befell them, He gives us a parable that brings these realities close to us. So He, glory be to Him, says:

{The example of those who take protectors other than Allah is like the spider, which takes a house. And indeed, the weakest of houses is the house of the spider, if only they knew.} (29:41)

The word (mathal) and its derivatives occur many times in the Noble Qur'an. The root m-th-l conveys a meaning we must understand. When it is said (mithl), with a sukun on the thaʼ, it means comparison (tashbih), but the comparison of one singular thing with another singular thing.

As in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him...﴾ (42:11) and His saying: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it...﴾ (42:40).

As for (mathal) with a fatha on the mim, it means the comparison of a story or of a plurality with a plurality, as in His saying: ﴿And present to them the parable of the life of this world: it is like water which We send down from the sky...﴾ (18:45).

So the Truth, glory be to Him, does not compare a thing with a thing; rather, He compares a complete image with another image. The life of this world, in its existence, its blossom, its adornment, its greenery and its enjoyments, and then its ending in decline, is like water when it descends from the sky and mingles with the earth's soil, so that beautiful flowering plants grow, which quickly turn into debris.

Therefore some who contend stubbornly have objected to the Qur'anic style in the saying of the Truth, exalted is He, about Jesus, peace be upon him: ﴿Indeed, the example of Jesus to Allah is like the example of Adam...﴾ (3:59).

The objection is that (mathal) here compares one singular thing with another singular thing, namely Jesus with Adam, peace be upon them both. We say: it compares a complete image with another. The objection arises from failure to understand the meaning intended by the verse. Allah does not compare Jesus with Adam as persons; rather, He compares the story of Adam's creation with the story of Jesus's creation. Adam was created without a father, and likewise Jesus was created without a father.

The meaning is: if you marvelled that Jesus was created without a father, you should marvel even more at the creation of Adam, who came without a father and without a mother. The trial lies in Adam, not in Jesus.

The matter is that Allah, exalted is He, willed to announce His creation as a manifestation of the absoluteness of His power, in that He does not create in one fixed manner. Rather, He creates as He wills, from a father and a mother, or without a father, or without a mother, and He creates from a father only, or from a mother only.

So this matter is not subject to causes; it is subject to the will of the One who causes, glory be to Him. When He wills, He says to a thing, "Be," and it is. A married couple may come together and be decreed barrenness, so they bear no children; and Allah may make the barren woman conceive, and make the aged woman give birth. The evidences for this are clear. So the absoluteness of power in this matter encompasses every case, without any limit confining it.

When the Truth, exalted is He, strikes examples for us, He wants by that to clarify for us the obscure by means of the clear, the vague by means of the evident, and the general by means of the detailed. The Qur'an has proceeded in this according to the custom of the Arabs, who used parables in explanation and clarification.

It is related that a certain man, who had a good reputation and a fine conduct among the people, was envied by another, who sought to attach to him an accusation that would disfigure his image and remove his standing among the people. So he accused him of frequenting a beautiful widow, and people indeed saw him going to her house, where a woman came out to him and he gave her something he had with him.

When the people verified the matter, they found her to be an elderly woman with small children who were poor, and this man was kind to them and bestowed upon them from what Allah had provided him. When they came to know this about the man, they esteemed him and raised his station, and his glory and merit increased in their eyes.

The poet took up this meaning and expressed it, using the parable, saying:
"When Allah wills to spread a virtue, He lets it be carried by the tongue of an envious person.
Were it not for the fire kindled by what is beside it, the fragrance of the aloe-wood would not be known."
The oud is a kind of incense, of pleasant fragrance, whose scent does not spread except when it is burned.

Among its derivatives also is (mithluhu), as in His saying: ﴿And examples of those who came before them have already passed.﴾ (13:6), meaning the punishments that befell the nations who denied, until He made them a lesson for others.

When a proverb becomes well known, it spreads on the tongues, and people strike it as an example, just as Hatim al-Ta'i became famous for generosity and generosity became a proverbial reference for him. A brief phrase among us may also become well known and become a proverb struck on fitting occasions, as we say to the student who neglects the whole year and then exerts himself on the night of the examination: "Before the shooting, he fills the quivers" (qabla al-rama'i tamla'u al-kana'in), keeping the exact wording of the proverb on every occasion, even when there is no shooting and no quivers.

Just as the proverb is said as it is, without change, whether for the singular, the dual, the masculine plural, or the feminine, so too we say "Mādhā warāʼaka yā ʻiṣām" with a kasra, because it was originally said to a woman.

The Truth, exalted is He, says: ﴿The example of those who take protectors other than Allah is like the spider, which takes a house...﴾ (29:41).

This is an example at the summit of belief, which Allah struck for us for clarification and explanation, and to bring matters close to our minds. Beware of saying, regarding the parable Allah has struck for you: "What did Allah intend by this?" For Allah, exalted is He, has said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is not shy to strike an example, even of a mosquito or what is above it...﴾ (2:26).

Some see that this mosquito is a trivial thing, so how would Allah make it an example? The truth is that the mosquito is one of the creatures of Allah, containing wonders and secrets that call you to reflection and contemplation, and it is not a trivial thing as you suppose. Rather, it is enough honour for you to reach the secret of greatness in it.

In this tiny creature are all the components of life and perception. Do you know where its mind is, and where its circulatory apparatus is... etc.? Besides the fly and the gnat and small creatures, do you not see the microbes which you cannot see with your naked eye, yet which afflict you, strong as you are, with what troubles and disturbs you?

So do not say: why does Allah strike examples with these things? For Allah ﴿is not shy to strike an example, even of a mosquito or what is above it﴾ (2:26). "What is above it" means in smallness and in indication; that is, what is smaller than it in size. For the greatness of creation is manifested in the largest thing, and likewise in the smallest thing of most precise craftsmanship.

If you look, for example, at the clock "Big Ben", which is the largest and most famous clock in the world, by which the world sets its time, you will find it a massive thing in size, so that the one coming from far away can see it and read it. It indicates the greatness of workmanship and the skill of the engineers who built it; its greatness lies in its massiveness and grandeur. But if you look at the same kind of clock which they placed in the setting of a ring, you will find in it too greatness and skill arising from the precision of craftsmanship in small size.

Likewise, the radio, when it first appeared, was the size of a threshing floor winnowing basin, and now it has become small, the size of a pocket.

Among the creatures of Allah are those so fine that you cannot perceive them with your senses. Strangely, a person asks to see Allah plainly, while he cannot see the traces of His creation and craftsmanship. You do not see jinn, you do not see microbes and germs, and you do not even see your soul which is between your two sides and by which you live. None of these things is seen or perceived by the other means of perception. So among His greatness, exalted is He, is that He perceives the sights, while the sights cannot perceive Him.

Let us return to the example Allah has struck for us: ﴿The example of those who take protectors other than Allah...﴾ (29:41), that is, partners and intercessors, ﴿is like the spider...﴾ (29:41), this weak creature which weaves its threads with this precision which we see, and which wove its threads over the cave during the Hijra of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and shared with the dove in confounding the disbelievers.

﴿...which takes a house﴾ (29:41), that is, out of these flimsy threads, ﴿And indeed, the weakest of houses is the house of the spider﴾ (29:41). The spider's error lies not in taking a house, but in taking as its house these flimsy threads, which a gust of wind is enough to sweep away. A house must be fortified to protect its occupant, and must have doors, windows, walls, and so on. But if it had made them a net to catch its prey, that would have been more suitable. Likewise, the disbelievers took idols as gods; had they taken them as evidence of the Truth's power in creation, that would have been more suitable and more beneficial.

Just as the spider's house is destroyed by a gust of wind and torn apart, and you, for example, clean your house, and perhaps the spider itself is swept away, so too Allah does with the deeds of the disbelievers: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ (25:23).

And likewise He strikes for them another example: ﴿The example of those who disbelieved in their Lord: their deeds are like ashes on which the wind blows hard on a stormy day...﴾ (14:18).

As for the meaning of ﴿if only they knew﴾ (29:41), that is, the reality of things: the spider's web is not fit to be a house, but it is fit to be a trap for insects. Likewise, idols and stones are not fit to be gods worshipped; rather, they serve as indication of the power of the Creator, glory be to Him. Had they reflected on them and on the secrets of their creation, they would have been guided through them to faith.

So they are, then, a proof of power, if only they knew. The mountain, this rock from which you carve your idols, is the first servant to you and to those lower than you of animals and plants. We have said before that inanimate matter serves plants and serves animals, and they all serve man.

Thus inanimate matter is the servant of servants, yet you have made it a god. Consider then this reversal, and the baseness of your thinking and the wickedness of your dispositions, in that you have made the lowest and most worthless of things the highest and most honourable of things, in your own opinion.

How, when Allah has distinguished you above all the kinds of creatures? You should have sought something higher than you, fitting for your worship; and then you would find nothing but Allah to take as a god.

Indeed, if you wish, read about inanimate matter in His saying: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days, and set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed in it...﴾ (41:9-10), that is, in the earth, ﴿firm mountains above it, and blessed it, and determined therein its sustenance in four days, equally for those who ask.﴾ (41:10)

It is as if the bare, firm mountains are the storehouses of sustenance for people through the ages: from them rocks crumble, and the silt is formed which water carries to us in the seasons of flooding, and from them the fertile layer is formed in the plains and valleys, becoming a source of abundant and renewed growth that never ceases. You remember the days of the flood and what the Nile of Egypt used to bring us of renewed goodness every year, and how the water used to come to us almost like flour, from the abundance of silt in it.

So would that the worshippers of idols, who carved rocks into idols, would contemplate these verses which indicate the power of the Creator, glory be to Him, instead of worshipping them besides Allah.

In another place the Truth, glory be to Him, also strikes for us an example at the summit of belief, saying, glory be to Him:

﴿Allah strikes an example: a man in whom are partners at odds with one another, and a man belonging wholly to one man. Are they equal in comparison? Praise be to Allah! But most of them do not know.﴾ (39:29)

He distinguishes between a slave owned by one master who receives command and prohibition from him alone, and a slave owned by several partners, who may not agree, but are at odds, each with his own demands for every order. How then can he satisfy them, and how can he fulfil their rights while they pull him in different directions?

So the one who worships Allah alone, with no partner, is like the slave of one master, while those who worship idols are like the slave with quarrelling partners. So the Truth, glory be to Him, strikes examples for people about realities, to make them clear to them with clear explanation.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

{Indeed, Allah knows whatever they invoke besides Him of anything. And He is the Mighty, the Wise.} (29:42)

He says, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah knows whatever they invoke besides Him of anything...﴾ (29:42) because when the noose was tightened around them, they said: "We do not worship idols; we only worship the stars that move these idols, or the angels." So Allah refuted them: ﴿Indeed, Allah knows whatever they invoke besides Him of anything...﴾ (29:42). His words here, ﴿of anything...﴾ (29:42), are for diminishment, as if what they invoke besides Him is not counted as anything, or it is too insignificant to be anything, or it means: Allah, glorified is He, knows whatever they invoke besides Him of any kind.

Or [the word] "shay'" (thing) comes from our saying: shaa yashaa shay'an (he willed, he wills, a willing). So the "shay'" is that which one wants another to do, and the One who willed is Allah, the Exalted. It is as if they worship the thing willed and leave its Creator, while He is most worthy of worship, glorified is He. ﴿So what has happened to you?!﴾ (37:154) You worship the created and leave the Creator; after Allah has honored you, you debase yourselves and accept what is inferior for yourselves, in that you worship what is lower than you in rank of creation, while idols are inanimate objects, and they are the lowest of the kinds of existence.

Then He says, glorified is He: ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ (29:42) The Mighty, who overcomes and is not overcome; and the Wise in all that He decrees and commands.

Then the Truthful, glory be to Him, says:

{And these parables We strike for mankind, but none understands them except those who have knowledge.} (29:43)

Whoever hears a parable from God, the Exalted, and then does not understand it, is not a person of knowledge. Therefore, those who objected to His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example — that of a mosquito or what is above it.﴾ (2:26), are not people of knowledge, for they considered the mosquito insignificant and saw that it did not deserve to be cited as an example.

We say to them: You are neither intelligent nor knowledgeable about the precision of the parable. Read: ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for that.﴾ (22:73) And more than that: ﴿And if the fly should steal from them a thing, they could not recover it from it.﴾ (22:73)

Set aside the matter of creation, and consider the simplest thing in the movement of our lives: when a fly lands on your food and takes something from it, can you retrieve it from it, however much strength and might you possess?
