If the birth of the secret comes and they have not reached it through their research, nor arrived at its premises, Allah reveals it to them, even by coincidence, and they have discovered many secrets of the universe by coincidence.

So the true unseen is that which has no premises leading to it, and which no one knows except Allah. Of it Allah said: ﴿Knower of the unseen; He does not disclose His unseen to anyone, except to a messenger whom He has approved.﴾ [al-Jinn 72:26-27] Therefore, the Messenger does not know the unseen; rather, he knows what the unseen is.

Then He, exalted be He, says: ﴿And those who believed in falsehood...﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:52] i.e., in worshipping what is other than Allah of idols and images, ﴿and disbelieved in Allah...﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:52] the Creator, the Necessarily Existent, ﴿it is they who are the losers.﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:52] Because the disbelief of creatures in the Creator does not affect His essence, nor the attributes of perfection in Him, for He created them with attributes of perfection, so He has the attributes of perfection, whether they believe or disbelieve.

But there is a difference between one who believes and one who disbelieves. Man by his nature is eager for life and attached to it, so much so that if he falls ill he seeks treatment to preserve his life, and he fears death, and sees the deaths of people around him, and how his forefathers preceded him and none of them remained immortal, and sees that death comes without causes; so much so that it was said: "Death without a cause is itself the cause."

Thus death is a reality that occurs, yet people doubt it and cannot imagine it for themselves, because they dislike it. Therefore it is said in the saying (athar): "I have never seen certainty more like doubt than people's certainty about death."

And from man's certainty about death, we see him loving to remain in his children, and in his children's children, so that his memory may endure for as long as possible. Since this is the case, why do you not believe in Allah, so that faith bequeaths to you an eternal life that lasts without end, which neither leaves you nor you it, and that is the life of the Hereafter? So who are the losers? The losers are the disbelievers who confined their lives to the span of their lives in this world.

Then the Almighty says:

{And they challenge you to hasten the punishment. And were it not for a specified term, the punishment would have come upon them already. And it will surely come upon them suddenly, while they are unaware.} (29:53)

It is strange that a person would ask for punishment for himself, and seek to hasten it if it is slow to come. So these people only demanded it because they believed it would not befall them; for if they were certain of its occurrence, they would not have demanded it.

﴿And were it not for a specified term, the punishment would have come upon them.﴾ (29:53) Because everything with Allah has its appointed time and term. Terms differ according to their owners: these are the lifespans and ages of people, which are scattered among them. But there is one term that encompasses them all and in which they all share, and that is the term of the Hour.

So His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿When their term comes, they cannot delay it by an hour, nor can they advance it.﴾ (7:34) means: with their scattered individual terms. As for the term of the Resurrection, it is one specified term with Allah, Exalted is He. Among the remarkable differences between the two terms is that the scattered terms in this world end a life, whereas the term of the Hereafter is where life begins.

The meaning of ﴿And were it not for a specified term, the punishment would have come upon them⦆ (29:53) is that the matter is not according to their whims and desires. Therefore, Exalted is He says: ﴿Man was created of haste.﴾ (21:37) And He says: ﴿I will show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten them.﴾ (21:37)

Accordingly, when the Prophet ﷺ concluded the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah between himself and the disbelievers of Makkah, and agreed to return with his companions without performing the ʿUmrah pilgrimage, the Companions became angry, as did ʿAlī and ʿUmar. They did not like this treaty, and some of them nearly opposed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ regarding their religion. The Prophet ﷺ entered upon Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, and said: (("The Muslims are destroyed.")) (1) She said: "Why, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "I commanded them, but they did not comply." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, excuse them. They are distressed; they came out eager for the House of Allah, and they were close to it, and then they are prevented and turned back. Excuse them, O Messenger of Allah, but go forth and do what Allah has commanded you, and leave them. If they see you do it, they will do it, and they will know that this is a firm decision."

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah went out, shaved his head and ended his ʿUmrah state, and the people did likewise. The counsel of the Lady Umm Salamah succeeded and rescued the situation.

Then Allah explained to them the wisdom of returning that year without fighting: ﴿There are believing men and women among you in Makkah whom you do not know, so that you might harm them unknowingly.⦆ In other words, if you entered Makkah upon them, you would kill them without knowing of their faith.

ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, as was his habit, was strict regarding the truth, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, are we not upon the truth?" He ﷺ said: "Yes." He said: "Are they not upon falsehood?" He ﷺ said: "Yes." He said: "Then why should we accept humiliation in our religion?" Abu Bakr said: "Hold to your stirrup, O ʿUmar," meaning: stop at your limit and restrain yourself. Then he said, to make clear the significance of this covenant: "There has never been a victory in Islam greater than the victory of Hudaybiyyah," not the conquest of Makkah.

Why? Because Hudaybiyyah obtained from the disbelievers the recognition of Muhammad, whereas they had been opposing him and not acknowledging his call, so that they would write a treaty with him and agree with him on a matter. Moreover, it gave the Messenger of Allah the opportunity to devote himself to the affair of the call and to spread it throughout the regions of the Arabian Peninsula. But at that time people's assumptions did not extend to what lay between Muhammad and his Lord. Servants are customarily hasty, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not hasten with the haste of His servants, until matters reach what He wills, Glorified is He.

Then the Exalted says: ﴿And it will surely come upon them suddenly, while they are unaware.⦆ (29:53) That is: unexpectedly, not according to their desire. ﴿While they are unaware⦆ (29:53): do they not perceive it at that moment, or do they not now perceive that it is true and that it will occur at its appointed term?

The intended meaning is that they do not now perceive that it is coming and that it has an appointed term, and that it will overtake them with its horrors. So it was incumbent upon them to know this now and to believe in it. Thus the intended meaning is not that they will be unaware of the suddenness, because perceiving the suddenness at that moment will not benefit them in anything.

As for the migration to Madinah after the migration to Abyssinia, it was to a house of security and faith at once, where you are safe in your religion, able to spread it and call to it, and find believing brothers who console you with their wealth and with all they possess. The Ansar in the city of the Messenger of Allah set the most magnificent example in history of equality. An Ansari would see his migrant brother who had left his family in Makkah and had a need for women, so he would divorce one of his wives so that he could marry her. So see what faith did to the Ansar.

In His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿So worship Me alone⦆ (29:56) there is a style that they call the restrictive style (qasr), like His saying: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.⦆ (1:5)

There is a difference between our saying "we worship You" and "You alone we worship." "We worship You" does not prevent us from worshipping others, whereas "You alone we worship" restricts worship to Allah, Exalted is He, and does not go beyond Him to anything else.

So the meaning, then, is: if you are going to migrate, let your migration be for Allah. The Prophet ﷺ explained it in the noble hadith: "Whoever's migration was to Allah and His Messenger, his migration is to Allah and His Messenger; and whoever's migration was for worldly gain he would obtain, or a woman he would marry, his migration is to what he migrated for." (3)

(1) Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (4/326) within the long hadith of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, from the hadith of al-Miswar ibn Makhramah al-Zuhri and Marwan ibn al-Hakam, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O people, sacrifice and shave." No one stood up; he repeated it, and no one stood up; he repeated it a third time, and no one stood up. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went in to Umm Salamah and said: "O Umm Salamah, what is the matter with the people?" She said: "O Messenger of Allah, what you have seen has overcome them. Do not speak to any of them, but go to your sacrificial animal, slaughter it and shave." So he went out without speaking to anyone until he reached his offering, slaughtered it, then sat and shaved; and the people stood up, sacrificing and shaving.

(2) Similar was narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (1785), Kitab al-Jihad, and by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4844) in his commentary on Surah al-Fath, from the hadith of Sahl ibn Hunayf, may Allah be pleased with him.

(3) A hadith agreed upon (Muttafaq ʿalayh). Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (1), and likewise by Muslim in his Sahih (1907), Kitab al-Imarah (155), from the hadith of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him.

Then the Almighty says:

﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed Hell encompasses the disbelievers.﴾ (29:54)

That is: say to them, "If you are hastening the punishment, it is coming without doubt, and if you are eager for it while you wait, [know that] it will fill you up, and you will say, 'Is there any more?'" Punishment corresponds to the power of the one who punishes, in strength and weakness, in comprehensiveness and extent. So when the one who punishes is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, none among the worlds can punish as He punishes.

The meaning of ﴿encompasses the disbelievers﴾ (al-Ankabut) is that the encompassing (al-ihatah) is that it includes a thing from all its directions. The directions are four: north, south, east and west, and between the principal directions are secondary directions, and between the secondary directions are also further secondary directions, and al-ihatah is that which includes all these directions.

From this is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire whose enclosure surrounds them...﴾ (18:29). That is: from all their directions.

Note 1 (occasion of revelation of the verse): al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (7/5247): "It was said: it was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah and his companions among the polytheists when they said, ﴿Or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you have claimed...﴾ (17:92)..."

Among the wonders of the Fire in the Hereafter is that fire in this world can torment a person with a flame surrounding him from which he cannot escape. But fire by its nature rises, because the flame tends upward. If it is beneath your foot, however, you can tread on it with your foot, as, for example, one puts out a cigarette butt (ʿaqb). When you step on it, you cut off its oxygen, and the fire goes out. But in the Fire of the Hereafter, it comes to them from all their directions:

{On the Day the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet, and He will say: "Taste what you used to do."} [29:55]

In another place He, glorified is He, says: ﴿For them there will be canopies of Fire above them, and beneath them canopies﴾ [39:16]

These two directions are not reached by fire in this world, because fire by its nature ascends upward, and if it is beneath the foot it is extinguished. So this is an escalation in punishment, in that it is not limited to encirclement from all their sides; rather it also reaches them from above them and from beneath them.

However, the one being punished may steel himself against the torment and hold firm so that he gives no satisfaction to his tormentors. For such a person there comes another kind of punishment, a punishment that humiliates and abases him, and it is said to him: ﴿Taste it; indeed you are the mighty, the noble﴾ [44:49]. Therefore the punishment is described as humiliating (muhin), painful (alim), great (ʿazim), and severe (shadid).

As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And He will say: "Taste what you used to do."﴾ [29:55], He did not say "Taste the Fire," but rather "Taste what you did," as if the deed itself will be the Fire that burns them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 29, verse 56:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿O My servants who believe, indeed My earth is vast, so worship Me alone.﴾ (29:56)

After the Truth, glorified is He, had spoken of the disbelievers and deniers, He wanted to create a balance in the context. So He speaks here of the believers, so that it would be more painful for the disbelievers: when the discourse about them is followed by what will befall them of punishment, alongside what the believers will attain of bliss, they will feel intense regret. For if the believers did not receive this bliss, the matter would be easier for them.

As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿O My servants...﴾ (29:56), we have already said that all creation are servants of Allah, and the servants of Allah are of two kinds: believer and disbeliever. Allah made each of them free in choice. The believer gave up his choice in favour of his Lord's choice, and preferred the will of Allah, glorified is He, over his own will, so he became a servant in everything, including choice. For this reason they deserve to be called servants and worshippers of Allah.

As for the disbeliever, he refused the will of his Lord, chose disbelief over faith and disobedience over obedience, and forgot that he is a servant of Allah, subdued in matters over which he cannot choose. It is as if Allah says to him: "You, O disbeliever, have rebelled against your Lord, and refused His method in (do) and (do not do), and have made rebellion against Allah a habit. Then why do you not rebel against what He decrees upon you of fates? Why do you not refuse illness or death? So you are in the grip of your Lord, and cannot escape from it."

Accordingly, the believer and the disbeliever are equal in servitude to Allah, but the difference lies in worship ('ibadiyya), where the believer came to it freely, content with the will of Allah. There is a difference between a servant who obeys you while you drag him on a chain, and a servant who serves you while he is free. Likewise, the believer came to faith in Allah by choice, with the possibility of disbelieving, and this is both servitude ('ubudiyya) and worship ('ibadiyya) together.

The meaning of ﴿indeed My earth is vast﴾ (29:56): their Lord addresses them with this address while they are on the earth and in its vastness, to draw their attention to the fact that they will be persecuted and tortured, and harm and pain will befall them. So He says to them: beware that this harshness should not divert you, beware that you should not retreat from your call. If this place does not suit you, then go to another place, for the earth of Allah is vast, so do not constrict it upon yourselves.

Therefore our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), said: "The earth belongs to Allah, and the servants are all Allah's. So if you see good, then settle where it is."

What we suffer from now is these borders and these restrictions that we have placed on the geography of Allah's earth. We have constricted upon ourselves what Allah had made wide for us. The earth of Allah has no entry visas, no passports, and no "blacklists."

For this reason we once said at the United Nations: if you strive to apply one principle from the principles of the Qur'an, no evil will exist on earth, namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the earth He has set down for the creatures﴾ (55:10).

The meaning: the whole earth is for all creatures. If your provision becomes restricted in one place, seek it in another place. Otherwise, what troubles people now is that there is land without people, or people without land. Here is Sudan, for example, beside us, with the finest lands, yet you find no one to cultivate it. Why? Because of the restrictions we have placed and by which we have constricted ourselves.

The poet spoke truly when he said:

By your life, lands have never constricted their people, but the characters of men constrict.

Then He, glorified is He, says ﴿So worship Me alone﴾ (29:56). If we take up the principle of emigration, we must know that emigration has conditions. The first: you emigrate to a place that preserves your faith for you and does not diminish it. Before you leave your country, look: will you be able in the land of emigration to perform your religious duties as Allah has obligated them upon you? If so, there is no objection; otherwise there is no emigration to a place that takes me out of the circle of faith, or that prevents me from carrying out the commands of my religion.

Would it please you to live gathering wealth in lands of disbelief, and to have your daughter enter upon you, for example, with a young man in her hand about whom you know nothing, imposed upon you as a fait accompli, having become acquainted with him in the manner of those people? At that time, all that you have gathered will not benefit you, and what has been wounded of your dignity will not be mended.

We have already clarified that emigration may be only to a abode of security, where you are secure in your religion, and secure that no one will tempt you away from it. Among this is the emigration that the Messenger of Allah commanded to Abyssinia, which was not a land of faith but a land of security.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) explained his command to emigrate there by saying: "In it there is a king under whom no one is wronged." After the emigration there, the truth of the Messenger of Allah became clear, as if he had complete knowledge of the environment around him and the conditions of its people.

For this reason, he did not command them, for example, to emigrate to the outskirts of the Arabian Peninsula, because it was subject to Quraysh by their sovereignty over the Ka'bah. No one could protect one whom Quraysh sought. Even those who emigrated with their religion to Abyssinia were not safe from Quraysh: Quraysh sent to the Negus someone to speak with him about them, and they carried to him enticing gifts so that he would hand over to them the emigrants among the believers in Muhammad. But this trick did not succeed with the just king, in whose heart faith had taken root; he loved the believers, defended them, and refused to return them. It is said that he embraced Islam afterwards, and when he died, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed over him.

1 From Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The lands are Allah's lands, and the servants are Allah's servants, so wherever you find good, settle there." Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/166). Al-'Ajluni cited it in Kashf al-Khafa' (1/342) with the wording "wherever you see kindness, settle there," and said: "Al-Tabari narrated it from Zubayr with a weak chain; al-Najm also attributed it to Ahmad and al-Tabarani from Zubayr with a weak chain."
2 From Umm Salama, who said: "When Mecca became constricting for us, and the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were harmed and tested, and they saw what afflicted them of trial in their religion, and that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) could not repel that from them, while the Messenger of Allah was protected by his people and his uncle, so that nothing reached him of what his companions were made to suffer, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: 'In the land of Abyssinia there is a king under whom no one is wronged, so join his country until Allah grants you relief and a way out of what you are in.'" A long hadith narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwa (2/301), and Ibn Hisham cited it in the Sira in similar wording (1/321).
3 He is: 'Amr ibn al-'As, Abu 'Abd Allah, conqueror of Egypt, one of the great Arabs and their cunning men, and among the people of opinion, resolve and stratagem. In the Jahiliyya he was among the fiercest against Islam, and he embraced Islam during the truce of Hudaybiyya. Born 50 BH, died 43 AH in Cairo at the age of 93 (al-A'lam of al-Zirikli 5/79). Ibn Hisham mentioned in the Sira (1/360) that "Quraysh sent 'Amr ibn al-'As and 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Rabi'a to the Negus to set against the emigrants and the Negus so that he would hand them over to them. 'Amr said: 'By God, I will tell him that they say that Jesus is a servant.'"
4 From Imran ibn Husayn that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Your brother al-Najashi has died, so stand and pray over him." He said: "We stood and formed rows behind him as one does for the dead, and prayed over him as one prays over the dead." Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (4/439, 446), al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (1039) who graded it sound, and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (4/70).

Then the Almighty, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Every soul shall taste death; then to Us you will be returned.﴾ [29:57]

That is, if you were to say—and indeed they did say it in fact—"We have no house or property in Medina, and no sources of livelihood there, and how can we abandon our children and the environment in which we live?", then know that you will inevitably depart from all of this. If you do not leave it while you are alive, you will surely leave it by death; for ﴿every soul shall taste death...﴾ [29:57].

And who knows? Perhaps you will return to your homeland again, just as God said to His Messenger: ﴿Indeed, He who ordained the Qur'an for you will surely bring you back to a return.﴾ [28:85]

And supposing you do not return to it, nothing will harm you, for you will certainly depart from it by death. It is as if the Almighty, blessed and exalted is He, is lightening for them what they encounter in leaving family, homeland, wealth and children.

Moreover, we notice in His saying, glory be to Him, ﴿every soul shall taste death...﴾ [29:57] after ﴿Indeed My earth is spacious...﴾ [29:56] that the thoughts which may occur to the human soul when God prescribes a matter that stirs up these thoughts, such as ﴿Indeed My earth is spacious...﴾ [29:56], and what it arouses in the soul of love of gathering and possession, is accompanied by the matter that calms these thoughts.

﴿Every soul shall taste death...﴾ [29:57]—so that we do not covet the debris of this world, and so that the allure of wealth and the emigration to gather it does not distract us; the end after all that is death, and the loss of everything you have gathered.

This matter is clear in His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this their year...﴾ [9:28]

When God, exalted is He, wanted to end the presence of the polytheists in the Sacred House, He, glory be to Him, knew that the Muslims would reckon the material consequence of preventing the polytheists from entering the Sacred Precinct, and that it would affect their trade and livelihoods in the seasons of commerce and pilgrimage.

Therefore He said immediately after it: ﴿And if you fear poverty (ʿaylah), Allah will enrich you from His bounty...﴾ [9:28] So whenever they recite it in the legislation, they know that God has been apprised of what is in their souls, and has come to them with the answer to it, so that they do not speak of it. This means that the legislation comes to treat all the thoughts of the soul, so that it does not remove you from anything you fear without the legislation bringing what dispels these fears.

[1] Al-Qurtubi mentioned in his tafsir (7/5250), on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to the believers in Mecca when the polytheists harmed them: "Go out to Medina and emigrate, and do not dwell alongside the wrongdoers." They said: "We have no house or property there, nor anyone to feed us or give us drink." Then there was revealed: ﴿And how many a creature does not carry its provision; Allah provides for it and for you...﴾ [29:60].

[2] ʿAylah: poverty. And ʿayyil: a poor person. It is said: ʿala yaʿilu ʿaylah, when he became poor. (Lisan al-ʿArab, root ʿ-y-l)

This is in contrast to: ﴿And indeed, Hell will encompass the disbelievers. On the Day the punishment will cover them from above them and from beneath their feet...﴾ (al-'Ankabut) Mentioning the contrast serves to increase the affliction of the disbelievers, as He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss. And indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire﴾ (al-Infitar).

So bringing together two opposites increases the joy of the believer and increases the regret of the disbeliever.

As for the meaning of ﴿We will surely settle them in the lofty chambers of Paradise...﴾ (al-'Ankabut), it means: We will cause them to descend and We will establish them therein, as in His saying, addressing His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿And [mention] when you left your family in the morning to station the believers at their positions for battle...﴾ (Al 'Imran), meaning: to station them in their places.

The word "Jannah" (garden) is applied to the land that is green, with trees and flowers, in this world, as in His saying: ﴿Would one of you like to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines...﴾ (al-Baqarah).

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have tested them as We tested the people of the garden...﴾ (al-Qalam).

And His saying: ﴿And present to them an example of two men: We gave one of them two gardens of grapevines...﴾ (al-Kahf).

If the garden of this world is in this form of fertility, growth and beauty, and in it are the means of sustenance and luxury, and if this is in the world of causes that we see, then what about what Allah has prepared for His creation in the Hereafter?

Among the wonders of Paradise is that ﴿rivers flow beneath it...﴾ (al-'Ankabut). We know that the rivers of this world flow through banks that contain the water, but in Paradise its rivers flow without banks.

Therefore, when we used to travel to cities of modernity and progress and see the ornaments and luxury of life, I would say to those with me: take a lesson from this bliss, for it is what humans have prepared for humans, so what about what the Lord of humans has prepared for humans?

If you see someone possessing bliss, do not harbor resentment toward him, but rather increase your certainty in Allah, the Exalted, and that what is with Him is greater than this. Do you not see that the Truth, blessed and exalted, when He informs us about Paradise, says: ﴿The example of Paradise which the righteous have been promised...﴾ (Muhammad), making it an example, because the words of language do not convey the meanings that are in Paradise nor describe them.

Therefore the Prophet ﷺ said: "In it is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived" (1). So everything that came about it is not a description of it but merely an example of it. Nevertheless, when He gave us the example of Paradise, He purified the example of its impurities, saying: ﴿In it are rivers of water unaltered (2) and rivers of milk whose taste does not change, and rivers of wine delicious to drinkers, and rivers of purified honey...﴾ (Muhammad). It is sufficient that you know that the bliss of Paradise comes commensurate with the capability and resources of the Bestower, glory be to Him.

As for His saying ﴿abiding therein...﴾ (al-'Ankabut): because bliss, however vast it is and however varied its forms, is spoiled and troubles its possessor that it will end, either by death or by poverty. But the bliss of Paradise is lasting; it does not cease or end, so it does not escape you nor do you escape it, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿neither cut off nor forbidden﴾ (al-Waqi'ah), nothing disturbs it.

So: the winner is the one who prefers the Hereafter over this world, because the bliss of this world is destined to end. Do not say: the age of the world is how many million years; rather its age is the duration of your staying in it. Otherwise, what benefit do you gain from someone else's age?

Furthermore, you enjoy this world according to your capacities and efforts, for the bliss of this world is through causes, but the bliss of the Hereafter is through the Causer, glory be to Him. Therefore you see pure bliss that nothing troubles. In this world you may eat a meal and it causes you troubles and discomforts, such as colic and bloating, in addition to what you dislike while relieving yourself of this meal's waste.

As for the Hereafter, Allah has prepared food for you according to need, such that it leaves no waste, because it was cooked by "Be" from Allah, the Exalted.

Therefore, one of the scholars of the Muslims was asked: "You say that in Paradise one eats and does not defecate, so how is that?" He said: "Why be surprised? Do you not see the fetus in its mother's womb being nourished and growing and not defecating? Because Allah, the Exalted, gives it its nourishment according to its need for growth, so no waste remains from it. If it defecated in its placenta, it would die in its mother's womb."

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿How excellent is the reward of the workers﴾ (al-'Ankabut): yes, yes, this is the reward; because you remained until the age of responsibility reclining in the bounties of Allah without He burdening you with anything, then He gives you for the period of responsibility a reward that does not end and has no limit. So what reward is more generous than this? And it is sufficient that the One who establishes this truth is Allah; He, glory be to Him, is the One who said: ﴿How excellent is the reward of the workers﴾ (al-'Ankabut).

(1) From Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah says: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Recite, if you wish: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes...﴾ (as-Sajdah)." Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3244, 7498), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (2824), Kitab al-Iman.

(2) "Asana al-ma'u ya'sanu": its smell changed, so it is "aasin." (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/20). In al-Tahdhib it is said: it is that which no one drinks because of its stench. (Mentioned by Ibn Manzur in Lisan al-Arab, entry: asana).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 29, verse 59:

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq) (subhanahu) says:

﴿Those who endured patiently and upon their Lord they rely.﴾

This is among the attributes of those who act. ﴿Those who endured patiently...﴾ So do not think that action (al-'amal) is only what happens amid comfortable living and the luxuries of life. The true doer is the one who endures patiently, and the phrase ﴿Those who endured patiently...﴾ indicates that he will be exposed to trial, as He (subhanahu) said: ﴿Do people think that they will be left to say, "We believe," and they will not be tested?﴾

Those who were persecuted and tortured until they were compelled to emigrate with their religion endured patiently. But there is something greater than patience (sabr), because your opponent may be patient toward you, so the matter requires musabara (steadfast mutual endurance). Therefore He (subhanahu) said: ﴿Be patient and vie in patience...﴾ The meaning of "sabarahu" is: he competed with him in patience.

Patience (sabr) is exercised against the calamities of life so that you may bear them, against the hardship of obligations, and against the enticement of sin. They say: "sabr 'ala al-ta'a" (patience in obedience) and "sabr 'an al-ma'asi" (patience in refraining from sin). The poet spoke truly when he said:
"Be a man like a molar that settles in its place,
chewing, unconcerned whether it is sweet or bitter."

So the meaning of ﴿Those who endured patiently...﴾ is patience over harm, ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾, that is, regarding provision (rizq). The emigrants, at the time of their migration, were concerned about the matter of provision, saying: "We have no house there, no property, and so on." So He (subhanahu) wished to reassure their hearts concerning the matter of provision, and said: ﴿And upon their Lord they rely.﴾

The One who created you must provide your sustenance. Among the wonders of provision is that your provision is not what you own, but what you actually benefit from. You may own something and have it stolen from you; food may be cooked for you and you do not eat it; more precisely, you may eat it and it does not reach your stomach; it may reach the stomach and you vomit it; and more than that, the nourishment may be turned into blood which then drains from you through a wound or the sting of a mosquito or otherwise, because that is not your provision, but the provision of another creature.

You are amazed when you see the crocodile, for example, despite its enormity and people's fear of it. Yet you see that after it eats, it comes out onto dry land, where it opens its mouth to small birds, and they take on the task of cleaning the food remnants between its teeth. You see complete harmony between them and positive cooperation. When the crocodile, for example, is exposed to an attack by the hunter, the bird makes a particular sound that the crocodile understands, and it hastens to flee.

So consider: from where does this bird obtain its strength? And where did God hide its provision? Therefore they say: "Whoever splits it, God creates its provision" (al-lee shaqqahu khalaqa laqqahu).

We have previously given an example of the particularity of provision with the fetus in its mother's womb. When the mother conceives the fetus, the blood turns into nourishment for the child; if she does not conceive, this blood is discharged to be thrown away without the mother benefiting from it. Why? Because it is the provision of the fetus, and not her provision.

Therefore, we find that the verse after it says (1):

﴿And how many a creature does not carry its provision; God provides for it and for you, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾

1 Occasion of revelation: Ibn 'Umar said: "We went out with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) until he entered some of the orchards of the Ansar, and he began to pick dates and eat. He said: 'O Ibn 'Umar, why do you not eat?' I said: 'I have no desire for it, O Messenger of God.' He said: 'But I have a desire for it. This is the fourth morning that I have not tasted food. Had I wished, I would have asked my Lord and He would have given me like the kingdom of Chosroes and Caesar. So how will you be, O Ibn 'Umar, when you remain among a people who store the provision of their year and whose certainty is weak?' He said: 'By God, we had not moved until this verse was revealed: ﴿And how many a creature does not carry its provision...﴾ (al-'Ankabut).'" Narrated by al-Wahidi al-Naysaburi in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 196). Al-Qurtubi said in his Tafsir (7/5250): "This is weak; what weakens it is that he (peace be upon him) used to store his family's provision for a year, as agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim, and the Companions did so while they were the mighty ones and people of certainty, and the Imams after them from the God-fearing who rely upon God."

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 29, verse 60:

He, glory be to Him, wishes to reassure His creatures about their provision, so He says: ﴿And how many a creature does not carry its provision! Allah provides for it and for you, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ (al-'Ankabut 29:60). "Ka-ayyin" has several meanings, such as the interrogative "kam" (how many) when you say to someone who denies your kindness: "How much have I done good to you?" meaning: very much. Likewise in ﴿And how many a creature...﴾ (29:60), meaning: many. As in ﴿And how many a prophet has fought, and with him were many devoted followers (rabbiyyun). They did not weaken for what befell them...﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:146).

The "dabbah" (creature) is that which crawls on the earth, and what is meant is every living being that moves. You might say: the ant, for example, we do not hear its footstep on the earth, so is it counted among the creatures? Yes, it has a footstep on the earth, but you do not hear it. The One who created it hears its footstep, because the One who accepts smallness accepts greatness, but you do not have the instrument of hearing.

The proof of this is that a person who suffers from weak hearing, for example, is advised by the doctor to fit a hearing aid, and he hears. Likewise with glasses for sight. So everything has a visible or audible effect, but what matters is the instrument that hears or sees. For this reason, when they want to exaggerate, they say: "So-and-so hears the footstep of an ant."

The meaning of ﴿how many a creature does not carry its provision﴾ is: not every creature carries its provision. Many of them carry no provision, yet they eat and live. It may mean: because they are unable to carry it, or they are able to carry it but do not do so. For example, lice and fleas, which multiply with neglect of personal hygiene, do they carry provision? The mosquito, which, though weak, feeds on the blood of a proud, tyrannical human, and the microbe that destroys a human... and so on: these do not carry their provision.

As for the donkey, for example, although it is able to carry, it does not carry its provision; so you see that when it is satisfied it stores nothing, and perhaps tramples the remaining food or urinates on it. Likewise all animals; indeed they say: among creatures, only humans, mice and ants know storing.

God placed storing in these creatures for a wisdom and to demonstrate the absoluteness of His power, and that storing among these creatures is not a deficiency on the part of the Creator, glory be to Him, in that He made some creatures unable to carry their provision; rather, He creates for them means that you are powerless to grasp.

You may contemplate ant colonies and their wonders. Researchers in this field have observed that if you leave a piece of food, for example, an ant comes and circles around it, then departs and sends a number of ants able to carry this piece; and if you double the weight of this piece, the number of ants doubles.

Thus it is a kingdom of extreme organization, precision and specialization. What is more amazing is that they observed the ants bringing out a small white powder in front of the nests; when they examined it, they found it to be the substance that causes the grain to sprout, so that it does not germinate, lest the nest collapse on them. Glory be to the One who created and proportioned, and who decreed and guided.

More amazing still, they found the ant splitting a coriander seed into four parts, because half a coriander seed can germinate on its own, so they divide the half.

Thus many creatures do not carry their provision. ﴿Allah provides for it and for you...﴾ (29:60). He mentions the creatures first in the context of provision, then joins "you" to them. So we are conjoined with the creatures in provision, although man is the origin, the honored one, and the whole world was created for him and to serve him. Yet He, glory be to Him, did not say: "We provide for you and them." Why? They said: because you might think they cannot manage until We provide for them before you.

The orientalists who take the Qur'an without the Arabic linguistic faculty have objected to His saying: ﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty...﴾ (al-Isra 17:31), and His saying: ﴿And do not kill your children because of poverty...﴾ (al-An'am 6:151).

They say: which of the two is more eloquent? And if one of them is eloquent, the other is not.

This objection arises from their assumption that the two verses have the same meaning, whereas they differ. In the first, ﴿for fear of poverty﴾, poverty does not exist here and they fear it. But in the second, ﴿because of poverty﴾, poverty actually exists. So they differ in the opening, and likewise they differ in the closing.

In the first He said: ﴿We provide for them and for you...﴾ (17:31), because poverty does not exist and you are not preoccupied with your own provision, so He began with the children. But in the second He said: ﴿We provide for you and for them...﴾ (6:151), and placed the parents first, because poverty exists and a person is first preoccupied with providing for himself before providing for his children.

Thus each verse has its meaning and harmony between its opening and its closing. The important thing is to contemplate the language of the Qur'an and understand from God His intended meaning.

As for His saying: ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ (29:60), He chose here "All-Hearing, All-Knowing" because the Truth, glory be to Him, has *qayyumiyyah* (sustaining authority) over His creation. He did not create them and then leave them to laws; rather He created the creation while He, glory be to Him, stands over it in His sustaining authority. Therefore He says, explaining His care for His handiwork: ﴿Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him﴾ (2:255), meaning: "My servants, sleep with your eyes full, for your Lord does not sleep."

The fitting of "All-Hearing" here is that when hunger stirs a person, he may cry out or do something that shows he is hungry. It is as if He says: "I did not make you so."

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?", they would surely say, "Allah." So how are they deluded away?﴾ [29:61]

He, exalted, says to those whom the Qur'an verse that was revealed upon the Messenger of Allah does not suffice, and who demand from him other signs: He says to them, "Allah has already placed the signs for you in the cosmos before He sent the messengers, signs indicating the miraculous nature in the heavens and in the earth. So is there any among you who can create anything of them, however small?"

The creation of the heavens and the earth is an unending cosmic miracle. Why, then, do you demand more signs? Allah made them only to demonstrate the truthfulness of the messengers in conveying the message from Allah, so that people would believe in them.

Therefore He, glorified, says in response to them: ﴿This is the creation of Allah; so show me what those other than Him have created...﴾ [31:11]. So the creation of the heavens, the earth, the sun and the moon is a miracle for the whole world, and especially for the disbelievers in it.

This matter of creation is so clear that no one can deny it, as we have already explained. Therefore they say here, in answering the question, ﴿Allah...﴾ [29:61]. This acknowledgment from them obliges the believer to praise Allah for it, so he says: "Praise be to Allah that they have acknowledged this truth themselves. Praise be to Allah, who made them utter the word of truth and manifested the proof that nullifies their disbelief."

As for His saying, glorified is He, ﴿So how are they deluded away?﴾ [29:61], it means: how, after this acknowledgment, do they turn away from Allah, and turn away from the truth?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 29, verse 62:

﴿Allah extends provision (yabsutu al-rizq) to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for whom He wills﴾ (al-'Ankabut). "Yabsutu" means He widens it, and "yaqdiru" means He constricts it.

The affliction of people in this matter is that they interpret provision (rizq) only as wealth, whereas in reality provision is everything from which a person benefits. Knowledge is provision, forbearance is provision, authority is provision, humility is provision, and mastery of one's craft is provision, and so on.

Allah, glorified is He, extends provision to whomever He wills and restricts it for whomever He wills. The one for whom it is restricted is in need of the one for whom it is extended. Likewise, He extends provision in one thing and restricts it in another. So He may extend to a person in intellect, for example, and restrict him in wealth.

It is as though the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, has scattered the gifts of faculties among His creatures and did not gather them all in one person. We have already explained that the total of faculties among everyone is ultimately equal, so whoever is extended in one thing is restricted in another, so that society remains bound by the bond of need, and people do not become independent of one another, and so that gifts are complementary among people, supporting one another rather than opposing one another.

Therefore, when the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, extends provision to one servant and measures it for another, this does not mean that He loves the first and dislikes the second. And if you look at all the aspects of provision and the angles of giving, you will find them equal.

When we reflect on His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others in degrees...﴾ (al-Zukhruf 32), then which is the one raised up, and which is the one raised above? Everyone is raised in the aspect of his specialty, and raised above in an aspect other than his specialty. Therefore, all are equal.

We have already given an example of this matter. We said: a great man who lives in a palace needs the simple worker who keeps the restroom in order and saves him from the foul smell that he finds distasteful. So he goes to him himself and seeks him out, and perhaps goes to his place of work and brings him in his luxurious car, and even begs him if he is busy.

In this case, you see the worker raised above the great pasha, and the elevation appears only at the time of need for the one who is elevated.

Also, if there were no rich and poor among people, who would handle our affairs in the field, in the factory, in the market, and so on? These matters must be built on need, not on favor. Therefore, if you wish to compare among creatures, do not belittle anyone, for he may be granted an advantage over you in some gift, and then you will be in need of him.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And if you asked them, "Who sends down water from the sky and with it gives life to the earth after its death?" they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "Praise be to Allah." But most of them do not reason.﴾ [29:63]

Here too they said "Allah," because the sending down of rain from the sky and the giving of life to the earth by it after its death is a clear cosmic sign that no one has disclaimed. It is established for Allah, the Exalted, and no one denies it, not even the disbelievers. So if you put this question to them, "they would surely say, 'Allah...'" [29:63]. Therefore, the Truth, glory be to Him, commands us to say after this acknowledgment, "Say, 'Praise be to Allah...'" [29:63], who made them speak the truth and established the proof against them, "But most of them do not reason" [29:63], because they acknowledged the signs of Allah in the creation of the universe, yet still disbelieved in Him.

Life: we know it as whatever exists in a human being, at the highest level of existence, of sensation and movement; when his sensation and movement end, he no longer has life. This life is described here with three attributes: worldly (dunya), frivolity (lahw), and play (la'b). The word "dunya" indicates that its counterpart is "ulya" (higher). So when you hear this description, "the worldly life," know that this description only came to distinguish it from another life, which shares with it being a life granted by God, except that it is a higher life. This higher life is what our Lord, may He be blessed and exalted, called "the Last Abode."

Although we have known the worldly life as sensation and movement in a human being, the reality, upon precise examination, is that everything in existence has a life suited to its function. The evidence is His saying, may He be exalted, when He ends this life: ﴿Everything perishes except His Face...﴾ (al-Qasas 28:88).

So whatever is called a "thing" must necessarily be subject to perishing, and perishing is opposed by life, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿That whoever perishes might perish upon clear evidence, and whoever lives might live upon clear evidence...﴾ (al-Anfal 8:42).

So life is the opposite of perishing. However, you know life in yourself through sensation and movement, and likewise life exists in every thing according to its nature. Even in inanimate matter there is life, which we observe in that a mountain is composed of many kinds of stones, which over time develop from stones into other things higher and more precious than stones. And since this change occurs in them, there must be in them life and an interaction that we do not perceive.

So, everything has life, but the pitfall is that we want a life like the life within us. I recall that when we were in the stage of education, we were told: there is a thing called the magnet, and a process called magnetization. When you magnetize a piece of iron, it gains the ability to attract another piece in a certain direction. So, in iron there is life, movement and interaction, but you do not have the instrument with which to perceive this movement, and within it are internal particles that are not perceived by the naked eye, which are then aligned by magnetization toward a specific direction.

And read His saying: ﴿They will say to their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" They will say, "God has given us speech, who gives speech to everything..."﴾ (Fussilat 41:21). So the limbs themselves have life, and they have speech and discourse, but we do not perceive it, because their life is not like our life. If you were to observe, for example, a plastic plate or cup, you would find its color changing over time, and the change of color in it indicates the presence of life and movement among its particles. Had there been no life in it, it would be solid like glass, not subject to any change of color.

And the Truth, may He be blessed and exalted, describes the Last Abode as ﴿the Living (al-Hayawan)...﴾ (al-Ankabut 29:64). There is a difference between hayat (life) and hayawan (true life). Hayat is this life we live in the world, which individuals live and plants live, and then it returns to death and annihilation. As for hayawan, it refers to the higher life in the Hereafter, because it is an enduring life, a real life.

And the Truth, glorified and exalted, gave us an image of the worldly life, the material life, in His saying about Adam: ﴿So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit...﴾ (al-Hijr 15:29). Thus Adam was created from clay, shaped, and breathed into from His Spirit, may He be exalted, and material life stirred within him.

But there is another life more exalted than this, of which Allah says: ﴿O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life...﴾ (al-Anfal 8:24). How would He address them with this when they were alive? It must be that the intended meaning is another life, other than this material life: the life of the spirit, of values, and of the method that the Messenger of Allah brought.

Therefore He named the method a "spirit": ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit (rawh) from Our command...﴾ (al-Shura 42:52). And He named the angel who descended with it a "spirit": ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down...﴾ (al-Shu'ara 26:193).

So: ﴿And indeed, the Last Abode—that is the Living (al-hayawan)...﴾ (al-Ankabut 29:64), meaning: the true life, which does not escape you nor you it, whose bliss does not part from you, and which nothing spoils for you. Just as enjoyment in the world is according to your capabilities and means, in the Hereafter bliss is according to the capacity of the Bestower, may He be glorified and exalted.

Then comes the description of the world as frivolity and play, and these are two movements of the human limbs, but it is a movement whose only aim is movement itself, without a purpose beyond it. Therefore we say of one who does a deed with no benefit, "abath" (futility).

So: frivolity (lahw) and play (la'b) are both futility, but they differ in another respect. Play is movement with no benefit, but it does not divert you from a duty that yields benefit, like a child when he plays; play does not divert him from anything. So play belongs to one who has not reached maturity. As for the adult who is accountable, play for him is called lahw, because he was charged with duty and abandoned what he was charged with for what he was not charged with, and it distracted him from duty. From this comes "lahw al-hadith" (idle talk) (1).

So His saying: ﴿And this worldly life is nothing but frivolity and play...﴾ (al-Ankabut 29:64), meaning: if it is stripped of the other life, the life of values that come through following the method.

And His saying: ﴿If only they knew (law kanu ya'lamun)﴾ (al-Ankabut 29:64) may be a conditional clause, meaning: their knowledge was impossible; or it may be an expression of wish, meaning: would that they knew this reality, the reality of the world and the reality of the Hereafter; for if they knew it, they would have turned to the method of their Lord to attain all this enduring bounty, and would have taken the path of faith instead of the path of disbelief. So the meaning is that they did not know.

(1) God says: ﴿And among people is one who buys idle talk to mislead from the way of Allah without knowledge...﴾ (Luqman 31:6). Al-Firyabi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿...among people is one who buys idle talk...﴾ that he said: "False speech, which is singing and the like." And ﴿to mislead from the way of Allah without knowledge﴾ he said: "The recitation of the Qur'an and the remembrance of Allah." It was revealed concerning a man from Quraysh who bought a singing slave-girl. (Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 6/504). In another report from him, it is al-Nadr ibn al-Harith.

Then the Lord, glorified is He, says:

﴿So when they board the ship, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion. But when He delivers them to the land, at once they associate others with Him.ﴩﷺ﴾

The context here shifts us from speaking about the reality of both this world and the Hereafter to a discussion of the ship (al-Fulk). What is the connection between them?

The Speaker here is Allah, the One who places everything in its proper place. It should not escape you that you must reflect upon the words of Allah to understand His intent. Allah does not want us to be content with the outward meaning of the Qur'an alone, but to delve deeply into its understanding and contemplation, and to examine its true contents: ﴿Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an...﴾ (82) (an-Nisa').

The connection here is that the preceding verse came to establish that this world is a realm of amusement and play, of no benefit if it is far removed from the method of Allah, and if it takes no account of another life, which is the true life, al-Hayawan (the life of the Hereafter). So it is incumbent upon the intelligent person to be keen on the Hereafter and to work for it by following the method of Allah in this world.

Therefore: this world is not an end in itself, but a means. And you, O one who has turned away from the method of your Lord, have made this world your goal. If this world is the goal, how base a goal it is! Rather, make it a means to the Hereafter and a field for the abode of al-Hayawan. Likewise the situation with the ship: it is a means that conveys you to a purpose and a goal, and it is not an end in itself.

﴿So when they board the ship, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion...﴾ (65) (al-'Ankabut). Al-Fulk means the ship, and it is used for both the singular and the plural. Allah says: ﴿And he was constructing the ship...﴾ (38) (Hud), and His words: ﴿They call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion...﴾ (22) (Yunus). It is clear from the context that this is not a call of praise, such as their saying, for example, ﴿Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we were not capable of it﴾ (13) (az-Zukhruf). Rather, it is the call of necessity, after they have been exposed to a severe calamity and destruction from which their means cannot save them, as evidenced by His words after it: ﴿But when He delivers them to the land, at once they associate others with Him﴾ (65) (al-'Ankabut).

This gives us that they boarded the ship, and when they were exposed to destruction and their means were exhausted, they called upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion (1).

In another scene the Qur'an says: ﴿Until, when you are in the ship and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice therein, there comes a storm wind and the waves come to them from everywhere, and they assume they are encompassed, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion: "If You should save us from this, we will surely be among the grateful."﴾ (22) (Yunus).

The meaning of ﴿they are encompassed...﴾ (22) (Yunus) is: there is for them no escape, no refuge, and no recourse to which they can turn, except to turn to Allah with sincere supplication and certain faith that they have no refuge but Allah. They had been, at the beginning of the journey, rejoicing in their vessel and delighted with it, and at that time Allah was not in their minds. Rather, when their stratagems were exhausted, they returned to the Truth, for the moment does not admit of evasion.

Because a person ordinarily does not deceive himself: even the disbeliever, when the means of salvation constrict him, turns instinctively to Allah, the Truth, and forgets his deities and idols besides Allah; for he does not delude his own self entirely, and does not persist at that time in the lie of the gods and idols.

Therefore: ﴿they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion...﴾ (65) (al-'Ankabut) is a sincere call, with firm certainty in the true God, a call untainted by any trace of shirk, outward or hidden. Nothing benefits at this time except Allah, the one truly worthy of worship.

We have previously clarified this matter with an example from our real life. We said: the barber used to play the role of the doctor in the village, and he had among the people the same status the doctor has at a time when there were no doctors. When the faculty of medicine produced doctors who spread out into the villages, the barber was the first to attack the doctor, because he competed with him for his livelihood and diverted people away from him; therefore he would disparage the doctor and cast doubt on his expertise and abilities.

But when his own son fell ill, his temperature rose, and he feared for him, he said to his wife: "Wait until the darkness of the night, so I can take him to the doctor" — meaning: in the heedlessness of people.

So the human being by nature does not deceive himself, and does not surrender himself when the matter becomes serious. Within him is an innate faith (fitrah imaniyyah), which, if it is purified within the human self, finds in the end only one power, the power of Allah.

Even the atheists, when the means constrict them, say: "O Lord, O Allah," saying it spontaneously, without passing through the reason with which they denied the existence of Allah. This means that the innate faith may be veiled and nullified by human accidents, but when the human accidents fall asleep and dissolve due to some event, the innate faith appears on the surface, inspiring you without your awareness.

Therefore we notice in His words, glorified is He: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified"...﴾ (172) (al-A'raf). They testified because they were still in the world of the atoms (alam al-dharr), where human accidents do not control them: ﴿lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were of this unaware" (172), or say, "Only our fathers associated others with Allah before, and we were descendants after them..."﴾ (173) (al-A'raf).

Allah created man as His khalifah (vicegerent) on earth, and subjected to him this whole universe. If he remains upholding this method and stops at the limit of vicegerency, he succeeds; but if he thinks he is the original owner of the universe, he will be disappointed and lose. Yet Allah, who created him, knows the accidents within him, for He is his Creator and Maker. Therefore He directs him: "You are My vicegerent on My earth, and you must look at what is asked of you and fulfil it, or else your life will be corrupted and you will clash with others, for you are not alone in it, and in order to be in harmony with others you must follow My method, within the framework of the laws of the One who made you His vicegerent."

Then He alerts him from another side: He says, "You, O human being, know that the means will respond to you. Beware of thinking that you have power over them, or that you have status and greatness, so that you forget that you are a vicegerent. Therefore He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Nay! Indeed, man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ (6–7) (al-'Alaq). Beware, when matters are accomplished for you and the means obey you: ﴿Indeed, to your Lord is the return﴾ (8) (al-'Alaq). Then there will confront you events that your means cannot repel, and you will find no return except to Me."

And how does man transgress when Allah has given him an overflow of His perfection, given him a power from His power and a knowledge from His knowledge... etc. If you look simply at Allah's bounties upon you, you will find them many. By Allah, what do you do if you wish to rise from your place, or to move your hand or foot? Nothing: as soon as you intend, your limbs respond to you, obeying you without your knowing how.

We have previously compared the movement of a person with the movement of an excavator, for example, and how it needs complex operations, each movement of which has its own special switch that performs it. So what would you do if you wished to perform such movements?

By mere intention, the limb responds to you, as though within you there is an overflow of His words: ﴿Indeed, His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ (82) (Ya-Sin). If you act by merely willing, why do you not believe this regarding Allah, blessed and exalted is He?

But this movement and the responsiveness of your limbs is not inherent in you; your Creator can take it from you, so that you wish to raise your hand and cannot. You are under His sustaining authority, exalted is He; He has not given you of His attributes and then left you. Our Lord, glorified is He, warns us: when you become self-sufficient, you will transgress; so be mindful that to your Lord is the return.

Then He draws our attention now to another matter before we encounter the dangers: ﴿And if Allah touches you with adversity...﴾ (107) (Yunus). So do not weary yourself, going here or there, for ﴿there is no remover of it except Him﴾ (107) (Yunus).

This is my advice to you, because you are My creation, and I love that My creation be upon the highest perfection. So if harm touches you that you cannot repel by your means, then take refuge at the door of your Lord.

These are three matters or counsels we present to you before events and calamities befall you: if you become self-sufficient, you will transgress; that to your Lord is the return; and if harm touches you, and you have no means to repel it, then there is none to turn to except Allah. The God who alerts us to dangers so that we may avoid them is a Merciful God.

So then: you love life, and when events and calamities befell you in the ship, you feared death and called upon Allah for salvation. You are keen on the life of this world. So why do you not believe in Allah, so that you may attain another life that is more enduring and more lasting? The way to it is through faith and certainty, and through the method of Allah in ﴿do﴾ and ﴿do not do﴾.

This is a matter the Qur'an mentioned, and the reality of life has confirmed it, and events have come as it said. The matter: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting or standing...﴾ (12) (Yunus). "Man" means man in general: the believer and the disbeliever. ﴿Or sitting or standing...﴾ (12) (Yunus) means: in all conditions. So when danger came to him and harm struck him, he called upon Allah in whatever state he was.

These states represent stages of the comfort of the self. For example, when you are walking while carrying something, when you tire, first you put that load down, then you stop walking to rest; if the tiredness is greater, you sit, and otherwise you lie down on your side.

When you are standing, the weight of the whole body is carried on the two feet, so the rest is less; in sitting, the weight of the body is distributed over the hips and the buttocks; in lying down, the weight of half the body is distributed on its other half, so the rest is greater. In light of this we understand that Allah responds to you when you call upon Him standing, or sitting, or on your side.

And strange is the state of man: when Allah rescues him from what he fears and removes harm from him, he returns again, wronging himself: ﴿But when We remove from him his harm, he passes on as if he had never called Us to a harm that touched him...﴾ (12) (Yunus).

In another scene the Qur'an says regarding this matter: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance; then when He bestows upon him a favour from Him, he forgets what he had been calling to before...﴾ (8) (az-Zumar). "And sets up rivals to Allah..." (8) (az-Zumar). He says: "The favour is due to so-and-so, and I sought help from so-and-so, and I turned to so-and-so."

We notice that the speech in these verses is about the individual person, and a person when he humbles himself to Allah is seen by no one; the matter is between him and his Lord. But the Truth, glorified is He, wishes to expose people to one another, so He says in another place: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish except Him...﴾ (67) (al-Isra').

Thus He mentions the group in order to expose them before one another, because a person conceals himself; so the wisdom of the plural here is that the sight of people may itself be a barrier against evil. For example, in the season of Hajj you see the great and the middling and the lowly alike in the circumambulation, and one of them stands weeping at al-Multazam. When the man of rank or position, in his own country he is who he is, sees you weeping in this situation, when he knows that you have seen him weeping, he humbles himself to you and does not look down on you afterward.

So when the Truth, glorified is He, warns us against returning to disobedience after He has removed harm from us, He is in fact giving us the protective vaccine in a form that occurs in reality, as though He, exalted is He, is saying to us: "Take care, and know that you are exposed through the Book of Allah regarding what you do in your lives; each of you must know that he is watched from eternity, and his thoughts are recorded upon him; for the meaning of the Qur'an is the Truth, which does not change, and if Allah has said something in it, it must come to pass as Allah has reported it."

(1) Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned, from Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Makkah, he fled from it. When he boarded the sea to go to Abyssinia, the ship was tossed about with them, and its people said: "O people, make your supplication sincerely to your Lord, for none saves here except Him." Ikrimah said: "By Allah, if none saves in the sea except Him, then none saves on land either except Him. O Allah, to You I make a pledge: if I come out, I will surely go and place my hand in the hand of Muhammad, and I will surely find him kind and merciful." And so it was. (Cited by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir, 3/421.)

The lam in "li-yakfurū... (66)" (al-'Ankabūt) is not the lam of causation (lam al-ta'līl), because disbelief was not their aim; when they returned after Allah had delivered them, they only reverted to their original state [1]. So the lam here is the lam of command (lam al-amr) [2], as if you said: "Thumma yā Zayd, wa-liqum 'Amr." The sign of the lam of command is that it is quiescent (sakin), and here it is kasra-vowelled because it stands at the beginning of the speech, where one does not begin with a quiescent letter; and if we had placed a letter before it, its quiescence would have become apparent.

Its like occurs in His saying: ﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾ (al-Hajj, 29).

And His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿Let the one of wealth spend from his wealth, and whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him...﴾ (al-Talaq, 7).

The evidence that it is the lam of command is the quiescence of the lam after it in the reading of one who reads it quiescent, and in ﴿And let them enjoy...﴾ (al-'Ankabūt, 66), and in His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿So they will come to know﴾ (al-'Ankabūt, 66). There is a difference in futurity between sa- and sawfa: had he said "fa-sa-ya'lamūn," it would have indicated a threat in the near future, that punishment would befall them in this world. But "sawfa" indicates the distant future, so it encompasses the threat in this world and in the Hereafter; it covers the whole of time. This is because at the beginning of the matter the Muslims were weak, unable to protect themselves, and they went to the Prophet (ﷺ) asking him to seek Allah's help for them. Had he then said in threatening the disbelievers "fa-sa-ya'lamūn," it would not have been appropriate; rather, he gave the widest span to the threat, saying: ﴿So they will come to know﴾ (al-'Ankabūt, 66).

They said: "What then is for us if we do so?" It was possible for him to say to them: "You will inherit the earth," or "the call of Allah will spread through you and you will triumph over your enemy." But such promises some of them might see, and some might die before they are fulfilled, so they would see none of them. Therefore he mentioned to them a reward in which all are equal, whether they live or die, saying: "For you is Paradise" [3].

Also, when he turns them away from the world of people toward a matter that is also in this world, it is a losing bargain. Rather, he wanted to turn them away from the world of people toward something greater than what is in the world of people, and there is nothing greater than the world of people except Paradise.

And the Companion whom the Prophet (ﷺ) informed that Paradise is the reward of the martyr, and who was chewing a date in his mouth, said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there not between me and Paradise only that I be killed in the way of Allah?" He said: "Yes." So he threw away the dates and hastened to the battlefield, seeking to hasten this reward [4].

Thus: "sawfa" is suitable for the whole future time, whereas "sa-" is for the near; therefore the Qur'an uses it in matters of this world, as in His saying: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves...﴾ (Fussilat, 53).

This showing extends from the time of the Messenger of Allah until the Hour is established. Every day, in the phenomena of the cosmos, there are matters that indicate the power of Allah, the Exalted; the future secrets of Allah in His creation never end, except with the greatest secret in the Hereafter. In the time of the Messenger of Allah He said ﴿We will show them...﴾ (Fussilat, 53), and it will remain so: ﴿We will show them...﴾ (Fussilat, 53), until the Hour is established.

We note that the mushafs still have a dispute in their script until now: here in ﴿And let them enjoy...﴾ (al-'Ankabūt, 66) you find a kasra under the lam, although it is quiescent, and this means that the Book of Allah prevails, and there is no one who can diminish it.

I recall that our master, the shaykh al-Baqi [5], may Allah be pleased with him and reward him with the best of rewards on behalf of Islam, compiled the indexed concordance of the words of the Noble Qur'an and sought to count its words, especially the word of majesty (Allah), for whose sake he compiled this book. Nevertheless, he forgot the word of majesty in the basmala, and began from ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ (al-Fatiha, 2); therefore the count was one short for him [6]. This is only because the Book of Allah is greater and too vast to be encompassed.

[1] Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (3/421): "This lam is called by many of the people of Arabic, tafsir and usul scholars lam al-'aqibah (the lam of consequence), because they do not intend it; and there is no doubt that it is so with respect to them. As for its relation to Allah's decree over them and His making them to be so, it is lam al-ta'lil (the lam of causation)."

[2] Jamal al-Din Ibn Hisham al-Ansari said in Mughni al-Labib (1/186), 'Isa al-Babi al-Halabi edition: "As for ﴿that they may disbelieve in what We have given them, and that they may enjoy...﴾ (al-'Ankabūt, 66), both lams are possible: the lam of causation, in which case what follows them is in the subjunctive, and the lam of threat, in which case it is jussive; the second is fixed for the second lam in the reading of one who makes it quiescent, which tends toward the first lam also being so; and supporting this is that after them is ﴿So they will come to know﴾ (al-'Ankabūt, 66)."

[3] On the authority of Abu Mas'ud al-Badri, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) set out, and with him al-'Abbas, to the seventy of the Ansar at al-'Aqabah beneath the tree, and he said: 'Let your speaker speak and not prolong the sermon, for there are spies among the polytheists, and if they know of you they will expose you.' Their speaker, who was Abu Umamah, said: 'Ask, O Muhammad, of your Lord whatever you wish, then ask for yourself and your companions whatever you wish, then inform us what reward we will have from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and from you if we do that.' He said: 'I ask of my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, that you worship Him and associate nothing with Him; and I ask for myself and my companions that you shelter us, help us, and protect us from what you protect yourselves from.' They said: 'What then is for us if we do that?' He said: 'For you is Paradise.' They said: 'Then that is for you.'" Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (4/120).

[4] Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (1899), and likewise al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4046), from the hadith of Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him) "that a man said to the Prophet on the day of Uhud..." the hadith. Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani said in al-Fath (7/354): "I have not identified his name."

[5] He is Muhammad Fu'ad 'Abd al-Baqi, born in a village in al-Qalyubiyya in Egypt in 1882 CE, raised in Cairo, and educated in some of its schools; then he worked as a translator from French at the Agricultural Bank (1905–1933) and devoted himself to authorship. He died in Cairo in 1968 CE at the age of 86 (al-A'lam of al-Zirikli 6/333).

[6] Muhammad Fu'ad 'Abd al-Baqi counted (1125) occurrences in the Qur'an in which the word of majesty appears in the genitive, beginning with His saying: ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ (al-Fatiha, 2).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 29, verse 67:

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq) subhanahu says:

﴿Have they not seen that We made a sanctuary secure, while people are snatched away from all around them? Do they then believe in falsehood and disbelieve in the blessing of Allah?﴾ (67)

(ra'a) We have said: it comes as a visual seeing (basariyya), and it comes in the sense of knowing ('ilm). An example of the latter is our saying in debate, for instance, "I see (ara) that in such-and-such matter is such-and-such." And they say: "And the seeing of dreams is not like the knowing of [what we know]..." And you find in the Qur'anic style speech about seeing addressed to one who did not witness the matter, as in His saying, glorified is He, addressing the Prophet (ﷺ):
﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾ (105:1) (al-Fil)

It is known that the Prophet did not see what happened concerning the affair of the elephant, because he was born in that year; so "ra'a" here means "'alima" (knew). But why did He shift from "alam taʿlam" (have you not known) to "alam tara" (have you not seen)? They said: because the speaker here is Allah, the Exalted, so it is as if He says to His Prophet (ﷺ): if I inform you of something, then my informing you of it is truer than your seeing.

He, subhanahu, says: ﴿Have they not seen that We made a sanctuary secure, while people are snatched away from all around them...﴾ (29:67) (al-'Ankabut). So the sanctuary is secure despite the terror it suffered before Islam, when Abraha frightened it, and in modern times when Juhayman frightened it, and throughout the ages there have occurred transgressions in the sanctuary which in appearance contradict this security.

And we say: the word ﴿sanctuary secure...﴾ (29:67) (al-'Ankabut) in the Qur'an, with respect to the Ka'ba, has three applications. Those who lived in it at the time these verses were revealed see it as a secure sanctuary, and this security has been bestowed upon them since the supplication of our master Abraham, peace be upon him.

When he supplicated his Lord: ﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation by Your sacred House...﴾ (14:37) (Ibrahim), it was an empty place, with no life in it and uninhabited, meaning there were no means of life in it. A person does not build or settle except where he finds a place in which he is secure for himself and where all the means of his life are available.

Therefore Abraham supplicated his Lord to make this place a secure town (balad), meaning one fit to be a town, so he said: ﴿My Lord, make this a secure town﴾ (2:126) (al-Baqara).

Here "balad" is indefinite, meaning: any town, whether for believers or disbelievers. When Allah answered him and made it a town like any town where the means of life are available, he supplicated again: ﴿My Lord, make this city secure...﴾ (14:35) (Ibrahim), i.e., this which has become a town, I want it to have a distinction over all towns, and a security greater than the security of any other town, a security specific to it, not the general security shared by all towns. Why? Because in it is Your House.

Therefore a person may find in it the killer of his father, and he is not touched until he leaves; the offender is secure if he enters the sanctuary, but the means of life are restricted for him until he leaves, so that people do not dare against the House of Allah and corrupt its security.
