From this specific security is that game is not hunted in it, its trees are not cut, and its inhabitant is not terrified.

It is as if the Truthful, glorified and exalted, says to the polytheists: Why do you not believe in this religion which has made for you a secure town, while people are snatched away from around you? Why do you not respect your presence in this security which Allah has bestowed upon you?

And it is strange of them that they say, as the Qur'an relates of them: ﴿And they say: If we follow the guidance with you, we would be snatched away from our land...﴾ (28:57) (al-Qasas). How, when We protected you in the days when you were polytheists worshipping idols? Would We leave you after you believe with the Messenger of Allah?

The story of this security began with the incident of the elephant, when Abraha came to demolish the House of Allah and divert people to a house he had built in Yemen, so Allah repelled their plot and made them like chewed-up straw (1). When we read this surah connected to what follows it, the reason for this security and this protection becomes clear to us. Read:

﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant? Did He not make their plot into misguidance? And He sent upon them birds in flocks, striking them with stones of hard clay, and He made them like eaten straw.﴾ (105:1-5) (al-Fil) Why?
﴿For the accustomed security of the Quraysh, their accustomed security of the caravan of winter and summer.﴾ (106:1-2) (Quraysh)

The reason that Allah made them like eaten straw is ﴿for the accustomed security of the Quraysh﴾ (106:1), because the lam in "li-ilaf" (for the security) is for causation, and it is at the beginning of the speech. So the reason Allah did not enable the enemies to demolish the House was so that the Quraysh would retain their awe and their standing among the Arabs, and their awe is tied to the House which people come to from every place.

This standing secures the trade of the Quraysh in the winter journey to Yemen and the summer journey to Syria; no one touches them with harm. And how would anyone dare against them or interfere with their trade, when they are the life of the House?

So the meaning of ﴿for the accustomed security of the Quraysh﴾ (106:1) is: Allah destroyed Abraha and his soldiers and did not enable them over the House, so that the Quraysh would remain, and so that Allah would perpetuate for them harmony and that they be loved by all people, and continue their secure trade journeys.

Therefore He says after it: ﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House, who fed them after hunger and secured them from fear﴾ (106:3-4) (Quraysh). It was obligatory upon them to worship the Lord of the House who bestowed these blessings upon them, for what they have of security, safety, food and drink is not by their own strength, but by their proximity to the House of Allah, and the House of Allah has sanctity among the Arabs, so none of them dares to attack the trade of the Quraysh.

Thus their saying to the Messenger of Allah: ﴿If we follow the guidance with you, we would be snatched away from our land...﴾ (28:57) is a proof of Allah against them, for at the time when people are snatched away from around them, they were in security, so it is a proof against them.

Moreover, the condition here, ﴿If we follow the guidance with you...﴾ (28:57), since you said about the religion that Muhammad brought that it is guidance, meaning guidance from Allah, it was obligatory upon you to believe in it if it became certain to you that it is guidance; otherwise you are liars in this saying. And why not, when you deny the Qur'an and call it fabrication, falsehood and sorcery, and now you call it guidance? This is a strange contradiction.

Did they not say: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man of the two towns?﴾ (43:31) (al-Zukhruf). The meaning of this is that the Qur'an has no flaw in it, but its calamity is that it was sent down upon this particular man.

As for His saying: ﴿Do they then believe in falsehood...﴾ (29:67) (al-'Ankabut), meaning: in idols, ﴿and disbelieve in the blessing of Allah?﴾ (29:67). He said ﴿the blessing of Allah...﴾ (29:67) and did not say, for example, "worship of Allah" or "disbelieve in faith in Allah," because if their belief had no cause other than the blessings of Allah upon them, that He fed them after hunger and secured them from fear, it would have been obligatory upon them to believe in Him.

Falsehood is the opposite of truth, and it is a vanishing that has no permanence; it quickly decays and ends. If you say: since falsehood vanishes and will end, what is the purpose of the struggle between truth and falsehood?

We say: were it not for the bite of falsehood upon society, people would not have longed for the truth to rescue them. Falsehood itself is one of the soldiers of truth, just as disbelief is one of the soldiers of faith. Were it not for disbelief and what disbelievers do to people, people would not have yearned for faith, which provides them security, tranquility, comfort and equality. Were it not for disbelief and what disbelievers do to people, people would not have yearned for faith.

Also, the meaning of "kufr" (disbelief) is to cover up (satr) the Necessarily Existent God, and covering requires something covered. So what is covered by disbelief? What is covered by disbelief is faith. Thus the word "kufr" itself is evidence of the existence of faith.

We have previously said: a person may dislike some things, while they are for his benefit and for a wisdom for which Allah created them. We illustrated this with pain, which a person complains of, while in reality it is an alert to him and a rousing so that he knows the cause of this pain and takes heed, repels the disease from himself, and seeks a remedy for it.

Pain in this sense is one of the soldiers of well-being; otherwise the most deadly diseases among humans are those without pain to alert to them, so they remain hidden in the body until their matter grows severe and their treatment becomes difficult. Therefore they describe it as "the malignant disease," because it creeps in the body without any sign appearing to indicate it.

So the Truthful, exalted is He, created pain for a wisdom: to alert you that at the place of pain there is a defect, and that the organ that hurts is not fit to perform its task. Therefore they say in defining well-being: "Well-being is that you do not feel your limbs. You have teeth you eat with, but you do not notice them, and perhaps you do not remember this blessing except when some defect afflicts them and pains you."

So: when you feel your organ and it aches, know that it is not normal, and that it is not performing its task as it should, so you must hasten to treat it.

Also, when falsehood flourishes and has a surge, that is only so that you feel the sweetness of truth, so that you long for it and desire it. Therefore Islam spread in lands where there was an Islamic majority, not by the sword as some like to say, but it spread through people seeing its principles and its tolerance.

In the lands of Persia and Byzantium, the people there suffered much hardship from their religions and their laws; when they heard about Islam, its principles and the tolerance of its teachings, they turned to it.

Were it not for falsehood's bite upon them, they would not have resorted to faith. Islam spread tremendously within half a century, and this was not the result of a surge of faith driving people into Islam, but rather the pull of misguidance toward faith. So it is as if Islam is propelled by two things: its people, who are eager for its spread, and a falsehood that drives people toward it.

The Truthful, glorified and exalted, gives us an example of truth and falsehood in His saying:
﴿He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their measure, and the torrent carries a swelling foam. And from what they heat in the fire seeking ornament or goods there is similar foam. Thus Allah strikes the truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum; but as for what benefits people, it remains upon the earth. Thus Allah sets forth examples﴾ (13:17) (al-Ra'd).

Foam (zabad) is the chaff and debris carried by the water, forming a layer on the surface of the water; then the air pushes it to the sides, and the water remains clear afterward. So foam is a figure for falsehood, because it rises above the surface of the water, but beware lest you think it has any importance, or that its height will last, for it is worthless residue, and it soon disappears, leaving the beneficial water. Just as foam forms on the surface of water, so it forms when metals are smelted: when a goldsmith, for example, smelts gold or silver, the pure metal comes out, leaving on the surface the dross that was mixed with it.

Therefore some of the knowers say: Allah, exalted is He, never abandons the truth or hands it over to falsehood forever; rather He leaves it for a time to test people's jealousy for it. If people do not become jealous for the truth, He, glorified is He, becomes jealous for it.

(1) Al-'asf al-ma'kul: the straw or leaves of a tree that has been struck by the disease "al-akkal," so parts of it have been eaten away. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/23).

Then the Exalted says:

﴿And who is more wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah, or denies the truth when it has come to him? Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the disbelievers?﴾ (68)

This is an interrogative form (istifham, a question used to make a point). Al-Haqq (the Truth), glorified and exalted is He, wants to establish a matter that the listener will affirm. So He did not phrase it as a declarative statement ("No one is more wrong"), because a declarative statement in itself may be true or false. Instead He used the interrogative form so that you would speak the matter yourself. It is like saying to someone who denies your favour: "Who gave you this garment?" He cannot do otherwise than acknowledge your kindness. But if you say to him as a statement, "I gave you this garment," the statement may be true or false, and he may deny it and say, "No, you did not give me anything."

So, presenting speech in the interrogative form is stronger in establishing a fact than the declarative form, because a declaration comes from the speaker, whereas the acknowledgement comes from the listener. You only pose a question while you are confident that the answer will come in line with what you want.

The meaning of "And who is more wrong..." (al-'Ankabut, 68) is: no one is more wrong. Wrongdoing (zulm) is taking a right away from its rightful owner and giving it to another. Wrongdoing may be great and immense, such as wrongdoing at the peak of belief, as He said: ﴿Indeed, associating others with Allah is a great wrong﴾ (Luqman, 13).

Wrongdoing may also be small and minor. The one who invents a lie against Allah is the most wrong, because if he had invented a lie against someone like himself, the matter would be minor. But whom has he invented it against? Against Allah. So his wrongdoing is immense. It is foolish to invent lies against Allah, because He, glorified is He, is stronger than you. He can expose and prove your lie, can repel you, and can stop you at your limit. Whoever dares this kind of wrongdoing has only wronged himself.

We have said that invention (iftira') is a lie, but it is deliberate. A person may lie while reporting according to what he knows, while reality is contrary to what he knows. For this reason, the scholars defined truthfulness and falsehood, saying: truthfulness is that speech corresponds to reality, and falsehood is that speech contradicts reality. So if I state a report according to what I know, and I do not intend to contradict reality, but my speech contradicts reality, then the report is false, but the reporter is not a liar.

As for His saying: ﴿or denies the truth when it has come to him...﴾ (al-'Ankabut, 68), it is as if he has gone beyond inventing a lie from the start. Rather, his lying has risen to another stage, and he deliberately denies a matter that is true and right. Then He establishes the punishment for this denial, also in the interrogative form: ﴿Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the disbelievers?﴾ (68). That is, has the Fire become too narrow for them, so that there is no place in it for these people? No, there are places in it for them. The evidence is that it will say, as it longs for them when it is asked: ﴿Is it filled? And it will say: Is there any more?﴾ (Qaf, 30).

It is as if the Exalted were saying: Why do these people invent lies against Allah? And why do they deny the truth? Know that Hell has no places for them? The interrogation in ﴿Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the disbelievers?﴾ is a rejecting interrogation (istifham inkari), which denies that the deniers and disbelievers could think that there is no place for them in Hell.

Al-Haqq, glorified is He, in His eternal will, willed to create creation from Adam, peace be upon him, until the Hour is established, and to give them choice: ﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ (al-Kahf, 29). He decreed that they would all believe, so He prepared their places in Paradise, and He decreed that they would all disbelieve, so He prepared their places in the Fire.

On the Day of Resurrection, the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire. Allah will make the believers inherit the places of the disbelievers in Paradise, and they will divide them among themselves. Likewise, the people of the Fire will divide among themselves the places of the believers in the Fire, through exchange (radd). So whoever had one place in the Fire will have two places.

Moreover, the interrogation ﴿Is there not in Hell a dwelling for the disbelievers?﴾ (68) makes the listener share in the speech, and it carries the sense of rebuke and reproach, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they would exchange winks. And when they returned to their people, they returned jesting. And when they saw them, they said: Indeed, these are misguided. But they were not sent as guardians over them. So today, those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, upon couches, looking on. Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾ (al-Mutaffifin, 29–36).

Allah turns to the believers who were mocked in this world: "Have We decreed that We would repay these disbelievers, and return your rights to you?" This is both a consolation to the believers and a rebuke to the disbelievers. They will say: "Yes, our Lord, yes, our Lord, yes, our Lord." So the Exalted wants to incite the believers against them, so that they will not soften toward them or show them compassion, because they transgressed and became arrogant, their proofs and evidences were presented to them, yet they denied them and persisted in their obstinacy, so they went to extremes in wrongdoing.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 29, verse 69:

We say: *jahada fulan yajhadu*, meaning he exhausted himself. *Ijtahada* means he insisted on exertion. *Jahada ghayrahu* means he strove against another. So *jahada* indicates *mufa'alah* (the form expressing reciprocity and participation), which cannot be completed except between two parties. In this form (*mufa'alah*) we give the sense of agency to one of them and the sense of being acted upon to the other, even though they are partners in the action. Each of them is an agent at one time and the object of the action at another time, as if you say: "Zayd shared with 'Amr, and 'Amr shared with Zayd." Or: the one who has the stronger side in the partnership is the agent and the other is the object.

After Allah, glorified is He, explained that the abode of the disbelieving deniers is in Hell, and that the believers are gathered against them, and since they have committed this great wrong, there must be a disciplining of them. This discipline is not to compel them to faith: ﴿So whoever wills, let him believe; and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ (Al-Kahf, 29). Rather, the discipline is that we proclaim our call openly and raise high the word of truth. So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him remain in his state. Therefore, the verse clarifies the stance of the believers before these deniers: ﴿And those who strive for Us—We will surely guide them to Our ways﴾ (29:69).

The meaning of *jahadu fina* ("strove for Us") is: for our sake and to support our religion. The disputes in which we strive for Allah are many. There is a dispute over the foundation of faith and the existence of the One God, such as the atheists who say that there is no god in the universe. These have one kind of struggle. And the people of polytheism, who acknowledge the existence of Allah but claim that He has a partner, have another kind of struggle.

So the struggle against the atheists is with logic and argument, so that they themselves affirm the existence of one God. We say to them: Has anyone ever claimed that he created himself or created another? Rather, reflect on the most trivial things you use in your lives. This glass cup, which is a luxury and not one of life's necessities: do you say that it came into being like this, without a maker? Then how did it come into being? Do we have, for example, a tree that produces these cups for us?

So it is a craft that has a craftsman, who used the intellect that Allah gave him, applied it to the materials that Allah placed in the universe, and derived from them this substance (glass).

The electric lamp that Edison invented: how much effort, research and study did it take, and then its manufacture requires factories, engineers and maintenance. Yet a small pebble breaks it and it goes out. Edison gained much fame, and we immortalized his memory, and humanity still remembers his favour.

Do they not look at the sun, which lights up the whole world since Allah created it until the Hour is established, without needing maintenance or spare parts? Can anyone take it to repair it? Has the sun ever refused to rise on any day, and does it still supply you with heat, rays, warmth and light?

Do you know who made the lamp, but you do not know who made the sun? You have thought about the most trivial things and known who made them, and you have dated them and immortalized their memory. Would it not have been more fitting for you to reflect on the greatness of Allah's creation and to believe in Him?

Then tell me, O atheist: when the darkness of night covers you, how do you light it? They say: every person lights his night's darkness according to his ability. At night you see different lights: this one sits by the light of a candle, another by the light of a kerosene lamp, another by the light of an electric bulb, and another by the light of a neon bulb. So the lights at night vary, indicating the capabilities of their owners. But when the sun rises and the divine lamp shines, all these lights are extinguished and have no effect in the presence of the lamp of the Greatest Creator, glorified is He.

Is this not an indication that a judgment has come to us from Allah, and that we should set aside all our judgments so that we may be illuminated by the judgment of Allah? Is the truthfulness of the perceptible not evidence of the truthfulness of the abstract?

And you, who claim that Allah has a partner in His dominion: who said that Allah has a partner? You yourself said it from your own mind. For when Allah, the Exalted, said: "I am the One God, with no partner for Me," no one contested it, and no one claimed to be a partner of Allah.

This is evidence that the partner does not exist, or that he exists but is unaware, or that he is aware but was unable to confront. In both cases, he is not fit to be a god.

Then, supposing he exists, what is his method? What did he command you and what did he forbid you? What has he prepared for you of bliss if you worship him? And what has he prepared for him of punishment if you disbelieve in him? So this alleged god is a god without a method, and his worship is void.

As for those who believe in a heavenly religion but do not believe in the Messenger (ﷺ), we say to them: It is enough of the aspects of greatness in the personality of Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah that he is not partisan for himself, because his heart is with everyone who believes in Allah, even if he disbelieves in him. Muhammad loves everyone who believes in his Lord, even if he disbelieves in Muhammad. He is zealous for his Lord even regarding one who denied him.

Then you, followers of the Jewish or Christian religions, who lived at the time of Islam's emergence and denied it, even though your religion came after a religion, and your messenger came after a previous messenger: why, when Muhammad came to you, did you deny him and disbelieve in him? Why did you permit that Jesus come after Moses, peace be upon them both, yet deny that Muhammad come after Jesus?

So for every dispute concerning the religion of Allah there is a special debate and a method of discussion that you undertake in light of: ﴿And those who strive for Us—We will surely guide them to Our ways﴾ (29:69). And you must first consider the position of the struggle you are undertaking. The struggle against atheists has one method, the struggle against polytheists has another, the struggle against the People of the Book has another, and the struggle of a Muslim against a Muslim also has a method, if disagreement arises between them, even though Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects, you are not [associated] with them in anything﴾ (Al-An'am, 159).

So whenever you see each of them at an extreme, such that you cannot follow either of them, know that they are both upon falsehood. For Islam is one thing, which we previously likened to pure white water that has not been mixed with any colour, smell or taste. If desires colour it and people divide into factions over it, just as they colour juices, then they have strayed from the right path and erred from the true religion.

For what came in it as a clear judgment from Allah, we agree upon. What Allah left to our ijtihad (independent reasoning) should be such that each of us respects the ijtihad of the other, and says: My opinion is correct but may be mistaken, and the opinion of others is mistaken but may be correct. By this reasoning, opinions coexist.

Allah, the Exalted, gives us the example for this. What He willed in the method as a definitive ruling comes as a definitive ruling in one statement, about which there is no disagreement. We have cited as an example the verse of ablution: ﴿O you who believe, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows...﴾ (Al-Ma'idah, 6).

He did not specify the face, because there is no disagreement among people about its specification. Rather, He specified the hands, because they are a place of disagreement. So the issues that arise among Muslims should have a special debate within this framework, without partisanship. What comes to you as a definitive ruling with no room for opinion is one that everyone must adhere to. What is left without explicit text and does not admit of disagreement, then let each one go to what the text admits.

For example, in our language the particle *bi* (ب) comes to indicate partitiveness, or instrumentality, or attachment. If you take it in one meaning, do not restrict others from taking it in another meaning.

If fighting breaks out between two groups of Muslims, there must be a moderate group that undertakes the task of reconciliation, as He, glorified is He, said:

﴿And if two groups of believers fight, make peace between them. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the command of Allah. And if it returns, then make peace between them with justice and act justly. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly﴾ (Al-Hujurat, 9).

We observe that Allah, the Exalted, called them believers. This means that faith does not prevent us from disagreeing. And this faith that does not prevent disagreement is what obliges us to have among us a moderate group that is neutral, not leaning here or there, performing the role of reconciliation and the role of deterring the aggressor who transgresses, until he returns to the right path and to the command of Allah.

If they return, we do not leave matters to be overshadowed by the shade of victory for one party and defeat for another. Rather, we reconcile between them and remove the rancour and enmity in their souls. The strong has given up his arrogance when we restrained his hand, and the weak has been strengthened by our standing at his side. So a kind of balance is achieved and the two scales are equalized. Let everyone return to the enclosure of security and peace.

There remains for us to speak of another struggle, which is more important: the struggle of the human soul. For the Prophet (ﷺ), when he returned from one of the military campaigns, said: "We have returned from the lesser jihad to the greater jihad." So he described the struggle against the soul as the greater jihad. Why? Because in the battlefield you struggle against an apparent enemy whose number and methods are clear to you. But if your enemy is from your own self and from within you, then its struggle is difficult for you. For you love to fulfil your desires for yourself, and to obey its inclinations and impulses, while it, in all of this, penetrates you and slips through you.

So you must stand in the struggle against the soul in a position in which you compare the immediate desires of the soul with the lasting regret it inherits for you, and with the reward of your Lord in a Paradise containing bliss that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and that has not occurred to the heart of any human being.

Place your Lord and your soul in this comparison and consider carefully. Know that your Lord has precedents with you, precedents of goodness that He prepared for you before you existed. He who prepared for you this whole universe and made it serve you is surely trustworthy regarding you. You are after Him and His craft. Have you ever seen a craftsman who sets out to his craft and then destroys it?

If you see, for example, a carpenter holding the chisel (*al-fara*) and carving into a piece of wood, know that he is preparing it to perform its task. Remember the story of the child Ayman, who came to his mother crying because the servant was beating the carpet. His mother took him and showed him the dust that falls from the carpet with each blow of the servant, and the child understood according to his level of understanding.

So too, Allah, the Exalted, when He tests His creatures, He tests them not out of malice towards them, but for their reform. Have we not often heard a mother say to her only child: "May I drink your fire" (*ilahi ashrab narak*)? By Allah, what would her state be if Allah answered her? Yet in reality she does not hate her only child and the fruit of her heart. Rather, she hates in him the trait that angered her.

So too, Allah, the Exalted, does not hate His servant. Rather, He hates in him the bad qualities, so He wishes to purify him of them through trial, until he returns pure as on the day his mother bore him. So, O human being, think well of your Lord.

So we say: among the greatest of struggles is your struggle against your own self, because it penetrates you so that you satisfy its desires, and because it is exposed to the enticement of passion and the whispering of Satan, who adorns for it every evil and makes every wrong appealing to it.

We have already explained how to distinguish between the adornment of Satan and the adornment of the self, because the self has a role in disobedience, as evidenced by the statement of the Prophet (ﷺ): "When Ramadan comes, the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of Hell are closed, and the devils are chained."

If all sins were due to Satan, we would not find anyone sinning in Ramadan. But there are many sins committed in Ramadan, which means they come from the adornment of the self. It is as if Allah, the Exalted, wanted to reveal to the son of Adam: "Behold, I have chained the devils, and yet you sin."

If you want to know whether a sin comes from the self or from Satan: the self keeps you at one specific sin and does not want any other, nor does it move you to another. It keeps pressing you until it makes you fall into it. But Satan wants you to be disobedient in whatever form and in whatever state. If you refuse him, he moves you to another sin.

The intelligent person should reflect: sin gives you a fleeting pleasure and a transient enjoyment, which is entirely unworthy of this human being whom Allah honoured, made His successor on earth, and master of this universe. The whole universe, with its earth and sky, serves him. Is it conceivable that the servant should live longer than the one he serves?

You will die after a year or after a hundred years, while the sun that serves you lasts for millions of years. So you must have another life that is more enduring and lasting than the life of your servant. If you are now in a life described as "this world" (*dunya*), this means that it is contrasted with another life described as "the higher" (*'ulya*), which is your life in the Hereafter, where there is no death at all.

And the Noble Qur'an, when it limits...

1. Abu Sulayman al-Darani said: The struggle in the verse is not only fighting the disbelievers. Rather, it is the victory of religion, the refutation of the falsifiers, the suppression of oppressors. Among its greatest forms is enjoining good and forbidding evil, and among it is striving against the souls in obedience to Allah, and this is the greater jihad. (Quoted by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir, 7/5255.)
